metadata.systemPrompt: The official ADOIT 21.0 documentation: the User Manual, the Administration Help and the Quick Start Guide. It covers how to use, configure and administer ADOIT.

documents.title: The ADOIT 21.0 User Manual
documents.summary: ADOIT by BOC Group is an IT service and management tool supporting ITIL, COBIT, TOGAF, and RiskIT standards, usable out-of-the-box or customizable to individual needs.
documents.content:
Welcome to the ADOIT Help. ADOIT is the IT service and management tool of the BOC Group.

ADOIT provides rich functionality for all typical IT management tasks. It is geared to international standards such as ITIL, COBIT, TOGAF and RiskIT, and the considerable experience and expertise of the BOC group gained from a variety of IT management projects.

Use ADOIT either out-of-the-box (ADOIT standard configuration) or expand it to fit your individual needs (ADOIT customising - "tailoring").

children.title: About this Manual
children.summary: This manual provides instructions on ADOIT's functions including Scenarios, Modelling, Analysis, Collaboration, Validation, and Accessibility features.
children.content:
In the following documentation you find instructions on how to use the manifold functions of ADOIT:
• ADOIT Scenarios: This part of the manual contains information about the scenarios in ADOIT that accommodate different stakeholders' needs.
• Modelling: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for the gathering of your enterprise architecture information.
• Analysis: This part of the manual contains information about the analysis functions in ADOIT.
• Collaboration and Sharing: This part of the manual provides an overview of the most important functions for collaboration and sharing content.
• Validation and Release: This part of the manual provides an overview of the validation functions and the release workflows in ADOIT.
• Accessibility, Videos and More: This part of the manual provides an overview of the help functions in ADOIT and functions for manipulating ADOIT itself.

children.title: Learn More
children.summary: Additional resources include the ADOIT Marketplace and BOC Group's EA Resources.
children.content:
For additional information, take a look at:
• ADOIT Marketplace
• BOC Group - EA Resources

children.title: Other Manuals
children.summary: For ADOIT administration questions, refer to the Administration Help manual.
children.content: For questions about administering ADOIT, please refer to the Administration Help.

children.title: ADOIT Scenarios
children.summary: ADOIT offers four scenarios—Design & Document, Workspaces, Control & Release, and Read & Explore—each catering to different stakeholder needs with scenario switching via a dropdown menu; availability depends on license and application library.
children.content:
ADOIT is organised into a number of so-called scenarios that accommodate different stakeholders' needs:
• "Design & Document"
• "Workspaces"
• "Control & Release"
• "Read & Explore"

Each user has access to one or more scenarios and can switch between them as needed.

Scenario Selection

When you log in to ADOIT for the first time, a scenario will be automatically selected (in order of the list above, if you have access to multiple scenarios).

For subsequent visits, ADOIT will always log you in to the scenario last used.

As you work, you can select the desired scenario from the dropdown menu at the top left corner of the program window.

note

You can also use this dropdown menu to switch to the Organisation Portal, if it is available.

Widgets

The individual functions of the scenarios are grouped in the form of widgets (= small program windows). When you click the icon , ADOIT provides a tooltip with information about the widget.

Further Information

For further information, see these topics:
• Design & Document: The purpose of the "Design & Document" scenario is to let users design services and architectures and to plan initiatives.
• Workspaces: Workspaces in ADOIT serve as collaboration hubs for enterprise architecture. They bundle together multiple functionalities to provide a guided approach to solving specific business needs and to empower the user to perform all relevant tasks and make decisions with a clear focus.
• Control & Release: The purpose of the "Control & Release" scenario is to let users review and release objects with a single click.
• Read & Explore: The purpose of the "Read & Explore" scenario is to let users get a quick overview of architecture artefacts in ADOIT.

note

Available scenarios vary depending on the application library and the licence.

children.title: Available Functions
children.summary: Common functions across Design & Document, Control & Release, and Read & Explore scenarios include various interactive and reporting features.
children.content:
Across all widgets and subordinated dashboards of the application scenarios
• "Design & Document"
• "Control & Release"
• "Read & Explore"

the following functions are available:

children.title: Open/Edit Elements
children.summary: Users can open/edit elements, confirm data actuality, access Insights dashboards, and toggle element visibility within charts, with data actuality status configurable per installation.
children.content:
• Open a model in the graphical editor by clicking the hyperlinked name.
• Open the properties of an object by clicking the hyperlinked name.
• Show or hide an element in a chart by clicking its name.
• Confirm the data actuality of an object via the icon .
• Open an Insights dashboard by clicking the icon .
• Hover over a list item to reveal icons for editing that item (e.g. to open an Insights dashboard).

note

The time period after which an object is marked as 'yellow' or 'red' if its data actuality was not confirmed by the responsible depends on the configuration of your ADOIT installation.

children.title: Create Reports
children.summary: Reports such as demands list, interface, and standard reports can be created via specific icons.
children.content:
• Create a demands list report via the icon .
• Create an interface report via the icon .
• Create a standard report via the icon .

children.title: General Tools
children.summary: Widgets support exporting content as PDF or Excel, refreshing data, and opening Management Dashboards for detailed model information.
children.content:
• Export the content of a widget as a PDF file or Excel file (XLSX format) via the icon .
• Refresh a widget via the icon .
• Open a "Management Dashboard" which contains detailed information regarding your models via the icon .

children.title: Interactive Pie Charts
children.summary: Interactive pie charts allow selection of items by clicking segments and opening detailed lists by double-clicking.
children.content:
• Select the corresponding items in the appropriate list by clicking a segment.
• Open a separate page which lists the corresponding items by double-clicking a segment.

children.title: Filter Objects by Responsibility (All/My)
children.summary: Widgets can filter objects by responsibility, showing either all relevant objects or only those assigned to the user as responsible, accountable, consulted, or informed.
children.content:
In some widgets, you can switch between displaying all or my relevant objects. Depending on the widget, the displayed objects may include Application Components, System software etc.).

In order to filter objects by responsibility:
1. Click the widget title (button ) to open a drop-down menu (1).
2. Select either the menu entry All or My (2).

All lists all relevant objects in the database.

My lists all relevant objects:
• For which you are assigned as responsible, accountable, consulted or informed business actor (properties in the chapter "Organisation").

children.title: The "Design & Document" Scenario
children.summary: The Design & Document scenario enables designing services and architectures, planning initiatives, and provides a start page with banners, recent items, favourites, and personal objects, plus toolbar access to creating, searching, dashboards, analyses, reports, AI Assistant, and Forms.
children.content:
The purpose of the "Design & Document" scenario is to let you design your services and architectures and to plan your initiatives.

What you will see on the "Design & Document" start page

The start page has the following appearance:
• Banner: The perfect place for an image that represents your organisation. Can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.
• Recently opened: Your most recently opened models and objects. Sorted by date. To see additional artefacts, click Show more....
• Favourites: Your favourite models and objects. Sorted alphabetically. To see additional artefacts, click Show more....
• My Objects: A compact list of all repository objects for which you are responsible. Grouped by type and sorted alphabetically. To see additional objects, click Show more.... For a more detailed dashboard of your objects, go to Analyse > Dashboards > My Objects.

View your most recently opened models and objects as well as your favourites as thumbnails or a list. You can easily switch between the two layouts using the Show list and Show tiles icons.

note

If custom images have been uploaded for specific ArchiMate elements, they will appear as thumbnails, replacing the standard icons for those elements.

Additional Options

The toolbar at the top of the screen provides access to some of the most used features in ADOIT:
• New : Create new models and objects.
• Find : Open the Explorer and the search function in ADOIT. Multiple search and filtering options help you quickly find the artefact you are looking for.
• Dashboards : Open and configure configurable dashboards.
• Analyse : This page has two sections: Analyses and Reports. Use the quick links at the top of the page to access these sections. The Analyses section serves as a starting point to run analyses on a data set of your choice. The Reports section shows the Reporting Board, where PDF and RTF reports can be created.

Information for upgrading users

The built-in legacy dashboards My Objects, Strategy, Business, Application and Technology have been removed in ADOIT 21.0. You can recreate most of these views using configurable dashboards.

If your licence allows it, you can access additional features in the bottom right corner:
• AI Assistant: Use the AI Assistant to interact with ADOIT. You can ask questions in natural language, search and retrieve repository information, and discuss enterprise architecture and ArchiMate concepts.
• Forms: ADOIT Forms enables you to design, manage and complete forms for ADOIT with an easy to use graphical user interface. For details, please refer to the ADOIT Forms user manual.

children.title: Workspaces
children.summary: Workspaces are collaborative hubs based on templates like Application Cost Management and Roadmaps, bundling functionalities to address specific business needs.
children.content:
Workspaces in ADOIT serve as collaboration hubs for enterprise architecture. They bundle together multiple functionalities to provide a guided approach to solving specific business needs and to empower the user to perform all relevant tasks and make decisions with a clear focus.

Templates

A workspace is created based on a template. In ADOIT 21.0, the following templates are available:
• Application Cost Management
• Application Compliance Assessment
• Application Investment Planning
• Capability Investment Planning
• Application-based Roadmap
• Capability-based Roadmap
• Goal-based Roadmap

children.title: The Workspaces Page
children.summary: The Workspaces page lists all created workspaces as tiles and allows opening or creating new workspaces via templates.
children.content:
The Workspaces page shows all workspaces that have been created. If no workspaces are available yet, the templates for creating new workspaces are displayed instead.

Open Workspaces Page

To open the Workspaces page:
• Select Workspaces from the dropdown menu at the top left corner of the program window.

Create New Workspace

See Create Workspace.

Open a Workspace

All workspaces are shown as tiles, sorted alphabetically.
• To open a workspace, click it.

children.title: Create Workspace
children.summary: Creating a workspace involves selecting a template, naming, adding users with permissions, choosing element types, configuring lifecycle or dates depending on template, and sending invitation emails; workspaces can be private or public with member and admin roles.
children.content:
You can create new workspaces on the Workspaces page:
1. Click New workspace and choose a template:
• To learn more about a template, select Open preview.
• Once you've made your decision, select Use template or click anywhere on the tile to proceed.

note

If no workspaces have been created yet, you can pick a template directly on the Workspaces page.
2. A setup wizard guides you through several steps. After completing each step, select Next to continue.

Step 1: Add a name and users
• Workspace name: Enter the name of the new workspace.
• Description: Optionally, enter a description of the new workspace.
• Add users: Select the users you want to collaborate with. Start typing the username or email address of a user, and then select the one you want when you see it.
• Usernames will only appear if the user has previously been shared with the active repository in the ADOIT Administration.
• If you enter an email address that is not associated with any user, you need to enter the full email address.
• Choose which permissions users should have for the new workspace. Users can either be members or admins.
• Private workspace: Choose whether the workspace should be private (= only visible for members and admins).

Step 2: Choose element types
• Select the element types to consider in your workspace. The available options depend on the selected template. For example, for Application-based Roadmaps, you can select application elements such as Application Components or Application Services.
3. Depending on the selected template, the setup wizard may include additional steps:

Step 3: Configure lifecycle [ Application Cost Management ]
• The setup for Application Cost Management includes one additional step.
• Optionally, enable Apply lifecycle dates to check contracts based on their validity period. If enabled, select the Valid year for which contract validity should be considered.

Step 3: Configure dates [ Investment Planning Workspaces ]
• The setup for Application Investment Planning and Capability Investment Planning includes includes one additional step.
• Workspace valid until: Optionally, define the intended lifetime of the workspace. After this date, you should create a new workspace to start the next assessment cycle.
• Survey period: Optionally, define the recommended period for collecting assessments by specifying when the survey opens and closes.

Step 3: Choose prioritisation method & Step 4: Choose time periods [ Roadmapping Workspaces ]
• The setup for Application-based Roadmaps, Capability-based Roadmaps, and Goal-based Roadmaps includes two additional steps.
• Choose a prioritisation method for assessing your requirements. You can select either the Value vs. Effort Method or the Eisenhower Matrix.
• Choose the time periods in which your roadmap should be planned and displayed. You can select months, quarters, or years.
4. Click Create workspace.

The first page of the workspace appears, and you can start working on the content right away.

User Types Explained
• Any person invited to join a workspace starts out as a member. Members have access to all content within a workspace. They can capture and assess architecture artefacts if they have sufficient user rights.
• The person who created the workspace starts out as an admin. Admins can do everything a member can do. Additionally, they can add or remove users from a workspace, make workspaces private or public, and rename or delete workspaces.

Who Can View and Edit Workspaces?

If a workspace is set to private, only users explicitly designated as members or admins can view and edit it.

If a workspace is not set to private, all users with write access to the "Objects" group—the main object group in the Object Catalogue—are treated as members, meaning they can capture and assess architecture artefacts within the workspace. Users with read access to the "Objects" group, however, can only view and edit workspaces where they are explicitly designated as members or admins.

Invitation Emails and Access to the Workspace

After the workspace is created, ADOIT sends invitation emails to all users you have invited to collaborate (provided they have an associated email address) as well as to any other email addresses you have specified that are not linked to a user account.

These invitation emails contain a link to the workspace. A login to ADOIT is required to access the link. If the recipient of the invitation does not yet have a ADOIT user account, one must be created.

note

Before ADOIT can send emails, the mail settings must be set correctly in the ADOIT Administration (see Email in the Administration Help).

children.title: Application Cost Management
children.summary: Application Cost Management workspace guides reviewing application landscape costs via scoping elements, assigning contracts, allocating costs, and reviewing summaries, focusing on Application Components and Services.
children.content:
The Application Cost Management template is a collaborative workspace for reviewing the costs of your application landscape based on the contracts that govern them. It guides you through scoping the relevant application elements, assigning and maintaining their contracts, allocating contract costs across application elements, and finally reviewing allocations and totals with charts and tables.

Which Elements Are Used?

Application Cost Management is enabled for Application Components and Application Services.

How Does Application Cost Management Work in ADOIT?

To begin, set up an Application Cost Management workspace (see Create Workspace).

Once you have created the workspace, follow these steps:
1. Scope – Select the application elements that define the scope of your cost review.
2. Assign Contracts – Link contracts to your application elements.
3. Cost Allocation – Allocate contract costs across application elements.
4. Summary – Review the results.

These steps are discussed in more detail in the following sections.

children.title: Scope
children.summary: The Scope page lets users select application elements to define the cost review scope.
children.content: The first page of the Application Cost Management template lets you select the application elements that define the scope of your cost review.

children.title: Select Application Elements for Cost Review
children.summary: Users add or remove application elements for cost review using search and bulk actions, filtering by element type if multiple are available.
children.content:
To define which application elements you want to include:
• In the left pane, all application elements that can be added to the workspace are displayed. Use the search box to quickly find a specific element.
• To add an element, click Add. To remove an element, click Remove. For bulk actions, use the Add all and Remove all links at the top of the page.
• If multiple element types are available in your workspace, the Element type list appears at the top left. Use it to control which elements are shown in the left pane. Depending on your workspace settings, you may choose Application Components and Application Services.

children.title: Filter by Workspace, Group, Investment Strategy or Lifecycle State
children.summary: Filters such as Workspaces, Groups, Investment Strategy (Gartner's TIME model), and Lifecycle State can be applied and combined to refine element selection.
children.content:
You can use filters to hone in on the specific elements you need:
• Click + Add Filter, and then choose the filter you want:
• Workspaces: Select elements that are already used or evaluated in another workspace.
• Groups: Select elements from specific object groups.
• Investment strategy: Select elements with confirmed investment strategies according to Gartner's TIME model (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, and Eliminate), as well as those with no confirmed investment strategy (indicated by "No entry").
• Lifecycle state: Select elements based on their lifecycle state (Draft, In development, In production, and Retired). You can also include elements without a confirmed lifecycle state (indicated by "No entry").

You can apply multiple conditions to each filter and combine different filters if required.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional options include opening Insights dashboards and renaming elements; after selection, users proceed to Assign Contracts.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Scope page:
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename an element that has been added to the workspace, hover over the element, and then click Edit .

After selecting your application elements, switch to the Assign Contracts tab to continue.

children.title: Assign Contracts
children.summary: Assign Contracts page lists application elements with linked contracts, showing investment strategy and lifecycle state.
children.content:
On the second page of the Application Cost Management template, you can link contracts to your application elements and capture key contract information such as expiry dates.

The application elements are listed along with their linked contracts. Application elements also display their current investment strategy and lifecycle state.

children.title: Link Contracts to Application Elements
children.summary: Contracts can be linked to application elements by searching or creating new contracts; assignments synchronize across workspaces reflecting repository relationships.
children.content:
To link contracts to an application element:
• Click Assign Contract below the element to search for an existing contract or create a new one.
• Start typing the name of a contract, and then select the one you want when you see it. If the contract does not yet exist, finish typing the name and press < Enter > to create it.
• To see more options, click Show more. This opens a support dialog with the following tabs:
• Assigned contracts: Displays all contracts already assigned to the element.
• All existing contracts: Lists all contracts in the repository. You can filter contracts, select the ones you want to assign, and click Add.

Contract Assignments Synchronized Across Workspaces

Contract assignments are automatically synchronized across workspaces. For workspaces using these application elements, relationships always reflect the relationships in the repository. For example, if you assign a contract to an application element in one workspace, the contract is also assigned to that application element when you use the same object in another workspace. Such assignments are also considered in other workspace steps and in all related calculations.

children.title: Capture Contract Details
children.summary: Contract details like description, valid from, and valid until dates can be captured and edited, with optional lifecycle date warnings if enabled.
children.content:
Expand a contract to view or edit additional information. The following fields are available:
• Description: A textual description of the contract.
• Valid from: Specifies the date from which the contract remains in effect.
• Valid until: Specifies the date until which the contract remains in effect.

All fields are optional and can be filled in at any time.

note

If you enabled Apply lifecycle dates when setting up the workspace, warnings are displayed next to the Valid from and Valid until fields if the contract does not match the configured Valid year. A contract satisfies this requirement if it either covers the entire Valid year or is completely contained within it.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Users can search, filter, remove, rename contracts, and open Insights dashboards; contract removal options include removing from one or all elements or deleting entirely.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Assign Contracts page:
• To find contracts or application elements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To filter contracts or application elements, click + Add Filter and choose the filter you want. You can filter application elements by investment strategy or lifecycle state, and contracts by application element.
• To remove a contract, hover over the contract, and then click Remove element . Choose whether to:
• Remove the contract only from the application element it has been added to.
• Remove it from all application elements in the workspace.
• Delete it entirely from all workspaces and the repository.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename a contract, hover over the contract, and then click Edit .

After linking contracts to your application elements, switch to the Cost Allocation tab to continue.

children.title: Cost Allocation
children.summary: Cost Allocation page allows distributing contract costs across linked application elements, showing total annual costs and allocations.
children.content:
The third page of the Application Cost Management template lets you allocate the costs of a contract across one or more application elements. This is useful when a single contract covers multiple applications or includes bundled cost items.

On this page, you will find a table listing all contracts in alphabetical order. For each contract, you can review the total annual cost, see which application elements it is linked to, and view how the annual cost is allocated across those applications.

children.title: Distribute Contract Costs
children.summary: Users enter annual contract costs and allocate percentages per application element, ensuring total allocation does not exceed 100%.
children.content:
To allocate the costs of a contract, two fields are available:
• Annual cost: Enter the expected cost of the contract for a 12-month period.
• Cost allocation %: For each application element supported by the contract, enter the percentage of the total annual cost allocated to it. The combined allocation for a contract cannot exceed 100%.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional options include searching elements and opening Insights dashboards; after allocation, users proceed to Summary.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Cost Allocation page:
• To find elements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .

After finishing the cost allocation, switch to the Summary tab to continue.

children.title: Summary
children.summary: Summary page displays total applications and contracts, detailed tables or bar charts of costs by investment strategy, and suggests next steps like creating workspaces or training.
children.content:
The last page of the Application Cost Management template offers a summary of all application elements in the workspace, their assigned contracts, and the resulting cost allocations. This page has the following areas:
• Applications in total: Shows the total number of application elements in the workspace.
• Contracts in total: Shows the total number of contracts considered in the workspace.
• Table/bar chart summary: You can switch between a table view and a bar chart using the Table view and Chart view icons. The table view provides a detailed overview of all application elements in the workspace, including their investment strategy, assigned contracts, total annual contract costs, and allocated costs per contract. The bar chart breaks down annual contract costs for application elements by investment strategy (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, and Eliminate, according to the TIME model). TIME classifications are based on the assessments described in TIME Definition.
• What's next?: Check out possible next steps here. How about creating another workspace, or taking part in a free online training for ADOIT?

children.title: Application Compliance Assessment
children.summary: Application Compliance Assessment workspace supports assessing application components against principles or constraints through scoping, assigning criteria, assessing fulfillment, and reviewing aggregated results.
children.content:
The Application Compliance Assessment template is a collaborative workspace for assessing and reviewing the compliance of your application landscape against defined principles and constraints. It guides you through selecting the relevant application components, assigning compliance criteria, assessing their fulfillment per application component, and finally reviewing aggregated compliance results using tables and key performance indicators.

Which Elements Are Used?

Application Compliance Assessment workspaces start from a set of Application Components. Based on these elements, you assign Principles or Constraints.

How Does Application Compliance Assessment Work in ADOIT?

To begin, set up an Application Compliance Assessment workspace (see Create Workspace).

Once you have created the workspace, follow these steps:
1. Scope – Select the application components that are in scope for the compliance assessment.
2. Compliance Criteria – Assign principles or constraints to the selected application components.
3. Assessment – Assess the fulfillment of the assigned compliance criteria per application component.
4. Summary – Review aggregated compliance results per application component or compliance criterion.

These steps are discussed in more detail in the following sections.

children.title: Scope
children.summary: Scope page defines which application components are included in the compliance assessment.
children.content: The first page of the Application Compliance Assessment template lets you define which application components are included in the compliance assessment.

children.title: Select Application Components for Compliance Assessment
children.summary: Users add or remove application components for assessment using search and bulk actions.
children.content:
To define which application components you want to include:
• In the left pane, all application components that can be added to the workspace are displayed. Use the search box to quickly find a specific element.
• To add an element, click Add. To remove an element, click Remove. For bulk actions, use the Add all and Remove all links at the top of the page.

children.title: Filter by Workspace, Group, Investment Strategy or Lifecycle State
children.summary: Filters for Workspaces, Groups, Investment Strategy (TIME model), and Lifecycle State can be applied and combined to narrow component selection.
children.content:
You can use filters to narrow down the list of application components:
• Click + Add Filter, and then choose the filter you want:
• Workspaces: Select elements that are already used or evaluated in another workspace.
• Groups: Select elements from specific object groups.
• Investment strategy: Select elements with confirmed investment strategies according to Gartner's TIME model (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, and Eliminate), as well as those with no confirmed investment strategy (indicated by "No entry").
• Lifecycle state: Select elements based on their lifecycle state (Draft, In development, In production, and Retired). You can also include elements without a confirmed lifecycle state (indicated by "No entry").

You can apply multiple conditions to each filter and combine different filters if required.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional options include opening Insights dashboards and renaming components; after selection, users proceed to Compliance Criteria.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Scope page:
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename an element that has been added to the workspace, hover over the element, and then click Edit .

After selecting your application components, switch to the Compliance Criteria tab to continue.

children.title: Compliance Criteria
children.summary: Compliance Criteria page allows assigning principles or constraints to selected application components, displaying their investment strategy and lifecycle state.
children.content:
On the second page of the Application Compliance Assessment template, you can assign compliance criteria (principles or constraints) to the application components that were selected in the previous step.

In addition to the assigned criteria, the current investment strategy and lifecycle state of each application component are displayed.

children.title: Assign Compliance Criteria to Application Components
children.summary: Criteria are assigned by searching or creating new principles or constraints; assignments synchronize across workspaces reflecting repository relationships.
children.content:
To assign criteria to an application component:
• Depending on your workspace setup, you will find the Assign Constraint or Assign Principle button below the element. Clicking it allows you to search for an existing criterion or create a new one.
• Start typing the name of a criterion, and then select the one you want when you see it. If the criterion does not yet exist, finish typing the name and press < Enter > to create it.
• To see more options, click Show more. This opens a support dialog with the following tabs:
• Assigned compliance criteria: Displays all criteria already assigned to the element.
• All existing compliance criteria: Lists all criteria in the repository. You can filter criteria, select the ones you want to assign, and click Add.

Criteria Assignments Synchronized Across Workspaces

Compliance criteria assignments are automatically synchronized across workspaces. For workspaces using these application elements, relationships always reflect the relationships in the repository. For example, if you assign a compliance criterion to an application element in one workspace, the criterion is also assigned to that application element when you use the same object in another workspace. Such assignments are also considered in other workspace steps and in all related calculations.

children.title: View and Edit Compliance Criteria Details
children.summary: Compliance criteria details such as descriptions can be viewed or edited at any time.
children.content:
Expand a criterion to view or edit additional information:
• Description: A textual description of the criterion.

This field is optional and can be filled in at any time.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Users can search, filter, remove, rename criteria, and open Insights dashboards; removal options include removing from one or all components or deleting entirely.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Compliance Criteria page:
• To find criteria or application components, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To filter criteria or application components, click + Add Filter and choose the filter you want. You can filter application components by investment strategy or lifecycle state, and criteria by application component.
• To remove a criterion, hover over the criterion, and then click Remove element . Choose whether to:
• Remove the criterion only from the application component it has been added to.
• Remove it from all application components in the workspace.
• Delete it entirely from all workspaces and the repository.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename a criterion, hover over the criterion, and then click Edit .

After assigning criteria to your application components, switch to the Assessment tab to continue.

children.title: Assessment
children.summary: Assessment page enables evaluating fulfillment status of assigned compliance criteria per application component.
children.content:
The third page of the Application Compliance Assessment template lets you assess the fulfillment of the compliance criteria that were assigned to the application components in the previous step.

The assessment is performed per application component and per assigned criterion (principle or constraint).

children.title: Assess Compliance
children.summary: Fulfillment status is selected individually per component and criterion, with options like Not met, Partially met, or Fully met.
children.content:
The fulfillment status is recorded individually for each application component and criterion combination:
• Fulfillment status: Select the appropriate fulfillment status of the criterion from the available values (for example, Not met, Partially met or Fully met).

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional options include searching elements and opening Insights dashboards; after assessment, users proceed to Summary.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Assessment page:
• To find elements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .

After finishing the assessment, switch to the Summary tab to continue.

children.title: Summary
children.summary: The Application Compliance Assessment template's last page summarizes assessment results, showing totals of application components and compliance criteria, fulfillment status via a donut chart, and three assessment views (Heatmap, per Application Component, per Criteria), excluding 'No entry' statuses from averages, and suggests next steps like creating workspaces or training.
children.content:
The last page of the Application Compliance Assessment template offers a comprehensive summary of the assessment results. This page has the following areas:
• Application Components in total: Shows the total number of application components evaluated in the workspace.
• Compliance Criteria in total: Shows the total number of unique compliance criteria assigned across all components.
• Fulfillment status: Click Show chart to open a donut chart a donut chart in which each segment represents a fulfillment status. Below the chart, the number of application component and criterion combinations per status is listed. Hover over a segment to see a tooltip listing the exact combinations with that status.
• Assessment Views (Heatmap / per Application / per Guideline): You can switch between three distinct evaluation perspectives:

Heatmap: Displays a matrix chart with application components in rows and criteria in columns. The colour-coded cells show the individual fulfillment status for each combination. Each row and column displays the averaged fulfillment score for that respective element.

per Application Component: Displays a tabular list grouped by application component. For each application component, it shows the averaged fulfillment score along with a detailed breakdown showing the individual fulfillment status for each combination with a criterion.

per Criteria: Displays a tabular list grouped by compliance criterion. For each criterion, it shows the averaged fulfillment score along with a detailed breakdown showing the individual fulfillment status for each combination with an application component.

note

Fulfillment statuses set to No entry do not drag the average down; they are excluded from the calculation.

• What's next?: Check out possible next steps here. How about creating another workspace, or taking part in a free online training for ADOIT?

children.title: Application Investment Planning
children.summary: The Application Investment Planning template guides collaborative assessment of application components and services by selecting elements, evaluating Business and Technology fitness, visualizing results in a TIME model, and assigning investment strategies to support transparent application investment planning.
children.content:
The Application Investment Planning template is a collaborative tool for assessing your application portfolio and defining an appropriate investment strategy. It guides you through selecting relevant elements, evaluating their Business fitness and Technology fitness, visualising the results in a TIME model, and assigning or adjusting investment strategies. This provides a transparent, evidence-based foundation for planning application investments.

Which Elements Are Used?

Application Investment Planning is enabled for Application Components (= applications) and Application Services.

How Does Application Investment Planning Work in ADOIT?

To begin, set up an Application Investment Planning workspace (see Create Workspace).

Once you have created the workspace, follow these steps:
1. Scope – Select the application elements that you want to evaluate and invest in.
2. Business Fitness & Technology Fitness – Perform the assessments.
3. TIME – Review the TIME categorisation of the selected elements.
4. Investment Strategy – Define the investment strategies.
5. Summary – Review the results.

These steps are discussed in more detail in the following sections.

children.title: Scope
children.summary: The Scope page of the Application Investment Planning template allows adding application elements to the workspace for evaluation and investment planning.
children.content: The first page of the Application Investment Planning template lets you add the application elements you want to evaluate and invest in to your workspace.

children.title: Select Elements for Investment Planning
children.summary: To select elements for investment planning, use the left pane to search and add or remove elements, apply bulk actions, and filter by element type (Application Components or Application Services) depending on workspace settings.
children.content:
To define which elements you want to assess:
• In the left pane, all elements that can be added to the workspace are displayed. Use the search box to quickly find a specific element.
• To add an element, click Add. To remove an element, click Remove. For bulk actions, use the Add all and Remove all links at the top of the page.
• If multiple element types are available in your workspace, the Element type list appears at the top left. Use it to control which elements are shown in the left pane. Depending on your workspace settings, you may choose Application Components and Application Services.

children.title: Filter by Workspace, Group, Investment Strategy or Lifecycle State
children.summary: Filters on the Scope page enable selecting elements by Workspaces, Groups, Investment strategy (TIME model categories or 'No entry'), and Lifecycle state, with support for multiple conditions and combined filters.
children.content:
You can use filters to hone in on the specific elements you need:
• Click + Add Filter, and then choose the filter you want:
• Workspaces: Select elements that are already used or evaluated in another workspace.
• Groups: Select elements from specific object groups.
• Investment strategy: Select elements with confirmed investment strategies according to Gartner's TIME model (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, and Eliminate), as well as those with no confirmed investment strategy (indicated by "No entry").
• Lifecycle state: Select elements based on their lifecycle state (Draft, In development, In production, and Retired). You can also include elements without a confirmed lifecycle state (indicated by "No entry").

You can apply multiple conditions to each filter and combine different filters if required.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional Scope page options include opening an element's Insights dashboard and renaming added elements; after selection, proceed to the Business Fitness tab.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Scope page:
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename an element that has been added to the workspace, hover over the element, and then click Edit .

After selecting your application elements, switch to the Business Fitness tab to continue.

children.title: Business Fitness & Technology Fitness
children.summary: The Business Fitness & Technology Fitness pages allow assessing application elements' business and technology fit, with combined information to avoid repetition.
children.content: On the second and third pages of the Application Investment Planning template, you can assess the business fit and technology fit of your application elements. As both assessments work in a similar way, the information for these pages is combined here in one section to avoid repetition.

children.title: Assess an Element
children.summary: Elements can be assessed by filling out surveys directly or sending surveys to editors, with status indicators (Completed, In progress, Sent, Outdated), automatic workspace membership for recipients, and email settings required for survey distribution; scores appear upon completion with notes and warnings for outdated assessments.
children.content:
No matter whether you are assessing business fit or technology fit, there are two ways to proceed:
• Fill Out a Survey on Your Own: In the left pane, select the element you want to assess. You can use the search box to quickly find it. Answer the survey questions, and optionally enter a note in the Additional information box once you are done.
• Send Out a Survey to an Editor: After selecting an element, click Send survey. Start typing the username of a user, and then select the one you want when you see it. If you want, you can customise the email notification and toggle whether you receive email updates when the survey is completed or the editor is removed. Click Send to send out the survey.

When the assessment is finished, the survey will be marked as Completed in the Status column. The overall score will appear in the Business fitness or Technology fit column. The user who filled out the survey, as well as the time and date of completion, will be shown above the survey questions.

note

See Workspaces: How the Score of a Survey Is Calculated for an explanation of how the overall score for an element is calculated.

Before you can send out a survey to another user, the mail settings must be set correctly in the ADOIT Administration (see Email in the Administration Help).

Survey recipients are automatically added to the workspace as members - they do not have to be explicitly added on the Set up your workspace page.

Other Survey Status
• If the assessment of an element has already started but not yet been completed, the survey will be marked as In progress .
• If the survey was sent out to an editor but has not yet been completed, it will be marked as Sent .
• If you defined a survey period when setting up the workspace, surveys completed before the survey period starts or after it ends will be marked as marked as Outdated . If you did not define a survey period, a survey will be marked as marked as Outdated if the assessment is more than 365 days old.
• A warning appears if the assessment results are outdated and differ from the element's current repository values—for example, if the element was assessed in a different workspace or its properties were updated manually.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: On the Business Fitness & Technology Fitness pages, users can remove filled-out survey replies and proceed to the TIME tab after completing assessments.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Business Fitness & Technology Fitness pages:
• To remove an already filled-out reply from a survey, click Remove selection.

After finishing the assessment, switch to the TIME tab to continue.

children.title: TIME Definition
children.summary: The TIME Definition page displays Gartner’s TIME model investment strategies (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, Eliminate) by plotting application elements based on calculated fitness scores from surveys, comparing technical quality against business value.
children.content:
The fourth page of the Application Investment Planning template lets you review the TIME categorisation of your application elements. Gartner’s TIME model proposes four investment strategies (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate and Eliminate).

Learn More

For additional information about the four investment strategies, take a look at Application Portfolio Strategy: Five Steps To Assessing Your Investment Decisions.

ADOIT will calculate the fitness scores of your application elements based on the survey results (see Assess an Element) and place them in the appropriate investment strategy quadrant. The quadrants measure the technical quality of an application against the business value it brings to the organisation.

children.title: Change Thresholds
children.summary: Users can edit the TIME model thresholds by dragging axes in a dialogue to adjust category boundaries, which updates element categorization colors and the Investment Strategy Kanban board accordingly.
children.content:
The x and y axes represent the thresholds between the TIME categories in the chart. You can change the thresholds to influence the automatic assignment of application elements to investment strategies:
• Click Edit thresholds. The chart opens in a new dialogue.
• Drag the axes to a new position, check which elements will be affected, and then click Edit thresholds.

The new thresholds will be saved to the workspace. Application elements will be re-rendered in a different colour if they fall into a different category after a threshold change. Additionally, the Kanban board on the Investment Strategy page will be updated to reflect the changes.

children.title: Use the Categories List
children.summary: The Categories List next to the TIME chart allows searching, collapsing/expanding categories, highlighting elements in the chart, and opening Insights dashboards; after review, users proceed to the Investment Strategy tab.
children.content:
The TIME categories and the application elements that belong to these categories are listed next to the chart. The following options are available:
• To find elements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To collapse or expand one of the assessment categories, click on it.
• To highlight an element in the chart, select it in the list.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .

Once you have gained an overview of the suggested investment strategies, switch to the Investment Strategy tab to continue.

children.title: Investment Strategy
children.summary: The Investment Strategy page features a Kanban board with columns for each investment strategy where elements start unassigned and can be auto-assigned based on fitness scores or manually moved to different strategy columns.
children.content:
The fifth page of the Application Investment Planning template allows you to view and define the investment strategies for your application elements. The page contains a Kanban board where each column represents a specific investment strategy.

All elements appear as cards that initially start in the Unassigned column. You can have ADOIT automatically place them in the recommended columns based on the previously assessed fitness score, or manually drag cards to other columns if you disagree with the recommendations.

children.title: Get More Information
children.summary: Investment Strategy cards display element name, Business and Technology fitness scores, calculated recommendations, optional AI suggestions based on machine learning with confidence over 50%, and warnings for outdated assessments.
children.content:
Before you decide on an investment strategy, make sure to review all the information ADOIT provides. The cards on the Kanban board show the current assessment state of an element:

The following information appears on each card:
• The Name of the element, as well as the Business fitness and Technology fitness scores from the assessments on the Business Fitness & Technology Fitness pages.
• The Recommendation shows the calculated investment strategy based on the survey data.
• In addition to the calculated recommendation, an alternative AI suggestion may be available. Click AI to view it.

note

AI suggestions are based on a machine learning analysis of previous decisions made for similarly assessed elements in your organisation. ADOIT only displays an AI suggestion when there is enough training data and the likelihood of the predicted alternative is greater than 50%.

• Warnings appear if the assessment results are outdated and differ from the element's current repository values—for example, if the element was assessed in a different workspace or its properties were updated manually.

children.title: Choose the Investment Strategy
children.summary: Users can assign investment strategies by moving cards to recommended columns, applying AI suggestions, or manual drag-and-drop; these actions update element properties (Business fitness, Technology fitness, Investment strategy) with score-to-category conversions.
children.content:
Once you have gathered all necessary information, you can make a final decision on the investment strategy for each application element. Choose one of the following options:
• Use Recommended Strategy: To automatically place an element in the proposed column according to the calculated investment strategy, click More on the card and then select Move to recommended. You can also place all elements at once: Click More at the top of the Unassigned column and then select Assign all according to recommendations.
• Use AI Suggestion: If an alternative AI suggestion is available, click AI on the card to view it. In the dialogue, click Move to < column name > to apply the suggestion and automatically move the element to the corresponding column.
• Make Your Own Choice: Drag the card to any column on the Kanban board. In this way, you can even define an investment strategy for elements that have not yet been assessed.

note

When you choose an investment strategy on the Kanban board, the following properties of the element are updated:
• Business fitness
• Technology fitness
• Investment strategy

You can access these properties in another ADOIT scenario, such as "Design & Document", in the "Classification" and "Lifecycle" chapters.

During the update, the Business fitness and Technology fitness assessment scores are converted to the predefined property values as follows:
• 0-25: Bad | 26-50: Medium | 51-75: Good | 76-100: Excellent

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional Investment Strategy page options include searching elements, changing strategies via drag-and-drop or menu, and opening Insights dashboards; after confirmation, proceed to the Summary tab.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Investment Strategy page:
• To find elements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To change an element’s investment strategy, simply drag its card into the appropriate column on the Kanban board. You can also click More on the card and select the new strategy using Move to < column name >.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, click More on the card, and then select Insights.

Once you have confirmed the investment strategy, switch to the Summary tab to continue.

children.title: Summary
children.summary: The Application Investment Planning summary page shows total elements, those without investment strategies, a donut chart of investment categories with element counts and names on hover, and a detailed table or bar chart of elements with fitness scores and assigned strategies, including warnings for outdated assessments and suggestions for next steps.
children.content:
The last page of the Application Investment Planning template offers a summary of all the application elements in the workspace. This page has the following areas:
• Applications in total: Shows the total number of elements in the workspace.
• Applications without investment strategy: Shows how many elements do not yet have an assigned investment strategy.
• Investment strategy: Click Show chart to open a donut chart in which each segment represents an investment category. Below the chart, the number of elements per category is listed. Hover over a segment to see the names of the elements in that category.
• Table/bar chart summary: Provides a detailed overview of all elements in the workspace, including their Business Fitness and Technology Fitness scores from the Business Fitness & Technology Fitness pages, as well as their assigned investment strategies. You can switch between a table view and a bar chart using the Table view and Chart view icons. The table view also shows the categorised assessment scores after they have been converted into the corresponding property values in the "Classification" chapter for each element (e.g. Business Fitness: "Excellent"; see Choose the Investment Strategy for details).

Hovering over a row reveals icons to open an element's Insights dashboard , or access the surveys and the Kanban board .

Warnings appear if the assessment results are outdated and differ from the element's current repository values—for example, if the element was assessed in a different workspace or its properties were updated manually.
• What's next?: Check out possible next steps here. How about creating another workspace, or taking part in a free online training for ADOIT?

children.title: Best Practices
children.summary: Best practices recommend organizing applications into multiple workspaces for confidentiality and clarity, assessing regularly (at least annually) while reusing workspaces to retain survey data, and noting that the last accepted investment strategy applies across multiple workspaces for an application.
children.content:
Here are some tips to help you use Application Investment Planning in ADOIT more effectively.

One or Many Workspaces?

Rather than using a single large workspace, organise your applications into different workspaces for different areas of the organisation. This helps in maintaining confidentiality and makes it easier to keep an overview.

Assess Regularly, Reuse Workspaces

Assess your applications regularly (at least once a year) to make sure the evaluation is still valid. Reuse existing workspaces for this so that the survey data remains, since it would otherwise be lost because it is saved in the context of the workspace.

Applications in Multiple Workspaces

An application can be in more than one workspace. Be aware that the last accepted investment strategy applies to all workspaces.

children.title: Capability Investment Planning
children.summary: The Capability Investment Planning template supports collaborative evaluation of Capabilities and Business Functions by selecting elements, assessing strategic importance and maturity, assigning investment strategies (recommended or manual), providing a clear basis for capability development and resource allocation.
children.content:
The Capability Investment Planning template is a collaborative tool for evaluating your Capabilities and Business Functions as well as determining how best to invest in them. It supports you in selecting the elements to evaluate, assessing their strategic importance and maturity, and ultimately assigning an investment strategy (either by applying the recommendation offered by ADOIT or by selecting a different strategy manually). This provides a clear, evidence-based foundation for planning capability development and resource allocation.

Which Elements Are Used?

Capability Investment Planning is enabled for Capabilities and Business Functions.

How Does Capability Investment Planning Work in ADOIT?

To begin, set up a Capability Investment Planning workspace (see Create Workspace).

Once you have created the workspace, follow these steps:
1. Scope – Select the elements that you want to evaluate and invest in.
2. Strategic Importance & Capability Maturity – Perform the assessments.
3. Strategic Positioning – Define the investment strategies.
4. Summary – Review the results.

These steps are discussed in more detail in the following sections.

children.content: The first page of the Capability Investment Planning template lets you add the elements you want to evaluate and invest in to your workspace.

children.title: Select Elements for Investment Planning

• If multiple element types are available in your workspace, the Element type list appears at the top left. Use it to control which elements are shown in the left pane. Depending on your workspace settings, you may choose Capabilities and Business Functions.

children.title: Filter by Workspace, Group or Level
children.summary: Filters allow selecting elements by Workspaces, Groups, and Level (for Capabilities only), with the Level property set in other scenarios; multiple conditions and combined filters are supported.

You can use filters to hone in on the specific elements you need:

• Level ( Capabilities only): Select capabilities from a specific hierarchical level.

note

The level can be set in another ADOIT scenario, such as "Design & Document", by changing the value of the Level property in the "General" chapter.

You can apply multiple conditions to each filter and combine different filters if required.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional Scope page options include opening an element's Insights dashboard and renaming added elements; after selection, proceed to the Strategic Importance tab.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Scope page:
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename an element that has been added to the workspace, hover over the element, and then click Edit .

After adding your elements, switch to the Strategic Importance tab to continue.

children.title: Strategic Importance & Capability Maturity
children.summary: The Strategic Importance & Capability Maturity pages enable assessing elements' strategic importance and maturity levels, with combined information to avoid repetition.
children.content: On the second and third pages of the Capability Investment Planning template, you can assess the strategic importance and the maturity level of your elements. As both assessments work in a similar way, the information for these pages is combined here in one section to avoid repetition.

Survey recipients are automatically added to the workspace as members - they do not have to be explicitly added on the Set up your workspace page.

Other Survey Status
• If the assessment of an element has already started but not yet been completed, the survey will be marked as In progress .
• If the survey was sent out to an editor but has not yet been completed, it will be marked as Sent .
• If you defined a survey period when setting up the workspace, surveys completed before the survey period starts or after it ends will be marked as marked as Outdated . If you did not define a survey period, a survey will be marked as marked as Outdated if the assessment is more than 365 days old.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: On the Strategic Importance & Capability Maturity pages, users can remove filled-out survey replies and proceed to the Investment Strategy tab after completing assessments.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Strategic Importance & Capability Maturity pages:
• To remove an already filled-out reply from a survey, click Remove selection.

After finishing the assessment, switch to the Investment Strategy tab to continue.

children.title: Strategic Positioning
children.summary: The Strategic Positioning page presents a Kanban board with four investment strategy columns (Minimal attention, Operational Stability, Strategic Priority, Strategic Strength) where elements start unassigned and can be auto-assigned based on assessed scores or manually moved.
children.content:
The fourth page of the Capability Investment Planning template allows you to view and modify the investment strategies for your elements.

ADOIT uses four investment strategies to classify Capabilities and Business Functions: Minimal attention, Operational Stability, Strategic Priority, and Strategic Strength. These strategies are represented as columns on a Kanban board.

All elements appear as cards that initially start in the Unassigned column. You can have ADOIT automatically place them in the recommended columns based on the previously assessed strategic importance and maturity scores, or manually drag cards to other columns if you disagree with the recommendations.

children.title: Get More Information
children.summary: Strategic Positioning cards show element name, Strategic importance and Maturity scores, calculated recommendations, optional AI suggestions with confidence over 50%, and warnings for outdated assessments.
children.content:
Before you decide on an investment strategy, make sure to review all the information ADOIT provides. The cards on the Kanban board show the current assessment state of an element:

The following information appears on each card:
• The Name of the element, as well as the Strategic importance and Maturity scores from the assessments on the Strategic Importance & Capability Maturity pages.
• The Recommendation shows the calculated investment strategy based on the survey data.

children.title: Choose the Investment Strategy
children.summary: Users assign investment strategies by moving cards to recommended columns, applying AI suggestions, or manual drag-and-drop; these update element properties (Strategic importance, Maturity) with score-to-category conversions accessible in other scenarios.
children.content:

• Strategic importance
• Maturity

You can access these properties in another ADOIT scenario, such as "Design & Document". During the update, the assessment scores are converted to the predefined values in the "Classification" chapter as follows:
• Strategic importance: 0-25: Very low | 26-50: Low | 51-75: High | 76-100: Very high
• Maturity: 0-25: Bad | 26-50: Medium | 51-75: Good | 76-100: Excellent

children.title: Change Thresholds
children.summary: Users can edit thresholds between investment strategy categories on a chart by dragging axes, affecting automatic assignment of elements and updating card information accordingly; changes are saved to the workspace.
children.content:
ADOIT proposes four investment strategies for Capabilities and Business Functions: Minimal attention, Operational Stability, Strategic Priority, and Strategic Strength.

The recommended investment category for your elements is calculated based on the survey results (see Assess an Element) by measuring the Strategic importance of an element against its Maturity.

You can change the thresholds between categories to influence the automatic assignment:
• Click Edit thresholds.

This opens a chart that visually represents the investment strategy categories as four quadrants. The x and y axes represent the thresholds between the categories. To change a threshold:
• Drag the axis to a new position, check which elements will be affected, and then click Edit thresholds.

The new threshold will be saved to the workspace. If the recommended strategy for an element changes, the information on the card will be updated, and you can move the card to the recommended category.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional Strategic Positioning page options include searching elements, changing strategies via drag-and-drop or menu, and opening Insights dashboards; after confirmation, proceed to the Summary tab.
children.content:

children.title: Summary
children.summary: The Capability Investment Planning summary page shows total elements, those without strategic positioning, a donut chart of investment categories with element counts and names on hover, and a detailed table or bar chart of elements with strategic importance and maturity scores and assigned strategies, including warnings for outdated assessments and suggestions for next steps.
children.content:
The last page of the Capability Investment Planning template offers a summary of all the elements in the workspace. This page has the following areas:

• Capabilities without strategic positioning: Shows how many elements do not yet have an assigned investment strategy.
