children.title: Application-Based Roadmap
children.summary: The Application-based Roadmap template in ADOIT enables planning around application elements by defining, prioritising, scheduling, and tracking Requirements to support application evolution or retirement through a structured six-step process.
children.content:
The Application-based Roadmap template provides a shared workspace for application-based planning. It helps you define, prioritise, schedule, and track Requirements that support the evolution, transformation, or retirement of your application landscape.

Structure your roadmap around your application elements to ensure that planning decisions are aligned with your architectural and strategic direction.

Which Elements Are Used?

Application-based Roadmaps start from a set of application elements, such as Application Components, Application Services, Application Functions, or Application Interfaces. Based on these elements, you define and manage the associated Requirements.

How Do Application-Based Roadmaps Work in ADOIT?

You can start from scratch or build on application elements that have already been analysed in an Application Investment Planning workspace.

To begin, set up an Application-based Roadmap workspace (see Create Workspace).

Once you have created the workspace, follow these steps:
1. Scope – Select the application elements that define the scope of your roadmap.
2. Requirements – Define the requirements for the selected elements.
3. Priority – Prioritise the defined requirements.
4. Schedule – Plan the requirements on a Kanban board.
5. Status – Track the progress of your requirements.
6. Summary – Review the results and determine your next steps.

These steps are discussed in more detail in the following sections.

children.title: Scope
children.summary: The Scope page of the Application-based Roadmap template allows selection of application elements that define the roadmap's scope.
children.content: The first page of the Application-based Roadmap template lets you select the application elements that define the scope of your roadmap.

children.title: Select Application Elements for Roadmap
children.summary: Select application elements to include in the roadmap by adding or removing them from the left pane, filtering by element type such as Application Components or Services.
children.content:
To define which application elements you want to include:
• In the left pane, all application elements that can be added to the workspace are displayed. Use the search box to quickly find a specific element.
• To add an element, click Add. To remove an element, click Remove. For bulk actions, use the Add all and Remove all links at the top of the page.
• If multiple element types are available in your workspace, the Element type list appears at the top left. Use it to control which elements are shown in the left pane. Depending on your workspace settings, you may choose Application Components, Application Services, Application Functions and Application Interfaces.

children.title: Filter by Workspace, Group, Investment Strategy or Lifecycle State
children.summary: Filters like Workspace, Group, Investment Strategy (Gartner's TIME model), and Lifecycle State can be applied and combined to refine the selection of application elements.
children.content:
You can use filters to hone in on the specific elements you need:
• Click + Add Filter, and then choose the filter you want:
• Workspaces: Select application elements that are already used or evaluated in another workspace.
• Groups: Select application elements from specific object groups.
• Investment strategy: Use this filter to select application elements with confirmed investment strategies according to Gartner's TIME model (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, and Eliminate), as well as those with no confirmed investment strategy (indicated by "No entry").
• Lifecycle state: Use this filter to select application elements based on their lifecycle state (Draft, In development, In production, and Retired). You can also include elements without a confirmed lifecycle state (indicated by "No entry").

You can apply multiple conditions to each filter and combine different filters if required.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional Scope page options include opening an element's Insights dashboard and renaming elements added to the workspace before proceeding to the Requirements tab.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the Scope page:
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename an element that has been added to the workspace, hover over the element, and then click Edit .

After selecting your application elements, switch to the Requirements tab to continue.

children.title: Requirements
children.summary: The Requirements page lists all application elements in the workspace along with their associated requirements, showing investment strategy, lifecycle state, and requirement status.
children.content:
On the second page of the Application-based Roadmap template, you can define requirements for all application elements that have been added to the workspace.

The application elements are listed along with their associated requirements. Furthermore, for application elements, the current investment strategy and lifecycle state are visible, while requirements display their status.

children.title: Add Requirements to Application Elements
children.summary: Requirements can be added to application elements by searching for existing ones, creating new ones, or using AI-generated suggestions if enabled, via an Add Requirement dialog with multiple tabs.
children.content:
There are two ways to add requirements to an application element. Choose one of the following options:
• Add Requirement: Click Add Requirement below the element to search for an existing requirement or create a new one.

Start typing the name of a requirement, and then select the one you want when you see it. If the requirement does not yet exist, finish typing the name and press < Enter > to create it.

To see more options, click Show more. This opens a support dialog with the following tabs:
• Assigned requirements: Displays all requirements already assigned to the element.
• All existing requirements: Lists all requirements in the repository. You can filter requirements, select the ones you want to assign, and click Add.
• AI: Click AI to browse AI-generated requirement suggestions. A list of relevant requirements will be created based on an AI model.

You can filter the results, select the requirements you want to assign, and click Add.

note

AI-generated suggestions must be enabled by your ADOIT administrator for each repository.

children.title: View and Edit Requirement Details
children.summary: Requirement details such as Description and Estimated cost can be viewed and edited by expanding the requirement entry; both fields are optional.
children.content:
Expand a requirement to view or edit additional information. Two fields are available:
• Description: A textual description of the requirement.
• Estimated cost: The estimated cost associated with the requirement.

Both fields are optional and can be filled in at any time.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: Additional options on the Requirements page include searching, filtering by element or requirement attributes, removing or deleting requirements, accessing Insights dashboards, and renaming requirements.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the second page of the Application-based Roadmap template:
• To find requirements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To filter application elements or requirements, click + Add Filter and choose the filter you want:
• Application elements: Filter by investment strategy or lifecycle state.
• Requirements: Filter by status or by the application elements they are associated with.
• To remove a requirement, hover over the requirement, and then click Remove element . Choose whether to:
• Remove the requirement only from the application element it has been added to.
• Remove it from all application elements in the workspace.
• Delete it entirely from all workspaces and the repository.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename a requirement, hover over the requirement, and then click Edit .

After adding requirements to your application elements, switch to the Priority tab to continue.

children.title: Priority
children.summary: The Priority page allows prioritisation of defined requirements for application elements.
children.content: The third page of the Application-based Roadmap template lets you prioritise the requirements that you defined in the previous step.

children.title: Value vs. Effort Method and Eisenhower Matrix
children.summary: Prioritisation methods include the Value vs. Effort Method and the Eisenhower Matrix, both using a 2×2 quadrant grid labeled by value/effort or urgency/importance with estimated costs displayed per quadrant.
children.content:
The appearance of the page depends on the prioritisation method chosen during the setup of the workspace:
• The Value vs. Effort Method allows your team to prioritise requirements based on their value and the effort required to implement them.
• The Eisenhower Matrix allows your team to organise requirements based on their urgency and importance.

The common visual element in both of these prioritisation methods is a 2×2 grid, which divides requirements into four quadrants. The quadrants are labelled to indicate the level of value and effort or importance and urgency required. Each quadrant displays the total estimated cost of the requirements placed in it.

children.title: Put Requirements into Quadrants
children.summary: Requirements can be prioritised by dragging them into quadrants or using the More menu; pairwise comparisons within quadrants can refine priority order.
children.content:
All requirements are listed in the column on the left. Requirements that have already been prioritised are greyed-out.

There are two ways to prioritise a requirement:
• Drag it to the quadrant you want.
• Click the More button , and then click Add to < quadrant-name >.

If you need to change the prioritisation, you can also move requirements from one quadrant to another.

note

Consider performing pairwise comparisons within each quadrant: Adapt the position of different requirements relative to each other to further refine their priority. This helps in determining which requirements within a specific category should be implemented first.

children.title: Change Thresholds
children.summary: Thresholds between quadrants on the prioritisation grid can be adjusted by dragging axes, with changes saved to the workspace.
children.content:
The x and y axes represent the thresholds between the quadrants in the chart. To change a threshold:
• Drag the axis to a new position.

The new threshold will be saved to the workspace.

Once you have prioritised the requirements, switch to the Schedule tab to continue.

children.title: Schedule

children.content:
The fourth page of the Application-based Roadmap template lets you schedule the requirements that you prioritised in the previous step. The page contains a Kanban board where each column represents a specific time period (months, quarters, or years depending on your workspace settings).

All requirements appear as cards that initially start in the Unassigned area on the left and can be dragged to a column to put them on the roadmap.

children.title: Get Information
children.summary: Kanban cards display prioritisation category, evaluation scores, and estimated costs to inform scheduling decisions.
children.content: Before deciding when a requirement should be implemented, it's essential to check all the information provided by ADOIT. The Kanban board cards display the prioritisation category (quadrant) and the scores assigned to the two evaluation criteria from the Priority page, as well as the estimated costs from the Requirements page.

children.title: Place Requirements on the Roadmap
children.summary: Requirements are placed on the roadmap by dragging cards to columns or using the More menu to move them; reassignment is supported.
children.content:
Once you have all the necessary information, you can define when a requirement should be implemented. There are two ways to place a requirement on the roadmap:
• Drag its card to the desired column on the Kanban board.
• Click More on the card, and then select a column under Move to < column name >.

If you need to reassign a requirement, you can simply move it to a different column.

children.title: Add or Remove Columns
children.summary: Columns representing time periods can be added or removed (only at roadmap ends) on the Kanban board to manage the schedule layout.
children.content:
You can manage the columns on your roadmap. Depending on your workspace settings, these columns may represent months, quarters, or years:
• To add a column, click the Add column button at the top, on the left or right side of the Kanban board.
• To remove a column, hover over it and click Remove column . Columns can only be removed at the beginning or end of the roadmap.

Once you have planned your requirements, switch to the Status tab to continue.

children.title: Status

children.content:
On the fifth page of the Application-based Roadmap template, you can track the implementation status of requirements over time using a Kanban board.

The Kanban board consists of columns that represent different statuses, with each requirement displayed as a card. Initially, all requirements appear in the Unassigned area on the left. You can assign a status by dragging a requirement card into the corresponding column. As progress is made, you can update the status by moving the cards between columns.

children.title: Get Information
children.summary: Status assignment should consider each card's prioritisation category and planned timeframe displayed on the Kanban board.
children.content: Each card on the Kanban board displays the assigned prioritisation category (quadrant) from the Priority page, as well as the planned implementation timeframe from the Schedule page. Check this information before you assign a status to a requirement.

children.title: Set the Status of the Requirements
children.summary: Requirement status can be set by dragging cards or via the More menu, with statuses including Not started, On-track, Caution, Off-track, and Completed.
children.content:
There are two ways to set the status of a requirement:
• Drag its card to the desired column on the Kanban board.
• Click More on the card, and then select a status under Move to < column name >.

If you need to update the status, you can simply move it to a different column.

note

The available statuses are: Not started, On-track, Caution, Off-track, and Completed.

Once all statuses are set, switch to the Summary tab to continue.

children.title: Summary

children.content:
The last page of the Application-based Roadmap template offers a summary of all the requirements in the workspace. This page has the following areas:
• Application elements in total: Displays the total number of application elements in the workspace.
• Requirements in total: Shows the total number of requirements in the workspace.
• Status per prioritisation: Click Show chart to open a sunburst chart that visually represents how requirements are categorised and their current progress. The inner rings indicate the assigned prioritisation category (quadrant) from the Priority page, while the outer rings show the status from the Status page. Below the chart, the number of requirements per status is listed. Hover over a slice in the outer ring to see the names of requirements in that specific category and status.
• Status per time period: Click Show Chart to open a bar chart displaying the number of requirements per time period and status. Hover over a bar to view the names of the requirements that fall within that specific time period and status.
• Table/Kanban summary: Provides a detailed overview of all application elements and their assigned requirements, including prioritisation category, planned timeframe, and current status. You can switch between a table view and a Kanban board using the Table view and Kanban view icons.
• What's next?: Check out possible next steps here. How about creating another workspace, or taking part in a free online training for ADOIT?

children.content:
Expand a requirement to view or edit additional information. Two fields are available:
• Description: A textual description of the requirement.
• Estimated cost: The estimated cost associated with the requirement.

Both fields are optional and can be filled in at any time.

children.title: Additional Options
children.summary: The second page of the Goal-based Roadmap template offers options to search, filter, remove, rename requirements, and open Insights dashboards for motivation elements before proceeding to prioritisation.
children.content:
The following additional options are available on the second page of the Goal-based Roadmap template:
• To find requirements, in the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.
• To filter requirements, click + Add Filter and choose the filter you want:
• Filter by status or by the motivation elements they are associated with.
• To remove a requirement, hover over the requirement, and then click Remove element . Choose whether to:
• Remove the requirement only from the motivation element it has been added to.
• Remove it from all motivation elements in the workspace.
• Delete it entirely from all workspaces and the repository.
• To open the Insights dashboard of an element, hover over the element, and then click Insights .
• To rename a requirement, hover over the requirement, and then click Edit .

After adding requirements to your motivation elements, switch to the Priority tab to continue.

children.title: Priority
children.summary: The third page of the Goal-based Roadmap template enables prioritisation of requirements defined earlier.
children.content: The third page of the Goal-based Roadmap template lets you prioritise the requirements that you defined in the previous step.

children.title: Value vs. Effort Method and Eisenhower Matrix
children.summary: The prioritisation page displays either the Value vs. Effort Method or Eisenhower Matrix as a 2×2 grid to categorise requirements by value/effort or urgency/importance, showing total estimated costs per quadrant.
children.content:
The appearance of the page depends on the prioritisation method chosen during the setup of the workspace:
• The Value vs. Effort Method allows your team to prioritise requirements based on their value and the effort required to implement them.
• The Eisenhower Matrix allows your team to organise requirements based on their urgency and importance.

The common visual element in both of these prioritisation methods is a 2×2 grid, which divides requirements into four quadrants. The quadrants are labelled to indicate the level of value and effort or importance and urgency required. Each quadrant displays the total estimated cost of the requirements placed in it.

children.title: Put Requirements into Quadrants
children.summary: Requirements can be prioritised by dragging them into quadrants or using the More button, with greyed-out items already prioritised; pairwise comparisons within quadrants are recommended for finer prioritisation.
children.content:
All requirements are listed in the column on the left. Requirements that have already been prioritised are greyed-out.

There are two ways to prioritise a requirement:
• Drag it to the quadrant you want.
• Click the More button , and then click Add to < quadrant-name >.

If you need to change the prioritisation, you can also move requirements from one quadrant to another.

note

Consider performing pairwise comparisons within each quadrant: Adapt the position of different requirements relative to each other to further refine their priority. This helps in determining which requirements within a specific category should be implemented first.

children.title: Change Thresholds
children.summary: Thresholds between quadrants on the prioritisation chart can be adjusted by dragging axes, with changes saved to the workspace before moving on to scheduling.
children.content:
The x and y axes represent the thresholds between the quadrants in the chart. To change a threshold:
• Drag the axis to a new position.

The new threshold will be saved to the workspace.

Once you have prioritised the requirements, switch to the Schedule tab to continue.

children.title: Schedule
children.summary: The fourth page of the Goal-based Roadmap template provides a Kanban board to schedule prioritised requirements by dragging cards into time period columns representing months, quarters, or years.
children.content:
The fourth page of the Goal-based Roadmap template lets you schedule the requirements that you prioritised in the previous step. The page contains a Kanban board where each column represents a specific time period (months, quarters, or years depending on your workspace settings).

All requirements appear as cards that initially start in the Unassigned area on the left and can be dragged to a column to put them on the roadmap.

children.title: Get Information
children.summary: Kanban board cards display prioritisation category, evaluation scores, and estimated costs to inform scheduling decisions for requirements.
children.content: Before deciding when a requirement should be implemented, it's essential to check all the information provided by ADOIT. The Kanban board cards display the prioritisation category (quadrant) and the scores assigned to the two evaluation criteria from the Priority page, as well as the estimated costs from the Requirements page.

children.title: Place Requirements on the Roadmap
children.summary: Requirements can be placed on the roadmap by dragging cards to desired columns or using the More menu, with easy reassignment by moving cards between columns.
children.content:
Once you have all the necessary information, you can define when a requirement should be implemented. There are two ways to place a requirement on the roadmap:
• Drag its card to the desired column on the Kanban board.
• Click More on the card, and then select a column under Move to < column name >.

If you need to reassign a requirement, you can simply move it to a different column.

children.title: Add or Remove Columns
children.summary: Roadmap columns representing time periods can be added or removed (only at start/end) via buttons on the Kanban board, before proceeding to status tracking.
children.content:
You can manage the columns on your roadmap. Depending on your workspace settings, these columns may represent months, quarters, or years:
• To add a column, click the Add column button at the top, on the left or right side of the Kanban board.
• To remove a column, hover over it and click Remove column . Columns can only be removed at the beginning or end of the roadmap.

Once you have planned your requirements, switch to the Status tab to continue.

children.title: Status
children.summary: The fifth page uses a Kanban board with columns representing statuses to track requirement implementation, allowing drag-and-drop assignment and updates from the Unassigned area.
children.content:
On the fifth page of the Goal-based Roadmap template, you can track the implementation status of requirements over time using a Kanban board.

The Kanban board consists of columns that represent different statuses, with each requirement displayed as a card. Initially, all requirements appear in the Unassigned area on the left. You can assign a status by dragging a requirement card into the corresponding column. As progress is made, you can update the status by moving the cards between columns.

children.title: Get Information
children.summary: Kanban cards show prioritisation category and planned timeframe to review before assigning or updating requirement statuses.
children.content: Each card on the Kanban board displays the assigned prioritisation category (quadrant) from the Priority page, as well as the planned implementation timeframe from the Schedule page. Check this information before you assign a status to a requirement.

children.title: Set the Status of the Requirements
children.summary: Requirement statuses can be set or updated by dragging cards or using the More menu, with available statuses including Not started, On-track, Caution, Off-track, and Completed; then proceed to summary.
children.content:
There are two ways to set the status of a requirement:
• Drag its card to the desired column on the Kanban board.
• Click More on the card, and then select a status under Move to < column name >.

If you need to update the status, you can simply move it to a different column.

note

The available statuses are: Not started, On-track, Caution, Off-track, and Completed.

Once all statuses are set, switch to the Summary tab to continue.

children.title: Summary
children.summary: The final Goal-based Roadmap page summarizes motivation elements, requirements, status per prioritisation and time period via charts, and provides detailed table/Kanban views plus next steps suggestions.
children.content:
The last page of the Goal-based Roadmap template offers a summary of all the requirements in the workspace. This page has the following areas:
• Motivation elements in total: Displays the total number of motivation elements in the workspace.
• Requirements in total: Shows the total number of requirements in the workspace.
• Status per prioritisation: Click Show chart to open a sunburst chart that visually represents how requirements are categorised and their current progress. The inner rings indicate the assigned prioritisation category (quadrant) from the Priority page, while the outer rings show the status from the Status page. Below the chart, the number of requirements per status is listed. Hover over a slice in the outer ring to see the names of requirements in that specific category and status.
• Status per time period: Click Show Chart to open a bar chart displaying the number of requirements per time period and status. Hover over a bar to view the names of the requirements that fall within that specific time period and status.
• Table/Kanban summary: Provides a detailed overview of all motivation elements and their assigned requirements, including prioritisation category, planned timeframe, and current status. You can switch between a table view and a Kanban board using the Table view and Kanban view icons.
• What's next?: Check out possible next steps here. How about creating another workspace, or taking part in a free online training for ADOIT?

children.title: Adjust Workspaces
children.summary: Workspaces can be renamed, deleted, and have settings changed including name, users, and permissions via the Workspaces Page or within the workspace; deletion is restricted to administrators.
children.content:
Workspaces can be renamed, deleted, and more.

Change Workspace Settings

You can change general workspace settings such as the name, assigned users and permissions. Choose one of the following options:
• On the Workspaces Page: Click the More button on the tile of the workspace, and then click Settings. Select the settings you want, and then click Save & Close.
• From the Workspace: Click the Settings button. Select the settings you want, and then click Save & Close.

note

For more information on the available settings, see Create Workspace.

Delete Workspace

Administrators can delete a workspace. Choose one of the following options:
• On the Workspaces Page: Click the More button on the tile of the workspace, and then click Delete.
• From the Workspace: Click the Settings button, and then click Delete workspace.

children.title: Search and Filter Workspaces
children.summary: The Workspaces page supports filtering by type and permissions, sorting by various criteria, and searching by name to quickly find workspaces.
children.content:
To help you quickly find a workspace on the Workspaces page, the following options are available:

Filter by Type

To filter workspaces by type:
• Click All types, and then select the option you want.

You can view all workspaces or just workspaces of a specific type.

Filter by Permissions

To filter workspaces by permissions:
• Click All workspaces, and then select the option you want.

You can view all workspaces, filter by creator, or view my workspaces (= all workspaces where you have been added as a member or admin).

Sort Workspaces

To sort workspaces:
• Click Sort by name, and then select the option you want.

You can sort workspaces by name, by author, by date of last change, or by template.

Search

To find a workspace:
• In the Filter... box, type the text you want to search for.

All workspaces that contain the search string in their name are shown.

children.title: Export Summary
children.summary: Workspace summaries can be exported as Excel files with content varying by workspace type, including survey sheets, summaries, requirement overviews, contract data, or compliance criteria.
children.content:
From any page within a workspace, you can export a summary as an Excel file (XLSX format):
• Click Export at the top right of the workspace.

Content of the Export File

The exported Excel file contains one or more sheets, depending on the workspace type:
• Planning: Exports for Application Investment Planning and Capability Investment Planning workspaces contain three sheets:
• One sheet per survey, containing all questions and recorded answers.
• A summary sheet with relevant data for all elements in the workspace.
• Roadmapping: Exports for Application-based Roadmaps, Capability-based Roadmaps, and Goal-based Roadmaps contain a single sheet. This sheet provides an overview of all elements and their assigned requirements.
• Cost management: Exports for Application Cost Management workspaces contain one sheet with relevant data for all application elements and their associated contracts.
• Compliance assessment: Exports for Application Compliance Assessment workspaces contain one sheet with relevant data for all application elements and their assigned compliance criteria.

children.title: The "Control & Release" Scenario
children.summary: The "Control & Release" scenario enables reviewing and releasing EA objects with one click, accessible only if EA workflow is enabled, and includes toolbar features like Find and Dashboards.
children.content:
The purpose of the "Control & Release" scenario is to let you review and release objects with a single click.

note

The "Control & Release" scenario is only avalaible if the EA workflow is enabled.

What you will see on the "Control & Release" start page

The start page has the following appearance:
• Review and release your EA objects with a single click: Review and release objects. The Control & Release dashboard will show you all repository objects with transitions that you can execute.

Additional Options

The toolbar at the top of the screen provides access to some of the most used features in ADOIT:
• Find : Open the Explorer and the search function in ADOIT. Multiple search and filtering options help you quickly find the artefact you are looking for.
• Dashboards : Open and configure configurable dashboards.

children.title: "Control & Release" Dashboard
children.summary: The "Control & Release" dashboard lists repository objects grouped by status for transition execution, with filtering options by responsibility, object type, and state, and quick release actions via the Actions button.
children.content:
This area lists all repository objects for which you can execute a transition. The objects are grouped by status and sorted alphabetically.

Object Release

You can release objects quickly. In order to execute a transition:
1. Click the Actions button to display all available transitions.
2. Click the appropriate icon.

Filter Architecture Elements (All/My)

You can switch between displaying All or My architecture elements (= objects). For details, please refer to the section Filter Objects by Responsibility (All/My).

Filter Architecture Elements by Object Type

In order to only display objects of a certain type:
1. Click the Object type filter button .
2. Select the object types which should be visible in ADOIT.
3. Click Apply.

Filter Architecture Elements by State

In order to filter objects by state:
• Click the icons , or .

You can show or hide objects in the state "Draft", "Under review" or "To be deleted".

children.title: The "Read & Explore" Scenario
children.summary: The "Read & Explore" scenario provides a read-only overview of architecture artefacts including personalised models/dashboards, recent and favourite artefacts, with toolbar access to Find, Dashboards, and optionally AI Assistant.
children.content:
Via the "Read & Explore" scenario users can get a quick overview of architecture artefacts in ADOIT.

note

The "Read & Explore" scenario is read-only. Users have no write access to repository content (including all models and objects and their relations).

What you will see on the "Read & Explore" start page

The start page ("Home") has the following appearance:
• Personal model or dashboard: A model or configurable dashboard that you can personalise according to your needs. You can use the suggested content or select your own.
• Recently opened: Your most recently opened models and objects. Sorted by date, with the most recent artefact placed at the top. To see additional artefacts, click Show more....
• Favourites: Your favourite models and objects. Sorted alphabetically. To see additional artefacts, click Show more....

View your most recently opened models and objects as well as your favourites as thumbnails or a list. You can easily switch between the two layouts using the Show list and Show tiles icons.

note

If custom images have been uploaded for specific ArchiMate elements, they will appear as thumbnails, replacing the standard icons for those elements.

Additional Options

The toolbar at the top of the screen provides access to some of the most used features in ADOIT:
• Find : Open the Explorer and the search function in ADOIT. Multiple search and filtering options help you quickly find the artefact you are looking for.
• Dashboards : Open and configure configurable dashboards.

Information for upgrading users

The built-in legacy dashboards Architecture Diagrams, Capabilities, Business Processes, Business Objects, Application Components and System Software have been removed in ADOIT 21.0. You can recreate most of these views using configurable dashboards.

If your licence allows it, you can access additional features in the bottom right corner:
• AI Assistant: Use the AI Assistant to interact with ADOIT. You can ask questions in natural language, search and retrieve repository information, and discuss enterprise architecture and ArchiMate concepts.

children.title: Personalise the Start Page
children.summary: Users can personalise the "Read & Explore" start page by selecting a model or configurable dashboard and restore administrator-defined defaults; personalisation requires administrator enablement.
children.content:
The ADOIT administrator can set default content that all users see when they open the "Read & Explore" start page. Users can personalise this content by selecting a model or configurable dashboard, and restore the default settings at any time.

Select a Model or Dashboard

To personalise the start page:
• On the "Read & Explore" start page, click the Personalise button.
• Select a model from the Model Catalogue or a configurable dashboard from the Object Catalogue, and then click OK.

Restore Default Settings

To restore the default settings, as defined by your ADOIT administrator:
• Click the down arrow symbol in the Personalise button, and then click Restore default settings.

The default settings will be restored. If your ADOIT administrator has defined default content for all users, it will be shown now. Otherwise, an empty widget will be shown.

note

If you are not able to personalise the start page, please ask your ADOIT administrator to enable the functionality in the ADOIT Administration.

children.title: Organisation Portal
children.summary: The Organisation Portal offers read-only, intuitive access to ADOIT models without user accounts, available only to existing licensed customers, accessible via login page or dropdown menu, using a technical user account.
children.content:
note

The Organisation Portal is no longer available to new customers. Existing customers with licences that include the Organisation Portal may continue to use it.

The Organisation Portal allows employees of your organisation easy and intuitive access to the models in the ADOIT database. Personalized dashboards and other complex functions are not included in the Organisation Portal. Access to the Organisation Portal does not require a user account.

note

The Organisation Portal is read-only. Users have no write access to repository content (including all models and objects and their relations).

To enter the Organisation Portal:
• Click the Go to Organisation Portal link on the ADOIT login page or:
• While logged in, select Organisation Portal from the dropdown menu at the top left corner of the program window. You will be logged out of ADOIT (a technical user account is used to access the Organisation Portal).

children.title: Modelling
children.summary: The Modelling section covers creating, connecting, editing models and objects, using AI Assistant, navigation, Explorer management, favourites, property editing, image embedding, document management, tabular editor, import/export, filtering, metamodel profiles, and scenario planning.
children.content:
In this part of the manual, the following topics are outlined:
• Create Models: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for creating new models in ADOIT.
• Model and Connect Objects: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for adding and connecting objects in the graphical editor.
• Edit Models: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for editing models in the graphical editor.
• Use the AI Assistant: The AI Assistant provides a chat for interacting with ADOIT. You can ask questions in natural language, search and retrieve repository information, and discuss enterprise architecture and ArchiMate concepts.
• Working with Navigation and View Tools: The navigation and view tools let you navigate through models, analyses etc. and control how you see your models.
• Working with the Explorer: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions managing models and objects in the Explorer.
• Favourites in ADOIT: Favourites are a great way to save models and objects that you want to access quickly in ADOIT.
• Add Information to Models & Objects: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for managing the properties of models, objects and connectors.
• Embed Images in Models: ADOIT allows uploading images into the database in order to use them in models.
• Document Management: ADOIT allows the import and management of external files in the database. The imported files are maintained as documents in the Object Catalogue.
• Tabular Editor: Large-Scale Property Editing: The tabular editor offers the opportunity to clearly display object properties, even in large models. Property values can be edited quickly and extensively.
• Import/Export ArchiMate Model Exchange File: The ArchiMate Model Exchange File format is the standard file format for the exchange of ArchiMate models between different applications. ADOIT supports importing and exporting ArchiMate models in the exchange file format.
• Import/Export Objects: Objects can be imported from other applications into ADOIT and exported from ADOIT into other applications.
• Filter Objects – Time Filter, State Filter & Categories Filter: ADOIT includes filter mechanisms which allow you to control the visibility of objects:
• Metamodel Profile Configurator: The Metamodel Profile Configurator allows power users to choose between various predefined metamodel profiles in ADOIT.
• Scenario Planning in ADOIT: With Scenario Planning in ADOIT, you can design future architectures without affecting your current repository data.

children.title: Create Models
children.summary: This section introduces key functions for creating new models in ADOIT.
children.content: The following sections provide an overview of the functions needed for creating new models in ADOIT.

children.title: Create Model
children.summary: Models can be created via the New button by selecting a model type or directly in the Model Catalogue, with search and filter options and administrator-defined recommendations available.
children.content:
To create a new model:
1. On the toolbar at the top of the screen, click New .
2. Select a model type. The model is created and simultaneously opened in the graphical editor.

Now you can start placing objects on the drawing area.

Recommendations

Your ADOIT administrator may define a set of recommended model and object types. They will be displayed in the Recommendations pane.

note

If no recommended elements have been configured, the Recommendations pane is not shown.

Find What You Need

To help you quickly find the artefact you want to create, the following options are available:
• Search for a Model or Object Type: In the Search box, type the text you want to search for. All model and object types that contain the search string in their name are displayed. To clear the search filter, click the icon .
• Filter by Topic: Click the button , select the topic you want, and then click Apply. You can display a topic-specific selection of model and object types. Additionally, you can display all models or all objects.

Create Models Directly in the Model Catalogue

Alternatively, you can create models directly in the Model Catalogue:
• Open the Model Catalogue. For details please refer to the sections Open Explorer and Switch between Catalogues in Explorer.
• Select the model group in which the model shall be created.
• Right-click the model group, and then click Create model.

children.title: The Drawing Area
children.summary: The drawing area in the graphical editor displays all modelled objects and connectors once a model is opened.
children.content: As soon as a (new or saved) model is opened in the graphical editor, a drawing area appears. All modelled objects and connectors are shown there.

children.title: The Modelling Bar
children.summary: The modelling bar appears when a model with write access is open, showing general function icons and available object types, varying by model mode.
children.content:
Whenever a model is shown in the graphical editor where you have write access, ADOIT activates the modelling bar. It contains icons for all object types that are available in the current mode of the active model. Thus, the look of the modelling bar varies widely.

The modelling bar is divided into two parts: The top end holds the general function icons (e.g. Edit, Create relation) and below them the available object types are displayed.

children.title: Save Model
children.summary: Models can be saved or saved as copies with new names and target groups via the Save button or its dropdown; read-only models only allow Save as.
children.content:
ADOIT gives you several options for saving a model.

Save

To save changes to a model:
1. Click the Save button in the menu bar of the model.
2. Enter a name for the model and define a target group if you are saving it for the first time.

Save as

To create a copy of the model with a new name:
1. Click the down arrow symbol in the Save button .
2. Select Save as from the drop-down menu.
3. Change the name of the model.
4. Define the target group for the new model.
5. Click OK. The model is created and simultaneously opened in the graphical editor.

note

If a model only allows read access, the Save button is replaced by the Save as button in the menu bar of the model.

children.title: Close Model
children.summary: Models can be closed individually via the close icon or collectively via the Opened views menu using Close all.
children.content:
Once a model is no longer required for work, you should close it to improve clarity.

Close Active Model

In order to close the currently active model:
• Click the icon at the top right corner of the open model.

Close Individual/All Open Models, Analyses etc.

In order to close models, analyses etc. you recently viewed:
• Click the Opened views button at the top right corner of the program window.
• Do one of the following:
• To close a specific model, click the "x" on a tile.
• To close all models, click the Close all button.

children.title: Model and Connect Objects
children.summary: This section outlines key functions for adding and connecting objects in the graphical editor.
children.content: The following sections provide an overview of the most important functions for adding and connecting objects in the graphical editor.

children.title: Create Objects in the Graphical Editor
children.summary: Objects can be created manually from the modelling bar or using the Hover Modelling Assistant which suggests next objects after the first manual creation; repository objects can also be created in the Object Catalogue.
children.content:
To create objects in the graphical editor, you can do the following:
• Create objects manually by selecting them in the modelling bar and placing them where you want to or:
• Once you have created the first object in a model manually, use the Hover Modelling Assistant to automatically place additional objects on the drawing area.

note

This scenario particularly applies to modelling objects. Repository objects can also be created directly in the Object Catalogue.

children.title: Create Objects Manually
children.summary: To create objects manually, select an object type from the modelling bar, place it on the drawing area, and enter a name.
children.content:
In order to create objects manually, proceed as follows:
1. Select an object in the modelling bar, and drag it onto the drawing area, or click where you want to add the object.
2. Enter a name for the object.

children.title: Create Objects Using the Hover Modelling Assistant
children.summary: The Hover Modelling Assistant suggests objects to add next, allowing automatic placement with connector selection, manual placement by dragging, or insertion between connected objects with automatic connector splitting.
children.content:
The Hover Modelling Assistant helps speed up the modelling process. Depending on the currently selected object, it suggests which objects should be added next.

In order to use the modelling assistant:
• Create a new object manually or select an object you have previously created. When you do that, the modelling assistant appears.

note

If the modelling assistant does not appear, it may be disabled. For details on how to adapt your personal settings, please refer to the section Modelling.

Now do one of the following:
• Place Object Automatically: Click the object you want to add to the model. The new object is placed on the drawing area close to the original object. Select the type of connector that should connect both objects and enter a name for the new object. If only one type of connector is possible, the connector will be created automatically.

To see additional object choices, click the More button , and then select an object from the menu that appears.
• Place Object Manually: Drag the object you want to add to the desired location on the drawing area. When you release the mouse button, the new object is created.
• Insert Object between Two Connected Objects: Select the object after which you want to insert the new object, and then click the object you want to add to the model. ADOIT splits the connector up automatically and connects the new object to the neighbouring objects.

children.title: Connect Objects
children.summary: Connectors between objects can be drawn manually via the Create relation icon or using the Hover Modelling Assistant, with ADOIT validating connector types and offering choices if multiple apply; connectors can be straight or right-angled.
children.content:
To draw a connector between two objects, choose one of the following options:

Draw Connector Manually

In order to draw a connector manually:
1. Click the Create relation icon at the top of the modelling bar.
2. Click the object the connector should start from.
3. Click the target object.

Draw Connector Using the Hover Modelling Assistant

In order to draw a connector using the modelling assistant:
1. Select the object the connector should start from. When you do that, the modelling assistant appears.
2. Select the Create relation icon , and drag it onto the target object, or click the target object.

note

If the modelling assistant does not appear, it may be disabled. For details on how to adapt your personal settings, please refer to the section Modelling.

For every connector type only certain object types are defined where it may begin or end. When drawing a connector, ADOIT instantly checks whether and how the “from and to” objects can be connected. The following cases can occur:
• One Type of Connector Matches "from and to" Objects: The connector is drawn.
• Several Types of Connectors Match "from and to" Objects: A support dialogue opens. All valid connector types for incoming and outgoing connectors are listed as sub items. Choose the desired connector type.
• Target Object Invalid for Connector: The connector cannot be created.

Rectangular Connectors vs. Straight Connectors

By default, ADOIT draws straight connectors . If you prefer, you can make ADOIT draw right-angled connectors . For details on how to adapt your personal settings, please refer to the section Modelling .

Connector not Visible if One Object Contains the Other

Objects can be placed on top of each other so that one object contains the other. If such objects are linked with a connector, it is automatically hidden when you drop one object inside the other.

children.title: Create Relations Using Drag-and-Drop Operations in the Graphical Editor
children.summary: Relations can be created by dragging models or objects from the Explorer to the graphical editor or nesting objects within the editor, with ADOIT suggesting valid relations based on the Application Library used.
children.content:
In the graphical editor, there are multiple ways to create relations by drag and drop. The following functions are available:
• Drag Model/Object from Explorer to Graphical Editor: Drag the model or object you want to reference from the Explorer to the desired object on the drawing area. A blue border will appear around the target object. When you release the mouse button, ADOIT will show you which relations are possible and let you decide which one to create.
• Nest Objects within Graphical Editor: Within the graphical editor, drag one object onto another. The objects may overlap, or be completely contained. A blue border will appear around the target object. When you release the mouse button, ADOIT will show you which relations can be created in this way. Simply choose the desired relation and it will be created.

This method can be used with existing objects, when you create new objects and when you copy and paste objects in the graphical editor.

note

Depending on the Application Library, different relations may be created by nesting objects. If you are using the ArchiMate Application Library, you can create all relations that are possible between the two objects.

children.title: Reuse Objects
children.summary: Repository objects can be reused in active models by dragging them from the Object Catalogue onto the drawing area, with existing connectors automatically drawn if applicable.
children.content:
In order to re-use a single (repository) object from the Object Catalogue in the active model, proceed as follows:
• Drag the object you want to re-use from the Object Catalogue to an empty space on the drawing area (multiple selection is possible).

note

If you re-use an object which contains relations to other objects in the active model, the corresponding connectors will be automatically drawn.

children.title: Differentiation between Repository Objects and Modelling Objects
children.summary: ADOIT differentiates repository objects, which can be reused across models and are stored in the Object Catalogue, from modelling objects, which exist only within their creating model and cannot be reused.
children.content:
ADOIT distinguishes between repository objects and modelling objects. Repository objects are created and maintained in the Object Catalogue or in models. They can be reused in different models. Modelling objects, by contrast, are maintained only in the models in which they are created. They are not contained in the Object Catalogue.

Repository objects can be reused. Modelling objects cannot be reused.

children.title: Move Objects in the Graphical Editor
children.summary: Objects in the graphical editor can be moved individually or in groups by drag-and-drop, and their layering adjusted via right-click options Move to front or Move to back.
children.content:
You can move objects individually or collectively in the graphical editor:

Move Object
• Move a single object by drag and drop.

Move Multiple Objects
• Hold the left mouse button and drag a (red) frame around the objects.
• Move the objects to their new position by drag and drop.

Move Object to the Front or Back
• Right-click the object, and then click Move to front or Move to back.

children.title: Select Container Object
children.summary: Container objects cannot be selected by single click; instead, click and hold until highlighted or click the container's header to select.
children.content:
Due to practical reasons, you cannot select container objects (e.g. a Swimlane) with a single click. You have two options:
• Click and hold the container object until it turns red or:
• Click the header of the container object.

children.title: Edit Models
children.summary: This section provides an overview of functions for editing models in the graphical editor.
children.content: The following sections provide an overview of the functions needed for editing models in the graphical editor.

children.title: Open Model
children.summary: Models can be opened by double-clicking in the Model Catalogue or by right-clicking and choosing to open in graphical editor (Model) or tabular editor (Table) for attribute editing.
children.content:
In order to open a model:
• Double-click the model in the Model Catalogue.

The model opens in the graphical editor.

In order to open a model with specific settings, proceed as follows:
• Select the model you want to open in the Model Catalogue.
• Right-click the model, point to Open, and then click either Model or Table.

The graphical editor ("Model") lets you design, modify and update models. The tabular editor ("Table") is ideal for the large-scale editing of attributes.

children.title: Search in Model
children.summary: Describes how to search for objects by name in the graphical editor using the 'Search in model' feature, including executing searches, moving focus between results, and closing the search box.
children.content:
You can search for objects in the graphical editor.

Execute Search

In order to execute a search in the active model:
• Click the More button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click Search in model .
• Enter the search string into the input field.

As you type, ADOIT will start highlighting objects that contain the search string in their name. The first search result will be focused.

Move Focus to the Next Search Result

In order to move the focus to the next search result:
• Press < Enter > or click the Search icon ().

Close Search Box

In order to close the search box:
• Click the icon .

children.title: Cut/Copy/Paste/Delete Objects in the Graphical Editor
children.summary: Explains keyboard shortcuts for Cut (Ctrl+X), Copy (Ctrl+C), Paste (Ctrl+V), Delete (Del), and Delete including Object Catalogue removal (Shift+Del) for objects in the graphical editor.
children.content:
The manipulation functions Cut, Copy, Paste and Delete are available in the graphical editor:
• Press < Ctrl > + < X > to cut an object.
• Press < Ctrl > + < C > to copy an object.
• Press < Ctrl > + < V > to paste an object.
• Press < Del > to remove an object from the model.
• Press < Shift > + < Del > to remove an object from the model and the Object Catalogue.

children.title: Special Case: Insert Object between Two Connected Objects
children.summary: Details the special function to insert an object between two connected objects by clicking the connector, which ADOIT then splits and reconnects automatically.
children.content:
Often it is necessary to insert an object between two connected objects. For this purpose, the graphical editor contains a function that automatically connects the new object to the model structure:
• Click the connector in question when placing the object. When positioned correctly, the connector is highlighted.

ADOIT splits the connector up automatically and connects the new object to the neighbouring objects.

children.title: Special Case: Delete Object with Incoming and Outgoing Connectors of One Type
children.summary: Describes the auto heal function that, when deleting an object with exactly one incoming and one outgoing connector of the same type, automatically reconnects the preceding and following objects; applicable to multiple objects as well.
children.content:
When you delete an object that has exactly one incoming and one outgoing connector of one type, a connector is drawn from the preceding object to the following object (auto heal function).

The auto heal function can also be applied to multiple objects at once. When deleting a set of two or more objects with exactly one incoming and one outgoing connector of one type and connectors of the same type running through the set, a connector from the previous to the following object is drawn.

children.title: Connector Functions
children.summary: Introduces an overview of connector editing functions in ADOIT graphical editor.
children.content: The following sections provide an overview of the functions needed for editing connectors.

children.title: Model Bendpoints
children.summary: Explains how to create connectors with multiple bendpoints by clicking on free spaces while drawing the connector.
children.content:
Connectors can be modelled with any number of bendpoints. In order to do this, proceed as follows:
• When drawing a connector, click consecutively on all free spaces of the drawing area where you want the connector to bend.

children.title: Create New Bendpoint
children.summary: Describes creating a new bendpoint by clicking on a connector and dragging it to a new position; not available if rectangular connectors are enabled.
children.content:
• Click on the connector at any free spot.
• Drag it into a new position.

note

If rectangular connectors are enabled, this function is not available.

children.title: Move Bendpoint
children.summary: Explains moving an existing bendpoint by clicking and dragging it; unavailable when rectangular connectors are enabled.
children.content:
• Click on the bendpoint.
• Drag it into a new position.

note

If rectangular connectors are enabled, this function is not available.

children.title: Delete Bendpoint
children.summary: Details deleting a bendpoint by dragging it to straighten adjacent lines or selecting it and pressing Del; not available with rectangular connectors enabled.
children.content:
• Drag the bendpoint to a place where the two adjacent connector lines form a straight line. As soon as the mouse button is released, the bendpoint is deleted.
• As an alternative, select only the bendpoint and press < Del >.

note

If rectangular connectors are enabled, this function is not available.

children.title: Merge Multiple Bendpoints
children.summary: Describes merging two bendpoints by dragging one over the other; function disabled if rectangular connectors are enabled.
children.content:
• Drag one of two bendpoints over the other.

note

If rectangular connectors are enabled, this function is not available.

children.title: Parallel Translation of Connectors
children.summary: Explains how to move straight connectors or individual segments of rectangular connectors horizontally or vertically by selecting and drag-and-drop.
children.content:
Horizontally or vertically drawn straight connectors can be moved as a whole:
• Select the connector.
• Move it in parallel by drag and drop.

You can also move individual segments of rectangular connectors in this manner.

children.title: Reallocate Connector
children.summary: Describes reallocating a connector's connection point by dragging it to a new object.
children.content:
• Select the connection point.
• Drag it to the new object.

children.title: Delete Connector
children.summary: Explains deleting connectors by selecting them (avoiding bendpoints) and pressing Del or using the context menu's Delete option.
children.content:
Unnecessary connectors can be easily deleted.
• Select the connector (click an area of the connector edge without a bendpoint) and press < Del >.
• As an alternative, from the context menu of the connector, select Delete.

children.title: Align Objects
children.summary: Details automatic alignment options for selected objects or all objects within a container, including vertical, horizontal, distribution, and edge alignments accessible via right-click Align menu.
children.content:
ADOIT allows you to automatically align objects in the graphical editor. In order to do so:
1. Select the objects you want to align.
2. Right-click the objects, point to Align, and then select an alignment option.

Additionally, you can align all objects within a container object (e.g. a Swimlane).
• Right-click the container object, point to Align, and then select an alignment option.

Alignment Options

The following alignment options are available:
• Align middle: Align the objects vertically
• Align center: Align the objects horizontally
• Distribute horizontally: Evenly distribute the objects horizontally
• Distribute vertically: Evenly distribute the objects vertically
• Align right: Align the right side of the objects with the right edge of the right-most object
• Align left: Align the left side of the objects with the left edge of the left-most object
• Align top: Align the top side of the selected objects with the top edge of the top-most object
• Align bottom: Align the bottom side of the selected objects with the bottom edge of the bottom-most object

children.title: Change Modelling Direction: Vertical/Horizontal
children.summary: Describes changing the modelling direction between vertical (top to bottom) and horizontal (left to right) in the graphical editor, including how it affects object placement and the Hover Modelling Assistant.
children.content:
The modelling direction can be set to horizontal (modelling is done from left to right) or vertical (modelling is done from top to bottom).

note

The default modelling direction for each model type is defined in the ADOIT Administration.

You can change the modelling direction for a specific model in the graphical editor. The objects on the drawing area are automatically rearranged.

The following options are available:

Change Direction: Vertical

To place the objects in the model from top to bottom instead of from left to right:
• Click the More button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click Change direction: vertical.

Change Direction: Horizontal

To place the objects in the model from left to right instead of from top to bottom:
• Click the More button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click Change direction: horizontal.

note

When using the Hover Modelling Assistant, the modelling direction determines where the next object is placed:
• Horizontal: To the right of the selected object
• Vertical: Below the selected object

children.title: Check Spelling
children.summary: Explains ADOIT's spell checking feature in text fields using browser-native capabilities, marking misspellings with wavy lines and allowing correction via right-click suggestions.
children.content:
ADOIT can look for and correct misspelled words in text fields. Spell checking is available, for example, when editing text attributes, in search boxes, during translation etc. Misspelled words are marked with a wavy line.

In order to correct a misspelling:
• Right-click the misspelled word, and then replace it with a suggested word from the list.

This feature uses native spell checking capabilities provided by the browser. Spell checking is available in Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome and Safari.

note

You can configure your browser to support multiple languages if desired. To find out how to install additional languages, please refer to the browser documentation.

children.title: Add/Remove Empty Space
children.summary: Describes adding or removing empty horizontal or vertical space between objects in the graphical editor by dragging bold grid lines after activating the Add/Remove empty space mode.
children.content:
In the graphical editor, you can add or remove any size of empty space between objects. In order to do so:
1. Click the Add/Remove empty space button at the top of the modelling bar (1).
2. Click the desired location of the drawing area (= where you want to add or remove space).

Now do one of the following:
• Insert Horizontal Empty Space: Drag the bold vertical line (2) to the right (→). When you release the mouse button, all objects that were located to the right of the original position will be moved further to the right.
• Insert Vertical Empty Space: Drag the bold horizontal line (3) down (↓). When you release the mouse button, all objects that were located below the original position will be moved further down.
• Remove Horizontal Empty Space: Drag the bold vertical line to the left (←). A dashed line indicates the border of the area that can be removed (4). When you release the mouse button, all objects that were located to the right of the original position will be moved further to the left.
• Remove Vertical Empty Space: Drag the bold horizontal line up (↑). A dashed line indicates the border of the area that can be removed. When you release the mouse button, all objects that were located below the original position will be moved further up.

children.title: Update All Relations
children.summary: Explains how to update all relations (connectors) in a model or selected objects to remove outdated connectors and redraw new ones via menu options in the graphical editor.
children.content:
In the graphical editor, relations between repository objects are often represented as connectors. When you open the properties of an object and modify these relations, the model may contain incorrect or outdated information.

To update relations:
1. Open the model in the graphical editor.
2. Do one of the following:
• To update all relations in the model, click the More button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click All objects: update all relations.
• To update relations of specific objects, right-click the objects, and then click Selected objects: update all relations.

Outdated connectors are removed and new connectors are drawn.

children.title: Work with the AI Assistant
children.summary: Introduces the AI Assistant chat feature for natural language interaction with ADOIT, including searching, retrieving, and creating repository data; requires Enterprise Edition and admin configuration.
children.content:
The AI Assistant provides a chat for interacting with ADOIT. You can ask questions in natural language, search and retrieve repository information, and discuss enterprise architecture and ArchiMate concepts.

note

The AI Assistant can find and analyse existing repository data. It can also create objects with a name and description and create relations between objects. Other changes to repository data must be made using the corresponding ADOIT components.

To use the AI Assistant, you must have access to the ADOIT Enterprise Edition and your ADOIT administrator must enable it and configure an AI provider.

The AI Assistant is limited to actions provided by your configured MCP tools. It cannot perform operations that are not defined there. See Preconfigured Tools for the current set of supported tools.

children.title: Open the AI Assistant
children.summary: Describes how to open the AI Assistant globally from scenario start pages or contextually within a model via the AI Assistant button, showing chat history and current conversation.
children.content:
You can open the AI Assistant from the Design & Document and Read & Explore scenario start pages, or from within a model.

Open the global chat

To open the AI Assistant independently of a specific model:
• On the Design & Document or Read & Explore scenario start page, click AI Assistant in the bottom right corner.

The AI Assistant opens in a chat dialog. The chat history is available in the left-side panel, while the current conversation is displayed on the right.

Open the model-context chat

To open the AI Assistant in the context of a specific model:
1. Open the model in the graphical editor or the tabular editor.
2. Click the AI Assistant button .

The AI Assistant opens on the right side of the program window, in the context of the current model.

children.title: Use the AI Assistant
children.summary: Explains conversational use of the AI Assistant for repository queries, ArchiMate knowledge, metadata, and practical support, including managing chats, copying content, and viewing MCP tool usage.
children.content:
You can interact with the AI conversationally.
1. Type your own questions freely:
• Use the free text field at the bottom (Ask any question).
• Ask in natural language, just like you would speak to a colleague.
2. Let the AI Assistant help you, for example in the following areas:
• Repository Data & Search: Search the repository for models and objects, browse saved searches, retrieve model and object details, and create objects and relations between objects.
• Enterprise Architecture Knowledge: Explain ArchiMate concepts, modelling approaches, architecture principles, governance, and best practices.
• Repository Metadata: List available object types, model types, and repository languages.
• Practical Support: Help interpret models, answer questions about your architecture landscape, and provide links to open the properties of models and objects.
3. Make use of what the AI tells you:
• Execute found saved searches and view the results directly in the chat.
• Open the properties of found models and objects using the provided links and edit their attributes.
• If the AI suggests improvements, you can apply them if you have write access, or leave a comment for the responsible colleagues.

Additional Options

The following additional options are available when using the AI Assistant:
• New chat: Start a new discussion in the global chat.
• Remove chat: Hover over a chat and select Delete chat in the global chat.
• Clear Chat: Deletes all messages in the model-context chat.
• Copy content: Copies text to your clipboard. Use Copy response at the end of an AI message, or hover over your own message and select Copy prompt.
• Show MCP usage: Shows or hides information about the MCP tools used to generate each AI response. The displayed information includes the number and names of the tools used. For an overview of the MCP tools available in ADOIT, see Preconfigured Tools in the Administration Help.

children.title: Chat History
children.summary: Details chat history management in the AI Assistant, including limits on number of global chats (10) and conversation context (25 requests), with no history in model-context chat.
children.content:
The global chat keeps a history of your conversations. You can access previous chats from the chat history in the left-side panel.

You can have up to 10 chats in the global chat history. When this limit is reached and a new chat is created, the chat that has not been used for the longest time is removed.

The model-context chat provides one chat for the current model, but does not maintain a chat history.

note

Chat history and conversation context are subject to different limits. Within a chat, a maximum of 25 requests is retained as conversation context. When you send the 26th request, the oldest request is removed from the context.

children.title: Working with Navigation and View Tools
children.summary: Introduces navigation and view tools for moving through models and controlling model display in ADOIT.
children.content: The navigation and view tools let you navigate through models, analyses etc. and control how you see your models.

children.title: Navigate through Open Models, Analyses etc.
children.summary: Explains navigating recently viewed models or analyses using forward/back arrows or the Opened views button showing tiles of recent items.
children.content:
In order to navigate through models, analyses etc. you recently viewed:
• Click the < and > arrows at the top right corner of the program window. The previous or next model is brought to the foreground. The models are ordered according to the sequence in which they were opened.
• Click the Opened views button at the top right corner of the program window. Any models you recently viewed are displayed as tiles. By clicking a tile, you can bring the selected model to the foreground.

children.title: Switch between Components in the Right-side Pane
children.summary: Describes switching or opening components in the right-side pane by selecting from a list or switching via the pane's upper-left icon.
children.content:
The right-side pane in ADOIT can hold various components like the colouring options or validation functions. To open or switch between components in the right-side pane:
• When the right-side pane is empty, a list of available components is displayed. From the list, choose the component you want to open.
• When the right-side pane already shows a component, you can switch to a different component. Click the icon in the upper-left corner of the pane, and then select the component you want to switch to.

children.title: Toggle Editor
children.summary: Explains toggling between the graphical editor ('Model') and tabular editor ('Table') for designing models or bulk editing properties via menu bar buttons.
children.content:
In order to open the active model in another editor:
• Click the Model or Table button in the menu bar of the model.

The graphical editor ("Model") lets you design, modify and update models. The tabular editor ("Table") is ideal for the large-scale editing of properties.

children.title: View Object Tooltips
children.summary: Describes viewing object tooltips showing Name and Description when having read access by hovering over objects; tooltip properties configurable in administration.
children.content:
Object tooltips are small windows that display information such as the Name and the Description of an object. They are displayed when you only have read access to a model.

To view an object tooltip:
• Position the mouse pointer over the object in the graphical editor.

note

The properties which should be considered when viewing object tooltips can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.

children.title: Make Objects Coloured and Create Heat Maps
children.summary: Details creating heat maps by colouring objects based on attribute values, including enabling colouring, selecting element and attribute, setting colour ranges for enumerations, numbers, or dates, and saving models to share heatmaps.
children.content:
You can make objects in the graphical editor coloured depending on the value of an attribute to highlight some aspects of your data. This is a great way to create conditional formatting heat maps. For example, Capabilities could be coloured red if there is a need for action, and gray if there is no need for action.

To start colouring:
• Click the More button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click Colour .

The colouring options appear at the right side of the program window. You can use these options to determine what the objects should look like in the model:
• Enable Colouring: Click the Enable colouring button to enable colouring. All other options in this panel are inactive unless you click this button.
• Select Element: Choose the object type you want to colour.
• Select Attribute: Choose the attribute whose value determines how the objects will be coloured. If the attribute is an enumeration, you will immediately see the colour assignment to the values of the attribute. If the attribute represents a number or a date, you have to set values for colouring first (see below).
• Reverse Colours: To invert the colour scheme, click the Reverse colours button .
• Change Colours: To change colours, click the colour circles.
• + Add Colouring: Click the + Add Colouring button to create an additional colouring rule for a different object type. When clicked, a new set of controls appears below the current set. You can add as many colouring rules as there are different object types. This allows you to colour multiple object types either according to the same attribute (if they share that attribute), or according to different attributes.

Set Values for Colouring

The initial colour assignment to the values of the attribute will differ depending on the data type of the selected attribute.
• Enumeration: If the selected attribute is an enumeration (= a predefined set of values you can choose from), then you don't need to do anything. Each value is automatically assigned a colour by ADOIT.
• Number: For attributes that store integers or floating point numbers, you can define up to 5 different value ranges and assign them to a colour. Define the value range in the From and To fields. A colour will be preselected for each value range. You can add or remove value ranges by clicking the "+" and "x" icons.
• Date: For attributes that store a date, you can define up to 5 different time periods and assign them to a colour. Define the period in the From and Until fields. You can either enter the start date and the end date manually or select them in the calendar. A colour will be preselected for each time period. You can add or remove time periods by clicking the "+" and "x" icons.

note

After colouring, save the model so that other users can see the heatmap.

When a model is opened and colouring is enabled, the colouring options will appear automatically. The heatmap legend is exported along with the graphical representation of the model when printing the model to PDF or exporting the model as a graphic file.

children.title: Display Formatted Annotations in Models
children.summary: Explains adding formatted annotations using Notes in models by placing a Note object, editing text with formatting options, and resizing to display content.
children.content:
