• When a technology is decommissioned
• When a technology replaces another

children.title: Access (Matrix)
children.summary: Access (Matrix) details a matrix chart visualization showing how Application Components interact with Business Objects using icons for read, write, master, and violation access rights.
children.content:
A changed visualisation is available for matrix charts based on the following templates:
• "Read-Write Matrix"

This visualisation shows how applications (Application Components) can act upon Business Objects. The following icons are used:

Read-Write Matrix
• Read: Application can read a business object
• Write: Application can write a business object
• Master: Application is considered as master of a business object
• Violation: Application can write data without being the master of a business object

children.title: Save Analysis
children.summary: Save Analysis explains saving analyses (data and charts) to the Model Catalogue with options to save changes or save as a new analysis with naming and target group settings, noting read-only analyses only allow Save as.
children.content:
You can save an analysis (= specific data and selected charts) to view it again later and share it with other users. Analyses are stored in the Model Catalogue.

The following options are available:

Save

To save changes to an analysis:
1. Click the Save button in the menu bar of the analysis.
2. Enter a name for the analysis and define a target group if you are saving it for the first time.

Save as

To create a copy of the analysis with a new name:
1. Click the down arrow symbol in the Save button .
2. Select Save as from the drop-down menu.
3. Change the name of the analysis.
4. Define the target group for the new analysis.
5. Click OK.

note

If an analysis only allows read access, the Save button is replaced by the Save as button in the menu bar of the analysis.

children.title: Close Analysis
children.summary: Close Analysis instructs closing an open analysis by clicking the close icon at the top right corner.
children.content:
To close an analysis:
• Click the icon at the top right corner of the open analysis.

children.title: Find Analysis
children.summary: Find Analysis provides tips to locate analyses via the Model Catalogue Explorer or the Analyses page in the Design & Document scenario, using browsing or search.
children.content:
Here are some tips to find an analysis in ADOIT:
• Model Catalogue: Analyses are stored in the Model Catalogue in the Explorer. You can browse the folders or use the search to find the analysis you're looking for.
• Analyse : In the "Design & Document" scenario, on the Analyses page, all analyses are shown in a compact list.

children.title: Delete Analysis
children.summary: Delete Analysis explains deleting an analysis by right-clicking it in the Model Catalogue and selecting Delete.
children.content:
To delete an analysis:
• Right-click the analysis in the Model Catalogue, and then click Delete.

children.title: Configurable Dashboards
children.summary: Configurable Dashboards introduces personalized dashboards as digital workspaces combining key information and metrics from various sources, allowing creation, sharing, and searching of dashboards with customizable widgets.
children.content:
With configurable dashboards, you can set up your own personalised digital workspace that brings together key information and metrics relevant to your role. A configurable dashboard serves as a central hub, combining data from different business processes and systems and presenting it in an intuitive, actionable format.

You can view dashboards your colleagues have set up, finding them quickly using the integrated search. Or create your own from scratch, choosing widgets from the widget library and arranging them freely to highlight what matters most, tailoring your workspace to your specific needs and priorities.

children.title: The Dashboards Page
children.summary: The Dashboards Page describes accessing and managing dashboards from a central page listing all dashboards as tiles sorted by last change date, with options to create new dashboards or open existing ones.
children.content:
The Dashboards page is your starting point for accessing and managing dashboards. Here, all dashboards that have been created are listed, and you can also create new dashboards from scratch.

Open Dashboards Page

To open the Dashboards page:
• At the top left of the screen, select Dashboards.

Create New Dashboard

See Create and Configure Dashboard.

Open a Dashboard

All dashboards are shown as tiles and sorted by date of last change.
• To open a dashboard, click it.

children.title: Create and Configure Dashboard
children.summary: Create and Configure Dashboard guides creating dashboards by naming them, adding and configuring widgets from the library (standard and pre-built), repositioning/resizing widgets, and saving, with notes on multilingual text fields and query limitations.
children.content:
It's easy to create your own dashboards. Here is what you need to do:
1. Open the Dashboards page.
2. Set up the new dashboard:
• Click Create Dashboard, enter a meaningful name, and then click Create. The new dashboard opens.
3. Add and configure widgets to visualise data:
• Click + Add widget to open the widget library on the right. It contains two tabs: Standard and Pre-built.
• Drag widgets to the dashboard and click Configure to edit the settings:
• Standard
• Configure Bar Chart
• Configure Gauge Chart
• Configure Pie Chart
• Configure Table
• Configure Text
• Configure Image
• Configure Number
• Model viewer
• Pre-built
• Use News
• Use All Application Components
• Use All Business Processes
• Use All System Software
• Use All Capabilities
• Use My Objects
4. Reposition and resize widgets as needed:
• Use the drag handle on the top left to move a widget to a new position.
• Use the handle on the bottom right to adjust the widget size.
5. Save your dashboard when finished:
• Click Save

note

For all widgets, text fields such as Title or Description can optionally be translated into all languages ADOIT supports. Click Translate next to the field and enter the translations.

note

When you configure a widget that visualises data from a saved query created using the search function (new search experience) in ADOIT, only elements from the first level are used and visualised. Queries that include transitive searches with nested filters are supported; however, related elements are not considered. This also applies if Detailed results is enabled in the search, as dashboards always use the top-level results.

children.title: Configure Bar Chart
children.summary: Configure Bar Chart explains setting up a bar chart widget by defining title, description, dataset query, grouping property, bar size calculation (count or aggregation), colours, legend, layout, label position, and sorting, with an example using Business fitness.
children.content:
The Bar Chart widget represents data as bars, allowing you to compare values across categories at a glance. The length of each bar is determined by the underlying dataset and the selected aggregation method.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the chart displays.
• Query* : Select a query to define the dataset for the widget. You can choose between:
• Saved queries: Queries created using the search function in ADOIT. These include private queries you created and public queries.
• Built-in queries: Predefined queries provided by ADOIT that represent commonly used views on models and objects.

The selected query determines which elements are included in the dataset.
• Group by* : Select the property that defines the bars in the chart. You can only choose enumeration attributes or relations that are displayed as columns in the search result.
• Bar size: Defines how the length of each bar is calculated. You have two main options:
• Number of results (default): Each bar shows the number of entries in that group.
• Aggregation: Select a numeric attribute from the search result for the Value. Bars still represent the groups (e.g., responsible persons), but their lengths now correspond to the aggregated attribute value. Choose the aggregation method Sum, Average, Min, or Max.
• Set colours: Choose colours for the bars. You can select them from the colour circles or enter hex values (e.g. #d62fd6).
• Show legend: Toggle to show or hide the chart legend.
• Chart layout: Choose whether to display the bars vertically or horizontally.
• Position of labels: If a horizontal layout is selected, choose whether labels appear inside or outside the bars.
• Sort by: Define how bars are sorted. Possible values are Default, Name (ascending), Name (descending), Value (ascending), and Value (descending).

Example: Visualise Business Fitness

For example, you can create a bar chart based on a saved query for System Software that includes the Business fitness attribute as a column in the search result. When you select Business fitness under Group by and Number of results under Bar size, the bars represent each fitness value (e.g., "Bad", "Good"), and their lengths show how many System Software elements fall under this classificiation.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the bar chart to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Gauge Chart
children.summary: Configure Gauge Chart describes configuring a gauge chart widget to display a single value or aggregated metric from a query or single artefact, selecting attributes, aggregation methods, colours, and providing an example visualizing Strategic importance.
children.content:
The Gauge Chart widget represents data as a single value displayed on a dial, helping you to quickly assess a key metric or status at a glance. It can be used either to display the value of a single artefact or to aggregate values across multiple artefacts of the same type.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the gauge chart displays.
• Data source selection* : Select how the value of the gauge chart is determined. You can choose between:
• Query (default): The gauge chart is based on a saved or built-in query and aggregates values across all artefacts returned by the query.
• Artefact: The gauge chart is based on a single artefact selected manually.

Depending on the selected data source, different configuration options are available:
• Options for Query:
• Query* : Select a saved or built-in query.
• Value* : Select the attribute whose values are used for the gauge calculation. You can select an enumeration attribute or a numeric attribute.
• Aggregation* : Define how the values of the artefacts returned by the query are aggregated. Possible values are Average and Median.
• Set colours: Define the colour of the gauge, for example by entering a hex value such as #109D59.
• Options for Artefact:
• Artefact* : Select a single model or object. Selecting multiple artefacts is not supported.
• Attribute* : Select an enumeration attribute or a numeric attribute whose value should be displayed on the gauge.
• Set colours: Define the colour of the gauge.

Example: Visualise Application Type (Artefact Selection)

For example, if you select the Application Component "Air Traffic Control 3.1" as the artefact and the attribute Strategic importance, the gauge will display the corresponding value, such as Low, High, or Very high.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the gauge chart to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Pie Chart
children.summary: The Pie Chart widget visualizes data as proportional slices representing categories or numerical intervals, configurable by title, description, query (saved or built-in), grouping property, and slice size calculation (number of results or aggregation), with options for colors and sorting.
children.content:
The Pie Chart widget represents data as proportional slices of a circle, allowing you to compare values as parts of a whole. Each slice represents either a category or a numerical interval, and its size reflects the number of entries or an aggregated value.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the chart displays.
• Query* : Select a query to define the dataset for the widget. You can choose between:
• Saved queries: Queries created using the search function in ADOIT. These include private queries you created and public queries.
• Built-in queries: Predefined queries provided by ADOIT that represent commonly used views on models and objects.

The selected query determines which elements are included in the dataset.
• Group by* : Select the property that defines the slices of the pie. You can choose between:
• Enumeration attributes or relations that are displayed as columns in the search result.
• Numeric attributes that are displayed as columns in the search result. When a numeric attribute is selected, the pie chart groups values into numerical intervals instead of categories.

Depending on which property you select under Group by, different configuration options are available:
• Options for enumeration attributes or relations:
• Value: Defines how the size of each slice is calculated. You have two main options:
• Number of results (default): Each slice represents the number of entries in that group.
• Aggregation: Select a numeric attribute from the search result for the Value. The size of each slice corresponds to the aggregated attribute value. Choose the aggregation method Sum, Average, Min, or Max.
• Set colours: Choose colours for the slices. You can select them from the colour circles or enter hex values (e.g. #5cb85c).
• Sort by: Define how slices are ordered. Possible values are Default, Name (ascending), Name (descending), Value (ascending), and Value (descending).
• Options for numeric attributes:
• Label numerical intervals: This section allows you to define how numeric values are grouped into intervals and displayed as pie slices:
• By default, two intervals are defined. You can add additional intervals by clicking + Add interval.
• Each interval consists of a Colour, a Label, and a numeric boundary:
• The first (upper) interval defines an upper boundary using Up to, defining the slice that contains elements with values up to the specified limit.
• The last (lower) interval defines a lower boundary using From, defining the slice that contains elements with values greater than or equal to the specified limit.
• Any additional intervals added between the first and last use Up to to define their upper boundary.

Example: Visualise Responsible Business Actors (Relation)

For example, you can create a pie chart based on a saved query for Business Processes that includes the Responsible business actors relation as a column in the search result. When you select Responsible business actors under Group by and Number of results under Value, each slice of the pie represents a responsible business actor, and its size shows how many business processes each business actor is responsible for.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the pie chart to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Table
children.summary: The Table widget displays query results in rows and columns, showing detailed information about models or objects, configurable by title, description, and query selection (saved or built-in).
children.content:
The Table widget displays data in a structured, tabular format. Each row represents a model or object returned by a query, and each column corresponds to a property included in that search result.

This widget is ideal for showing detailed information at a glance, such as lists of risks, processes, or applications with key attributes like owner, status, or value.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the table displays.
• Query* : Select a query to define the dataset for the widget. You can choose between:
• Saved queries: Queries created using the search function in ADOIT. These include private queries you created and public queries.
• Built-in queries: Predefined queries provided by ADOIT that represent commonly used views on models and objects.

The selected query determines which elements are included in the dataset.

Example: Display a List of Capabilities

For example, you can create a table widget based on a saved query for Capabilities that includes the Business fitness, Process fitness, and Technological fitness properties as columns. Each row in the table represents a single capability, while the columns show the corresponding values, allowing you to compare and review information at a glance.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the table to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Text
children.summary: The Text widget displays formatted arbitrary text on dashboards for notes or explanations, configurable by title, description, and text content with formatting options.
children.content:
The Text widget allows you to display arbitrary text on your dashboard. It is useful for notes, instructions, or additional explanations related to other dashboard widgets.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the text represents or its purpose.
• Text* : Enter the text content to be displayed. You can apply formatting and change the font family, font size, text colour, or make the text bold, italic, etc.

Example: Explain a Chart Widget

You can use a text widget to provide context or explanation for a nearby chart. For instance, place a text widget next to a pie chart showing the distribution of process responsibilities, and enter a short note describing how to interpret the chart slices, what each category represents, or key insights users should notice.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the text widget to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Image
children.summary: The Image widget allows uploading and displaying images on dashboards, useful for logos or illustrations, configurable by title, description, and image selection or drag-and-drop upload.
children.content:
The Image widget allows you to display an image on your dashboard. This is useful for logos, illustrations, or any visual content that supports the context of other dashboard widgets.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of the image’s purpose or context.
• Image* : Click + Choose and select the image you want to upload. You can also drag a file from your computer to the Drag and drop files here to upload area.

Example: Display a Logo

For instance, you can add your company logo as an image widget at the top of your dashboard to provide branding.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the image to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Number
children.summary: The Number widget highlights a single numeric value from a query, configurable by title, description, query (saved or built-in), value type (number of results or aggregation), and display color.
children.content:
The Number widget highlights a single numeric value on your dashboard. It is ideal for displaying key figures such as the number of processes, applications, or risks matching a query.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the widget displays.
• Query* : Select a query to define the dataset for the widget. You can choose between:
• Saved queries: Queries created using the search function in ADOIT. These include private queries you created and public queries.
• Built-in queries: Predefined queries provided by ADOIT that represent commonly used views on models and objects.

The selected query determines which elements are included in the dataset.
• Value: Defines what the widget displays. You have two main options:
• Number of results (default): The widget shows the total number of search results.
• Aggregation: Choose a numeric attribute from the search result to display an aggregated value (for example, the total or average cost). Choose the aggregation method Sum, Average, Min, or Max.
• Set colours: Define the colour in which the number is displayed. You can enter a hex value (e.g. #007bff).

Example: Show the Total Number of Draft Application Components

For example, you can create a number widget based on a saved query for Application Components. The widget then displays the total number of application components. To make it visually stand out, you can set the number colour to green (#5cb85c).

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the number widget to the dashboard.

children.title: Configure Model Viewer
children.summary: The Model Viewer widget embeds a selected model directly on the dashboard for quick access and navigation, configurable by title, description, and model selection.
children.content:
The Model Viewer widget displays a model directly on your dashboard, allowing you to quickly access and navigate important models without leaving your personalised workspace.

After adding the widget, configure it using the following options (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the widget displays.
• Model* : Click Select model and choose the model that you want to display in the widget.

Example: Display an Application Landscape

For example, you can select a capability map which serves as a framework for your organisation's digitalisation efforts. Users can view and navigate the model without first opening it from the repository.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings and add the model viewer to the dashboard.

children.title: Use News
children.summary: The News widget shows recent changes in models and objects in a tabular view, configurable by title, description, filters for changes since last login, model types, and object types.
children.content:
The News widget provides a detailed overview of the most recent changes in models and objects in the database in a tabular view. It helps you stay informed about created, updated, or released content.

After adding the widget, you can tailor it to your needs. Configuration-wise, the following options are avilable (mandatory fields are marked with * ):
• Title* : Enter a title for the widget.
• Description: Provide a short explanation of what the news widget displays.
• Show only changes since last login: Enable this option to display only changes that occurred since your last login.
• Filter model types: Expand this section to restrict the displayed news to specific model types. Select one or more model types.
• Filter object types: Expand this section to restrict the displayed news to specific object types. Select one or more object types.

Example: Display a List of Objects

For example, you can create a news widget that shows information about objects in the repository. Select the object types you want to monitor under Filter Object Types. Each row in the table represents a single object, while the columns show the date of the change, and the type of action performed.

Once you have configured all options, click Save to apply your settings.

children.title: Use Overview Widgets
children.summary: Overview widgets provide predefined, role-based insights with limited configuration, offering fast access to relevant information based on predefined data sets.
children.content:
ADOIT provides several overview widgets that are pre-built to deliver role-based, user-specific insights.

Overview widgets are based on predefined data sets. While their configuration options are limited, they provide a fast and consistent way to access information that is directly relevant to your roles and responsibilities.

children.title: All Application Components
children.summary: The All Application Components widget lists all Application Components with default properties like responsible actors, fitness metrics, confidentiality, and lifecycle state; only title and description are configurable.
children.content:
The All Application Components widget provides a detailed overview of all Application Components in the database. It shows the current value of the following properties by default, with additional properties displayable as columns:
• Responsible business actors
• Strategic importance
• Business fitness
• Technology fitness
• Cost fitness
• Business continuity fitness
• Security fitness
• Confidentiality
• Lifecycle state

Configuration-wise, only the Title and Description of the widget can be adapted.

children.title: All Business Processes
children.summary: The All Business Processes widget lists all Business Processes with default properties such as responsible actors, strategic importance, cost efficiency, and compliance; only title and description are configurable.
children.content:
The All Business Processes widget provides a detailed overview of all Business Processes in the database. It shows the current value of the following properties by default, with additional properties displayable as columns:
• Responsible business actors
• Strategic importance
• Cost efficiency
• Cycle time
• Quality
• Customer satisfaction
• IT support
• Compliance

Configuration-wise, only the Title and Description of the widget can be adapted.

children.title: All System Software
children.summary: The All System Software widget lists all System Software elements with default properties including responsible actors, specialization, fitness metrics, and standards lifecycle; only title and description are configurable.
children.content:
The All System Software widget provides a detailed overview of all System Software elements in the database. It shows the current value of the following properties by default, with additional properties displayable as columns:
• Responsible business actors
• Specialisation
• Business fitness
• Technology fitness
• Standards lifecycle

Configuration-wise, only the Title and Description of the widget can be adapted.

children.title: All Capabilities
children.summary: The All Capabilities widget lists all Capabilities with default properties like responsible actors and various fitness metrics; only title and description are configurable.
children.content:
The All Capabilities widget provides a detailed overview of all Capabilities in the database. It shows the current value of the following properties by default, with additional properties displayable as columns:
• Responsible business actors
• Business fitness
• Process fitness
• Information fitness
• Technological fitness
• Cost fitness

Configuration-wise, only the Title and Description of the widget can be adapted.

children.title: My Objects
children.summary: The My Objects widget shows repository objects where the user is assigned as Responsible business actor, with configurable title, description, and object type filters.
children.content:
The My Objects widget provides a focused overview of all repository objects for which you are assigned as Responsible business actor (property in the chapter "Organisation").

Configuration-wise, you can only adapt the Title and Description of the widget and restrict the displayed object types under Filter object types (default: all).

children.title: Use Built-in Queries
children.summary: Widgets based on search queries can use built-in queries, which are predefined data sets offering common views on models and objects, available in the Query selector for dashboards.
children.content:
In addition to saved queries from the search function in ADOIT, widgets based on a search query (for example, Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Table, or Number) can also be configured using built-in queries.

Built-in queries are predefined data sets that provide commonly used views on models and objects. They are available in the Query selector when configuring a widget.

The following built-in queries are available for configurable dashboards:
• All Application Components
• All Business Processes
• All Capabilities
• All System Software

children.title: Manage Dashboards
children.summary: Configurable dashboards support editing, deletion, sharing, and other management actions.
children.content: Configurable dashboards can be edited, deleted, shared, and more.

children.title: Refresh Dashboard
children.summary: Dashboards and individual widgets can be refreshed to display the latest data via the More menu's Refresh option.
children.content:
To update a dashboard so that all widgets display the latest data:
• Click More at the top right of the dashboard, then select Refresh.

Instead of refreshing the entire dashboard, you can also refresh an individual widget:
• At the top right of the widget, click More, and then select Refresh.

children.title: Edit Dashboard
children.summary: Dashboards can be edited by entering edit mode to rename, add, reposition, resize, configure, or delete widgets, with changes saved upon completion.
children.content:
To edit an existing dashboard:
• On the Dashboards Page: Click More on the dashboard tile, and then select Configure. This opens the dashboard in edit mode.
• Within an Open Dashboard: Click Configure at the top left of the dashboard to enable edit mode.

Once in edit mode, the following options are available:
• Rename Dashboard: Click the pencil icon next to the dashboard name to edit it.
• Configure Widgets:
• Add, Reposition, and Resize Widgets: Drag widgets from the widget library onto the dashboard, move them using the drag handle at the top left, and resize using the handle at the bottom right.
• Edit Widget: At the top right of the widget, click More, and then select Configure to modify the widget configuration.

note

See Create and Configure Dashboard for more information on configuring widgets.
• Delete Widget: At the top right of the widget, click More, and then select Delete to remove it from the dashboard.

After making your changes, click Save to update the dashboard.

children.title: Clone Dashboard
children.summary: Dashboards can be cloned to create copies named 'Copy of <dashboard name>' as starting points for new dashboards.
children.content:
You can create a copy of an existing dashboard and use it as a starting point for a new one:
• On the Dashboards Page: Click More on the dashboard tile, and then select Clone.

A new dashboard named Copy of < dashboard name > is created.

children.title: Delete Dashboard
children.summary: Dashboards can be deleted from the Dashboards page or within an open dashboard via the More menu's Delete option.
children.content:
To remove a dashboard that is no longer needed:
• On the Dashboards Page: Click More on the dashboard tile, and then select Delete.
• Within an Open Dashboard: Click More at the top right of the dashboard, then select Delete.

children.title: Manage Favourites for Dashboards
children.summary: Dashboards can be marked or unmarked as favourites from the Dashboards page or within an open dashboard.
children.content:
To add or remove dashboards as favourites:
• On the Dashboards Page: Click More on the dashboard tile, and then select Mark as favourite or Remove from favourites.
• Within an Open Dashboard: Click Mark as favourite or Remove from favourites next to the dashboard name.

children.title: Share Dashboard
children.summary: Dashboards can be shared by generating a URL, which can be emailed to users or copied for distribution, with options to add recipients and personal messages.
children.content:
You can generate a URL for a dashboard. This way you can e.g. easily share it with your colleagues via email.

To generate a URL:
• On the Dashboards Page: Click More on the dashboard tile, and then select Share.
• Within an Open Dashboard: Click More at the top right of the dashboard, then select Share.

Now do one of the following:
• Share the URL by email. In the Add people box, start typing the username or email address of a user, and then select the one you want when you see it. If the recipient is not a user or has no email address associated, you need to enter the full email address. Add additional recipients as needed. In the Include a message box, you can add a personal message if you want. When you are done, click Share and the message will be sent.
• Paste the URL wherever you need it. Click Copy to directly copy the URL to the clipboard, or copy the URL manually from the Copy link box.

children.title: Filter Dashboards
children.summary: Dashboards can be filtered on the Dashboards page by All, Created by me, or Favourites to narrow displayed dashboards.
children.content:
You can filter the dashboards shown on the Dashboards page by selecting an option at the top of the page:
• All (default): Shows all dashboards.
• Created by me: Shows only dashboards you created.
• Favourites: Shows only your favourite dashboards.

children.title: Find Dashboards
children.summary: Dashboards can be searched by typing text in the Search box to find dashboards with matching names.
children.content:
To find a dashboard on the Dashboards page:
• In the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.

All dashboards that contain the search string in their name are shown.

children.title: Manage Save Location & Permissions
children.summary: Dashboards are repository objects stored in personal folders by default, can be moved to other object groups, and have permissions managed by administrators at group or individual levels.
children.content:
Dashboards are repository objects and can be managed like other objects in ADOIT:
• New dashboards are stored in your personal objects folder (Personal Objects\<username>\Dashboards).
• Dashboards can be moved to a different object group to change their storage location.
• ADOIT administrators can assign permissions at the object group or individual dashboard level to control who can view or edit dashboards.

children.title: View Widget Data
children.summary: Users can explore and interact with widget data, with available actions depending on widget type.
children.content: You can explore and interact with the data displayed in widgets. The available actions depend on the widget type.

children.title: View Models
children.summary: The Model Viewer widget supports zoom controls, opening the model in the graphical editor, and exporting the displayed model as an image.
children.content:
The Model viewer widget lets you you view and navigate models directly from the dashboard:
• Use Increase zoom, Decrease zoom or Fit model to window size to adjust the zoom level.
• At the top right of the widget, click More, and then:
• Select Open to open the model in the graphical editor.
• Select Export > Export image to export the displayed model as an image (see Graphic Options).

children.title: Open Saved Query
children.summary: Widgets based on saved queries allow opening the underlying query for viewing or modification if the user is the creator.
children.content:
For widgets that are based on a saved query (for example, Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Table, or Number), you can open the underlying query to see or refine the dataset:
• At the top right of the widget, click More, and then select Open saved query.

The related saved query opens in a new window, allowing you to view the saved query and, if you are its creator, modify it.

children.title: Open Properties
children.summary: Widgets based on model or object data allow opening the properties of the related artefact in a new window.
children.content:
For widgets based on model or object data (for example, Gauge Chart), you can open the properties of the related artefact.
• At the top right of the widget, click More, and then select Open.

The properties of the artefact open in a new window.

children.title: Interact with Charts
children.summary: Charts are interactive: Bar Charts and Pie Charts allow clicking elements to open tabular views of underlying data, with Pie Charts also supporting toggling slices via the legend.
children.content:
Charts are interactive, allowing you to explore underlying data directly from the dashboard.
• Bar Charts: Click a bar to open a tabular view showing all elements in that category.
• Pie Charts: Click a slice to open a tabular view showing all elements in that category. You can also click a name in the legend to toggle a slice on or off, removing or re-adding it in the chart view.

children.title: Search, Filter, and Configure Table Columns
children.summary: Table and News widgets provide filtering by column with various operators, search functionality, column visibility selection, and grouping entries by model or object type.
children.content:
Widgets that display data in a table, such as the Table and News widgets, provide several tools that help you find, filter, and organise data more efficiently.

Use Table Filters

You can narrow down the displayed rows in widgets that present their data in a table by using column filters.
1. Click the filter icon in a column header to start building your filter.
2. Depending on the type of data in the column, select the available filter options (for example, whether all rules or any rules must be fulfilled).
3. To build a rule, choose an operator such as Starts with, Contains, or Equals. Then enter or select the value to filter for.
4. Optionally, click Add rule to include additional filter conditions.
5. Click Apply to confirm your filter settings.

The available filter options depend on the type of data shown in a column, for example text, selectable values, or dates. The filter dialog adapts accordingly.

Search

To search a table:
• In the Search... box, type the text you want to search for.

As you type, the table is filtered to show only rows where the search term appears.

Show or Hide Columns

To change which columns are displayed in a table:
• At the top right of the widget, click More, select Select columns..., and then choose the columns you want.

Group Table Entries by Type

To group the listed elements in a table by model or object type:
• At the top right of the widget, click More, and then select Group by type.

children.title: Reporting Board
children.summary: The Reporting Board enables creation of various reports from a central dashboard.
children.content: The Reporting Board allows you to create different reports from one central dashboard.

children.title: Open Reporting Board
children.summary: The Reporting Board is accessed via the Analyse menu by selecting Reports, opening the Explorer view.
children.content:
To open the Reporting Board:
• On the toolbar at the top of the screen, click Analyse , and then select Reports.

The Reporting Board opens and the Explorer is displayed.

children.title: Create Reports
children.summary: Reports are created by selecting models or objects, choosing a report type, configuring options, and confirming; alternatively, items can be dragged from the Explorer to reports on the Reporting Board.
children.content:
To create a report:
1. Click the report you want to create.
2. Select the models or objects you want to create a report on, and then click OK.
3. Select the desired report options , and then click OK.

Select Models/Objects in Explorer

Alternatively, you can create reports with the Explorer as the starting point:
1. Select the models/objects you want to create a report on in the Explorer.
2. Drag the items to the appropriate report on the Reporting Board.

children.title: Collaboration and Sharing
children.summary: This manual section covers collaboration and sharing features including comments, publishing, translation, and sharing or embedding models.
children.content:
In this part of the manual, the following topics are outlined:
• Comments: Comments allow ADOIT users to leave feedback and suggestions that can help improve models and objects.
• Publishing: This chapter provides an overview of the most important publication functions of ADOIT.
• Translation: This chapter provides an overview of functions for translating models and objects in the database.
• Share or Embed Models: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for sharing models with other users or embedding models into other applications.

children.title: Comments
children.summary: Comments enable users to leave feedback and suggestions on models and objects, supporting threaded discussions.
children.content: Comments allow ADOIT users to leave feedback and suggestions that can help improve models and objects. As other users respond and a discussion unfolds, you will be able to see the entire conversation, with the original message at the top and replies below it.

children.title: View Comments
children.summary: Comments can be viewed via the Comments button in model or object views, with comment bubbles indicating comment counts on objects in the graphical editor.
children.content:
To view comments on a model or object:
• Open the model, or open the properties of the object.
• Click the Comments button in the menu bar.

The Comments pane opens. You can use it to both read comments by your colleagues and create your own comments on models and objects.

When a model is open in the graphical editor, a bubble will appear next to each object in the model. The number in the bubble shows how many comments an object has . Objects with no comments display a bubble with a plus icon inside . You can add a comment by clicking on a bubble.

children.title: Add a Comment
children.summary: Comments can be added in the Comments pane or directly in the graphical editor using comment bubbles, supporting mentions with email notifications and text formatting.
children.content:
Add a Comment to a repository object or a model as a whole in the Comments pane. Or add a comment to a specific modelling object directly in the graphical editor.

To add a comment:

In the Comments Pane
1. Click the New Comment button .
2. If you add a comment to a model, choose what you want to comment on. From the Choose element list that opens, select the model itself, or an object in the model.
3. In the Add a comment box, type your comment. Use @ to mention someone, and they will receive an email notification. To format text, select the text and you can make it bold, italic, etc. When you are done, click the Send button or press < Enter >.

In the Graphical Editor
1. Click the comment bubble next to the object you want to comment on.
2. In the Add a comment box, type your comment. Use @ to mention someone, and they will receive an email notification. To format text, select the text and you can make it bold, italic, etc. When you are done, click the Send button or press < Enter >.

note

Before ADOIT can send emails, the email settings must be set correctly in the ADOIT Administration and users must have an email address associated with their account.

children.title: Leave a Reply
children.summary: Replies to comments can be added in the Comments pane or graphical editor by expanding conversations and typing in the reply box.
children.content:
In the Comments pane, you can find all comments on a model or object. You can expand a conversation to see any replies. Also, you can directly access the comments for a specific modelling object in the graphical editor using the comment bubbles.

To leave a reply:

In the Comments Pane
1. Click a conversation to expand or collapse it.
2. Type your comment in the Leave a reply box to respond.

In the Graphical Editor
1. Click the comment bubble next to an object to view all conversations.
2. Click a conversation to expand or collapse it.
3. Type your comment in the Leave a reply box to respond.

children.title: Edit or Delete Comments
children.summary: Users can edit or delete their own comments and delete entire conversations via the More menu on comments or conversations, subject to permissions.
children.content:
You can edit or delete your own comments.

Edit Comment

To edit a comment:
• Double-click the comment or:
• Click the More button at the top right corner of the comment, and then click Edit.

Delete Comment

To delete a comment:
• Click the More button at the top right corner of the comment, and then click Delete.

Delete Conversation

To delete the entire conversation (the comment and any replies to it):
• Click the More button at the top right corner of the conversation, and then click Delete.

note

For detailed information on who can edit or delete comments, see Permissions and Notifications.

children.title: Open and Resolved Comments
children.summary: Comments can be resolved to move them to a Resolved catalogue without deletion, with options to switch views, resolve, or reopen conversations.
children.content:
You can resolve a comment when a discussion is finished. The entire conversation will move to the Resolved catalogue in the Comments pane, but will not be deleted.

Switch between Open and Resolved Comments

To switch between open and resolved comments:
• Click the Open or Resolved button at the top of the Comments pane.

note

When a model is open in the graphical editor, the bubbles in the model are updated as you switch. Depending on the selected catalogue, the bubbles will show the number of open or resolved comments . Speech bubbles with a plus sign are displayed only when open comments are selected.

Resolve Comment

To resolve a comment:
• Click the More button at the top right corner of the conversation, and then click Resolve.

Reopen comment

To reopen a conversation:
• Click the More button at the top right corner of the conversation, and then click Reopen.

children.title: Show or Hide Comments in Model
children.summary: Comment bubbles in the graphical editor can be shown or hidden via a toggle button in the Comments pane.
children.content:
You can hide the bubbles in the graphical editor, and show them again at any time:
• In the Comments pane, click the Show comments in model button.

children.title: Show or Hide Comments Pane
children.summary: The Comments pane can be hidden or shown to adjust workspace using icons at the pane's top left.
children.content:
You can hide the Comments pane to increase your workspace, and show it again at any time:
• To hide the pane, click the icon at the top left corner of the widget.
• To show the pane again, click the icon .

children.title: Permissions and Notifications
children.summary: Comment permissions allow users to edit/delete their own comments, anyone to resolve/reopen comments, and responsible users to delete comments; email notifications are sent for mentions, comments on responsible objects, replies, and status changes.
children.content:
Who can modify my comments? Will I receive an email when someone responds to my comment? Read on for the details.

Permissions

The following permissions apply to comments:
• You can edit or delete your own comments.
• Anyone can resolve or reopen a comment.
• Additionally, if you are responsible for an object, you can delete comments.

Notifications

You will receive email notifications in the following situations:
• If someone uses @ to mention you directly.
• If you are responsible for an object or model, and someone writes a comment on it.
• If you are part of a conversation, and someone posts a new reply.
• If you are part of a conversation, and someone resolves or reopens the comment.

Who is Responsible for an Object or Model?

Someone is responsible for an object or model if they are assigned as:
• Accountable business actors
• Responsible business actors

These properties can be found in the chapter "Organisation".

children.title: Publishing
children.summary: This chapter outlines key publication functions available in ADOIT.
children.content: This chapter provides an overview of the most important publication functions of ADOIT.

children.title: Create Report
children.summary: Reports in PDF or RTF formats can be created from selected models or objects via context menus or widgets, with options configurable before generation; note limitations with PNG images of 8-bit depth.
children.content:
You can create various PDF and RTF reports based on models or objects. These reports e.g. provide an overview of the values of certain attributes across all the selected elements.

In order to create a report:
1. Select the models/objects you want to create a report on.
2. Right-click the selection, point to Reports, and then choose the desired report from the submenu. The settings dialogue opens.
3. Select the desired report options.
4. Confirm with OK.

note

You can create reports this way using e.g. the Explorer or the graphical editor as a starting point. Additionally, it is possible to create reports from various widgets and dashboards by clicking the appropriate icon.

note

Different kinds of reports are available depending on your Application Library and product configuration.

caution

PDF reports for models cannot be generated if PNG images with an 8-bit bit depth are used, whether within the models you want to create a report on or as a corporate logo.

children.title: Report Options
children.summary: Report options in ADOIT include selecting document type (PDF or RTF), page layout with headers/footers, corporate identity schemes for logos and company data, image layout for model graphics sizing, and content filters to control visible properties and hide empty attributes.
children.content:
The following report options are available:

Document type (1)

Select the file format for generating the report. You can choose between PDF (default format for quality printing) and RTF (cross-platform document interchange format).

Page layout (2)

Page layouts determine the appearance of the header and footer in the report. These layouts can contain logos, text, meta information like the username and printing timestamp and much more.

Corporate identity (3)

If several corporate identity schemes (CI schemes) are available, you can select one of them for creating the report. A CI scheme consists of a company logo and company data. Depending on the page layout, the CI scheme will be displayed on the title page and in the header and footer.

note

In the user settings, you can specify which CI scheme is set as the default. CI schemes can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.

Image layout (4)

Modify the size and orientation (portrait or landscape) of model graphics in the report:
• Fit on one page: The model is enlarged or reduced to fit exactly on one page.
• Apply settings from model: Apply print settings from the model to determine the size and orientation of model graphics. For this purpose, the settings have to be saved for specific models.

This option is only available when creating a standard report for models.

Content filter

The options in this area affect the content of the report.
• Property filter (5): Here you can change the active property filter. The property filter influences which properties are visible in the report.
• Hide empty attributes (6): Activate Hide empty attributes to hide all properties with no value in the report. You can combine this filter with any property filter.

note

For information on which attributes are considered "empty", please refer to the section Display or Hide Empty Properties.

children.title: Available Reports
children.summary: Available reports include the Standard Report, which provides overviews of selected models or objects with properties, graphics, and contained objects, with availability depending on the Application Library, e.g., ArchiMate.
children.content:
The following reports are available:

Standard Report

This report provides an overview of the selected models or objects:
• For Models: The report includes the properties of the models, the model graphics, and the objects contained within the models. The objects are sorted according to their type.
• For Objects: The report lists the selected objects grouped by type. It displays all properties that contain data; alternatively, you can choose to include empty properties in the report.

note

Available reports depend on the Application Library. The configuration described here applies to the ArchiMate Application Library.

children.title: HTML Publication
children.summary: HTML Publication enables distribution of ADOIT modelling content as static HTML files viewable in browsers without ADOIT access, featuring simplified UI with catalogues, graphical viewer, properties, and search.
children.content:
HTML publishing allows you to distribute modelling content to users with no access to ADOIT. Models and objects are provided as static HTML files which can be opened in a web browser. The user interface of the HTML publication is a simplified version of ADOIT complete with Model and Object Catalogues, a graphical model viewer, properties and a search function.

You can e.g. send a generated HTML publication to your colleagues via email or make it available on a web server for people to view.

children.title: Create HTML Publication
children.summary: To create an HTML publication, select models/objects or groups, define scope options like including referenced or subordinated models/objects, choose languages, and confirm to generate and download the publication.
children.content:
In order to create an HTML publication:
1. Right-click a model or object, point to Reports, and then click HTML Publishing.
2. In the Models and Object areas, select individual models, objects or entire groups that should to be included in the HTML publication.
3. Select the scope of the HTML publication:
• Select the Including referenced models check box to include all models referenced by the selected models and objects.
• Select the Include subordinated model groups check box to include the entire hierarchy below a selected group into the export – not only the selected hierarchy level.
• Select the Including referenced objects check box to include all objects referenced by the selected models and objects.
• Select the Include subordinated object groups check box to include the entire hierarchy below a selected group into the export – not only the selected hierarchy level.
4. Select the languages in which the modelling content should be available.
5. Click OK.

The HTML publication is being generated. The download will start automatically.

children.title: View HTML Publication
children.summary: To view an HTML publication, extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the index.html file in a web browser to display the content.
children.content:
In order to view an HTML publication:
1. Extract the downloaded .zip file into a folder of your choice.
2. Navigate to the folder where you extracted the HTML publication, and then open the file index.html in a web browser.

The HTML publication is displayed.

children.title: Open Model
children.summary: Open a model in the HTML publication by double-clicking it in the Model Catalogue, which opens it in the graphical model viewer.
children.content:
In order to open a model included in the HTML publication:
• Double-click the model in the Model Catalogue.

The model opens in the graphical model viewer.

children.title: Open Properties
children.summary: Open properties in the HTML publication by right-clicking a model and selecting Open Properties or by double-clicking an object to view its properties.
children.content:
You can open the properties of models and objects included in the HTML publication.

Open Model Properties

In order to open the properties of a model included in the HTML publication:
• Right-click the model, and then click Open Properties.

Open Object Properties

In order to open the properties of an object included in the HTML publication:
• Double-click the object.

children.title: Open Referenced Document
children.summary: Referenced documents in HTML publications can be opened via the Representation object's properties by clicking the referenced document link, requiring Base URL configuration and user login to ADOIT.
children.content:
In order to open a referenced document in the HTML publication:
1. Open the properties of the Representation object which contains the referenced document.
2. In the chapter General, click the link to the document in the attribute Referenced representation. ADOIT opens in a new tab.
3. Log in to ADOIT. The properties of the Representation object open.
4. Click the link to the document in the attribute Referenced representation.

The document is downloaded.

note

This feature is only available if the Base URL is configured in the ADOIT Administration.

note

The object type for documents depends on the Application Library and product configuration. By default, imported files are Representations in the ArchiMate Application Library.

children.title: Search
children.summary: Search in HTML publications by entering text in the Search tab; extended search allows filtering by models or objects and restricting by types to refine results.
children.content:
In order to search for models or objects in the HTML publication:
1. Click the Search tab to start the search.
2. In the Search box, type your search text, and then press < Enter >.

All models and objects containing the search term in their Name or Description are displayed.

Extended Search

In order to refine your search:
• Select the Extended Search check box.
• Now do one of the following:
• From the Search In list, select to display either Models or Objects only.
• From the Restrict Search to list, select either All Model/Object Types or restrict the search to certain types.
• Press < Enter > to refresh the search results.

children.title: Save Image
children.summary: Export an open model as a PNG graphic file in the HTML publication by right-clicking the model and selecting Save Image.
children.content:
It's possible to export an open model as a graphic file (in PNG format) in the HTML publication. In order to do so:
• Right-click the model, and then click Save Image.

children.title: Generate URL
children.summary: Generate a URL for an open model in the HTML publication by right-clicking the model and selecting Generate URL.
children.content:
It's possible to generate a URL based on an open model in the HTML publication. In order to do so:
• Right-click the model, and then click Generate URL.

children.title: Pending Actions
children.summary: The Pending Actions overview tracks report generation status, listing queued or processing reports, accessible via the Pending actions button, with options to cancel reports.
children.content:
The pending actions overview allows you to track the state of the reports you are currently generating (including HTML publications). It lists all reports that are queued (Pending...) or being generated (Processing...). When a report is completed, it will be downloaded automatically.

Open Pending Actions

In order to open the pending actions overview:
• Click the Pending actions button at the top right corner of the program window.

Cancel Report

In order to cancel a report:
• Click the Cancel button .

note

The total number of reports currently being generated is displayed within the Pending actions button.

children.title: Print Model to PDF
children.summary: Models can be printed to PDF from the graphical editor by using the Export menu, selecting Print PDF, configuring print settings, and confirming the print.
children.content:
Models in the graphical editor can be printed as a PDF document. You can save this document on your computer, share it with colleagues or print it on paper.

To print a model to PDF:
1. Click the Export button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click Print PDF. The print dialogue opens.
2. Select the desired print settings.
3. Confirm with Print.

children.title: Print Settings
children.summary: Print settings include preview with page selection, paper size, print templates (Standard or Model Report), page layout for headers/footers, corporate identity schemes, orientation, scaling options, and image quality (dpi).
children.content:
The following print settings are available:

Preview (1)

The left part of the dialogue box contains a print preview. This preview corresponds to the settings on the right part of the dialogue box.
• Page selection: To omit particular pages during printing, click them in the preview window. They will be highlighted and omitted during printing. You can un-mark pages by clicking them again.

note

In the user settings, you can specify whether the page breaks and page numbers displayed here in the preview are also visible in the graphical editor.

Paper size (2)

The setting Paper size determines whether the document shall be printed in A0, A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, B4, B5 or C5 format.

note

Additional paper sizes can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.

Print Template (3)

Print templates allow you to control the layout and content of the PDF document when printing a model. If you are using the ArchiMate Application Library, you can choose between the following options:
• Standard: A minimalistic layout that emphasizes the model image.
• Model Report (PDF): A layout based on the standard report for models (see Available Reports for details).

When selecting a print template, you can configure the page layout (4) separately.

Page layout (4)

Page layouts supplement the selected print template (3) and determine the appearance of the header and footer. These layouts can contain logos, text, meta information like the username and printing timestamp and much more.

Corporate identity (5)

Select a corporate identity scheme (CI scheme) to display in the PDF document. This makes it possible to embed company logos and display corporate data. If you are using a page layout without header and footer, the CI scheme will not be visible.

note

In the user settings, you can specify which CI scheme is set as the default. CI schemes can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.

Orientation (6)

The setting Orientation determines whether the document shall be printed in Portrait or Landscape orientation.

Size (7)

Models need not always be printed in a standard size, but can be scaled to meet your needs when printed. The following sizing options are available:
• Factor: The model is printed with a defined zoom factor, ranging from 1% to 400%. Default: 100% (the original size).
• Fit onto page: The model is scaled to exactly fill one printing page. The necessary zoom factor is calculated automatically.
• No. pages / height: The model is scaled to fill the printing pages determined in height. Factor and width in pages are calculated automatically.
• No. pages / width: The model is scaled to fill the printing pages determined in width. Factor and height in pages are calculated automatically.

Image quality (8)

The setting Image quality determines whether the document shall be printed at 72, 150 or 300 dpi.

children.title: Save Model-Specific Print Settings
children.summary: Model-specific print settings can be saved by applying settings in the print dialog, confirming print or cancel, and then saving the model.
children.content:
You can save the print settings that you defined for a specific model. In order to do so:
1. In the print settings dialog box, click the Apply button.
2. Click either the Print or Cancel button.
3. Click the Save button in the menu bar of the model.

children.title: Generate Image
children.summary: Models can be exported as graphic files via Export image, with options to select graphic settings and optionally crop the image using Ctrl+Shift+drag.
children.content:
Models in the graphical editor can be exported as graphic files. You can use these graphical model views in other applications than ADOIT (e.g. in a word processor).

In order to generate a graphic:
1. Click the Export button in the menu bar of the open model, and then click Export image. The settings dialogue opens.
2. Select the desired graphic options.
3. Confirm with Export image.

Optionally you can also:
• Crop the image. Press and hold < Ctrl >, < Shift > and the left mouse button and drag a frame around the part of the model which shall appear in the graphic file.

children.title: Graphic Options
children.summary: Graphic options include preview with display detail, image format selection (PNG, JPEG, SVG), scale factor (1%-400%), and image quality (72, 150, or 300 dpi).
children.content:
The following graphic options are available:

Preview

The left part of the dialogue contains a preview.
• Display Detail: The part of the model which shall appear in the graphic file is visualised by a coloured border (by default the whole model).

Image format

Select the image format for generating images. You can choose between PNG (lossless, bigger size pixel-based image format), JPEG (lossy, smaller size pixel-based image format), and SVG (vector-based image format).

Scale

The graphic is generated with a defined zoom factor, ranging from 1% to 400%. Default: 100% (the original size). After selecting a factor, the expected graphic size (in mm) is calculated and displayed.

Image quality

The setting Image quality determines whether the graphic shall be generated at 72, 150 or 300 dpi.

children.title: Translation
children.summary: Overview of translation functions for models, objects, and groups in ADOIT.
children.content: The following sections provide an overview of functions for translating models, objects and groups.

children.title: Start Translation
children.summary: Start translation by selecting models, objects, or groups and using context menu options to open the translation editor for models, objects, or group names.
children.content:
Depending on what needs to be translated, the translation process is started in different ways.

Translate Models and Objects

You can translate specific models and objects, or you can translate entire groups and all the models and objects in them. In order to do so:
• Select the items you want to translate.
• Now do one of the following:
• To translate specific models and objects, right-click the selection, point to More, and then click Translate .
• To translate entire groups, right-click the selection, point to More, point to Translate, and then click Translate models or Translate objects .

The translation editor opens.

Translate Names of Groups

In order to translate the names of groups:
• In the Explorer, select the model groups or object groups you want to translate.
• Right-click the selection, point to More, point to Translate, and then click Translate groups .

The translation editor opens.

children.title: Structure of the Translation Editor
children.summary: The translation editor features a hierarchical item selection tree, an attribute selection table highlighting untranslated attributes, and a content translation widget with text or rich text editing for efficient translation.
children.content:
The translation editor is a specialised tabular editor, designed for translating models, objects and groups quickly and efficiently or for updating existing translations.

The translation editor is structured as follows:

Item Selection Widget (1)

The elements selected for translation are displayed as a hierarchical tree structure.
• Model Translation: Models including their objects and relations are displayed.
• Object Translation: Objects including their relations are displayed.
• Group Translation: Groups are displayed.

note

Only outgoing relations (icon ) that have properties are displayed in the translation editor.

Elements that contain attributes which have to be translated are highlighted. This facilitates recognising necessary translations.

Select an element from the tree to browse its attributes in the Attribute Selection Widget (2).

Attribute Selection Widget (2)

All attributes of the currently selected element which are relevant for translation are displayed in a table structure.
• Every row of this table represents a single chapter from the properties or an attribute.
• The first table column contains the name of the element.
• The second column contains the text in the Primary Language (as defined in the Application Library) by default.
• The third column contains the text in another language.
• Table entries which are highlighted and marked by an indicator icon () have to be translated: The content in this cell has either not yet been translated or it is older than the text in the Primary Language.
• If a cell has to be translated, the name in the first column of the row as well as the parent chapter are highlighted too. This facilitates recognising necessary translations.

Select an attribute from the table to translate it in the Content Translation Widget (3).

note

The Primary Language is the language which is defined as the main language in the Application Library.

Content Translation Widget (3)

The actual translation of the selected attribute takes place in this widget. For single-line text attributes the new value can be entered into a text field. For translating multi-line attributes rich text editing support is available.

children.title: Translate Content
children.summary: Translate content by selecting elements and attributes in the translation editor, entering translations, saving changes, and optionally attaching language-specific links or documents.
children.content:
To translate content in the translation editor:
1. Select an element from the tree view to browse its attributes.
2. Select an attribute from the table to translate it.
3. Enter the translation in the appropriate text field.
4. Confirm by clicking the Save button in the menu bar of the translation editor.

Besides translating text, you can also:
• Set up language specific links.
• Make documents available in different language versions. In order to so, click the Attach file icon .

note

Once you have edited a highlighted entry, it is marked as translated (= not highlighted anymore). This also applies to its parent elements unless they still contain other children which have to be translated.

children.title: Select Languages for Translation
children.summary: Select languages displayed in the translation editor by clicking the language button in a column header and choosing from the dropdown, facilitating translation between multiple languages.
children.content:
In order to select which languages are displayed in the translation editor:
• Click the button in the header of the column of which you want to change the language.
• Select the desired language from the drop-down list.

note

This function is especially useful when three or more languages are in use. It allows you to translate between any two of them.

children.title: Navigation Shortcuts
children.summary: Navigation shortcuts in the translation editor include toggling tree and attributes view, expanding/collapsing nodes, navigating tree/attributes, filtering untranslated elements, and saving translations with specified key combinations.
children.content:
Content in the tree can be shown or hidden by clicking the “+” and “-“ icons next to the elements. The following additional options are available:
• Switch between Tree and Attributes: Press < Ctrl > + < Enter >.
• Expand/Collapse Selected Node: Press < Ctrl > + < Shift > + < Alt > + < Left Arrow/Right Arrow >.
• Navigate in Tree/Attributes: Press < Ctrl > + < Shift > + < Alt > + < Up Arrow/Down Arrow >.
• Filter Translated Elements: Press < Ctrl > + F.
• Save Translation: Press < Ctrl > + S.

note

Click the Displays available keyboard shortcuts button in the menu bar of the translation editor to open an overview of all available keyboard shortcuts of the translation editor.

children.title: Get Write Access
children.summary: To gain write access to locked elements (marked with a lock icon) in the translation editor, select the element and click the provided link to attempt acquiring write access.
children.content:
Elements only allowing read access are marked by a small lock icon (). This is e.g. the case if they are currently being edited by another user when you start the translation. In order to try to get write access to these elements later:
• Select the locked element from the tree view. Instead of the attributes of the selected element an information message is displayed.
• Click the highlighted link to try to get write access.

children.title: Filter Translated Elements
children.summary: Filter the translation editor to show only elements needing translation by toggling the filter button, hiding already translated elements.
children.content:
In order to only display elements that need to be translated in the translation editor:
• Click the Shows only elements which need to be translated button in the menu bar of the translation editor.

As long as the filter is active, elements which are marked as translated are not shown in the translation editor.

children.title: Show/Hide Relations
children.summary: Show or hide relations in the translation editor using the toggle button; hiding relations removes them from view.
children.content:
In order to show or hide relations in the translation editor:
• Click the Shows/hides relations button in the menu bar of the translation editor.

As long as the filter is active, relations are not shown in the translation editor.

children.title: Automatically Translate Content
children.summary: Automatically translate content by clicking the translation icon in the content translation widget and confirming the proposed translation, subject to ADOIT configuration.
children.content:
In order to automatically translate elements:
• Click the icon in the menu bar of the content translation widget. A dialogue window with a translation proposal opens.
• Confirm with OK to accept the proposal.

note

The availability of this function depends on the configuration of your ADOIT installation.

children.title: Reset Translation
children.summary: Reset translations for specific models or objects or for all objects in a model via the More menu in the translation editor, restoring fallback values.
children.content:
You can reset translations of models and objects, meaning the fallback value will be shown again. The following options are available:

Reset Translation of Model or Object

To reset the translation of a specific model or object:
1. Select an element from the tree view.
2. Click the More button in the menu bar of the translation editor, and then click Reset ' < language > ' values.

Reset Translations for All Objects in a Model

To reset translations for all objects in a model:
1. Select a model from the tree view.
2. Click the More button in the menu bar of the translation editor, and then click Reset ' < language > ' values for all objects in the model.

children.title: Multiple Languages and Fallback Behaviour
children.summary: Multiple languages use fallback rules where set values apply per language, missing values fall back to the Primary Language, and if missing there, to another language's value; the Primary Language is defined in the Application Library.
children.content:
The following rules apply:
• Rule 1: If a value has been set in a particular language, this value always applies to that language.
• Rule 2: If a value has NOT been set in a particular language, the value in the Primary Language applies.
• Rule 3: If a value has NOT been set in a particular language, and the value has NOT been set in the Primary Language, a value set in another language applies.

note

The Primary Language is the language which is defined as the main language in the Application Library.

The fallback behaviour is best explained with an example:

Example: Fallback Behaviour

Consider that multiple languages are in use: English, German and French. French is the Primary Language.
• Create a model "Kundenbetreuung" in German. The model is called:
• German: "Kundenbetreuung" (see Rule 1)
• French: "Kundenbetreuung" (see Rule 3)
• English: "Kundenbetreuung" (see Rule 3)
• Next, translate the name of the model to "Service Clients" in French. The model is now called:
• German: "Kundenbetreuung" (see Rule 1)
• French: "Service Clients" (see Rule 1)
• English: "Service Clients" (see Rule 2)
• Next, translate the name of the model to "Customer Service" in English. The model is now called:
• German: "Kundenbetreuung" (see Rule 1)
• French: "Service Clients" (see Rule 1)
• English: "Customer Service" (see Rule 1)

children.title: Share or Embed Models
children.summary: Overview of key functions for sharing models with users or embedding models into other applications.
children.content: This chapter provides an overview of the most important functions for sharing models with other users or embedding models into other applications.

children.title: Share Models, Objects and Analyses
children.summary: Generate and share URLs for models, objects, and analyses via email or copy, with options for latest version linking and access control depending on login status; special URLs can directly open application scenarios.
children.content:
You can generate a URL based on models, objects and analyses. This way you can e.g. easily share an analysis with your colleagues via email or add a specific model to your browser's bookmarks.

To generate a URL:
1. Open the model or analysis, or open the properties of the object.
2. Click the Share button .
3. Optional: The Link opens latest version option is only available for objects in a release workflow. Select this option to ensure the generated URL will automatically direct to the latest released version - regardless of which version you are currently viewing. Clear this option if you want to share an older version.
4. Now do one of the following:
• Share the URL by email. In the Add people box, start typing the username or email address of a user, and then select the one you want when you see it. If the recipient is not a user or has no email address associated, you need to enter the full email address. Add additional recipients as needed. In the Include a message box, you can add a personal message if you want. When you are done, click Share and the message will be sent.
• Paste the URL wherever you need it. Click Copy to directly copy the URL to the clipboard, or copy the URL manually from the Copy link box.

note

Before ADOIT can send emails, the email settings must be set correctly in the ADOIT Administration.

Who Can Access These URLs?

If a user uses the Organisation Portal anonymously (= without supplying user credentials) and generates a URL, anyone can access the content. Otherwise, accessing the URL requires a login to ADOIT.

Language

The generated URL contains the current language as a parameter. When the URL is accessed, the content is opened in the same language the URL was created in.

Example

You are working in English and have generated a URL for a model. The generated URL automatically points to the model in English.
