Special Case: Generate URL for Application Scenario

When you open a URL for an application scenario, you will skip the ADOIT start page and go directly to the selected scenario. In order to generate such a URL:
• "Design & Document": Add "?scenarioID=ait_scenario_1 _ design_and_document" to the URL at which ADOIT is available.
• "Control & Release": Add "?scenarioID=ait_scenario_3 _ control_and_release" to the URL at which ADOIT is available.
• "Read & Explore": Add "?scenarioID=ait_scenario_4 _ explore_and_contribute" to the URL at which ADOIT is available.

Example

ADOIT is available at the URL http://server:8000/ADOIT21_0. You want to create a URL to directly access the "Design & Document" scenario.

The URL should look like this:

ht ﻿ tp://server:8000/ADOIT21_0?scenarioID=ait_scenario_1 _ design_and_document

children.title: Embed ADOIT as an iFrame
children.summary: Embed ADOIT or specific models in websites using HTML iFrames with customizable size and URL parameters like language; embedding requires configuring security.src.frame-ancestors in adoxx_web.properties and restarting Tomcat.
children.content:
The HTML element iFrame allows you to embed ADOIT in a website. This may include e.g. a blog or the website of your organisation. Embedding ADOIT in another web application is also possible.

Embed ADOIT in a Website
• Insert the URL at which ADOIT is available into the following HTML code:

<iframe src="URL" width="800" height="800"/>
• Insert the code into the web page where you want ADOIT to appear. Adjust the width (width) and height (height) to fit the dimensions of your website.

Embed a Specific Model in a Website
• Generate a URL which references the model which you want to embed in your website.
• Insert the model URL into the following HTML code:

<iframe src="MODEL URL" width="800" height="800"/>
• Insert the code into the web page where you want the model to appear. Adjust the width (width) and height (height) to fit the dimensions of your website.

Additional Options

When embedding ADOIT in a website, you can customize the appearance and behaviour of the iFrame by adding different URL parameters:
• Set language: To set the language in which ADOIT is displayed, add "&lang= < language code >" to the URL. Depending on the product configuration, possible language codes are e.g. “en” for English or “de” for German. By default, this parameter is already included in a model URL.

Passing Multiple Parameters

Only the first parameter is separated from the URL with a question mark (?). To pass multiple parameters to the same URL, pass all parameters after the first parameter using an ampersand (&).

Enable Embedding ADOIT as an iFrame

Displaying ADOIT within a frame is not allowed due to security reasons by default. The iFrame will remain blank in this case. To enable embedding ADOIT as an iFrame:
1. Open the folder “ < Tomcat installation > /webapps“ and open the file ADOIT21_0.war with a file archiver. Edit the file adoxx_web.properties which can be found inside.
2. Set security.src.frame-ancestors based on the pages which should be allowed to embed ADOIT as an iFrame. The parameter 'self' allows you to embed ADOIT from pages with the same origin as the web server. In addition, one or more URLs of websites may be specified. Separate the parameters with a space. Save the changes afterwards.

Example

If you want to allow embedding ADOIT as an iFrame from the same origin and https://example.com, you can use:

security.src.frame-ancestors = 'self' ht ﻿ tps://example.com

The Apache Tomcat web server has to be restarted for the configuration changes to become effective.

children.title: Access ADOIT via a REST API
children.summary: ADOIT provides a REST API for accessing model data from other applications, with activation instructions in Administration Help and usage details in the ADOxx Developer Portal.
children.content:
ADOIT provides a REST interface. This interface can be used to access data in ADOIT from other applications.

Via the REST API included in ADOIT you can e.g. display a model graphic or other model data from another application.

note

Instructions on how to activate access to the REST API are covered in the chapter REST API in the Administration Help.

For information on how to use the REST API, please refer to the ADOxx Developer Portal.

If you have questions, please contact your ADOIT consultant.

children.title: Validation and Release
children.summary: Introduction to validation functions for checking model compliance with guidelines and overview of preconfigured release workflows in ADOIT.
children.content:
In this part of the manual, the following topics are outlined:
• Validation: The validation functions in ADOIT allow you to check whether models and objects comply to the modelling guidelines.
• Release Workflows: This chapter provides an overview of the preconfigured release workflows that are included in ADOIT.

children.title: Validation
children.summary: Validation functions check models and objects against modelling guidelines, such as mandatory properties, with configurable check categories and individual checks.
children.content:
The validation functions in ADOIT allow you to check whether models and objects comply to the modelling guidelines. If the modelling guidelines are violated, ADOIT shows corresponding notifications.

Examples of Modelling Guidelines

• Mandatory object properties should be filled to ensure a minimum of descriptive information.

There are several check categories, which, in turn, consist of one or several individual checks.

note

The provision of check categories and individual checks depends on the configuration of your ADOIT installation. They can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.

children.title: Run Checks
children.summary: Run validation checks on models or objects either all at once or by selected categories, with results shown in the Validate widget.
children.content:
You can either run all checks at once or run checks by category. When you validate a model or object, the "Validate" widget opens at the right side of the program window. The checks are run and the results are displayed.

Validate Model

To validate a model:
1. Open the model in the graphical editor.
2. Click the Validate button in the menu bar of the model, and then click either All or By category....
3. In case you chose By category... in step 2, a dialogue is displayed. Select one or more categories and confirm with OK.

Validate Object

To validate an object:
1. Open the properties of the object.
2. Click the More button at the top right corner of the properties pane, point to Validate , and then click either All or By category....
3. In case you chose By category... in step 2, a dialogue is displayed. Select one or more categories and confirm with OK.

children.title: Navigate through Results
children.summary: Navigate validation results grouped by category and notification type, using expand/collapse icons to browse findings.
children.content:
ADOIT displays the results of the checks on a separate page for each model or object.

Within a page, the results are grouped by category (e.g. Methodical) and then type of notification (e.g. Errors or Warnings).

In order to navigate through the results:
• Click the and icons to collapse or expand categories (1) and types of notifications (2).

children.title: Filter Results
children.summary: Filter validation results by notification types such as To-dos, Information, Warnings, or Errors to show or hide specific results.
children.content:
In order to filter the results of the checks:
• Click the To-dos , Information , Warnings or Errors buttons.

You can show or hide results.

children.title: Change Categories
children.summary: Change displayed validation check categories by selecting all or restricting to certain categories via the All selected button.
children.content:
To change which check categories are displayed:
1. Click the All selected button.
2. From the list, either Select all categories or restrict the validation to certain categories.
3. Click OK to refresh the "Validate" widget.

children.title: Display Full Text of Notification
children.summary: Display full notification texts during validation by clicking Read more, or view hints by hovering over the light bulb icon.
children.content:
When you check models and objects, notifications are often only displayed in abbreviated form for space reasons.

To display the full text of a notification:
• Click Read more.

To only display the hint in the notification:
• Move the mouse pointer over the light bulb .

children.title: Display Model/Object
children.summary: Instructions to display the model or object referenced by a notification by clicking the notification title, opening the model and highlighting the object if selected.
children.content:
To display the model or object to which a notification refers:
• Click the title of the notification.

The model is opened (if currently closed). If an object is selected, it is highlighted in the model.

children.title: Mark ToDo as Completed
children.summary: To mark a ToDo check as completed, select its checkbox in the notification; this state is saved and visible to all users in the "Validate" widget.
children.content:
ToDos are checks which have to be verified manually. If your check yields a positive result, you can mark the ToDo as completed. In order to do so:
• Select the check box within the notification.

The checked state is saved and will be visible to all users in the "Validate" widget.

children.title: Fill Mandatory Properties
children.summary: ADOIT warns when mandatory properties are unfilled; clicking the listed property in the notification jumps directly to it for completion.
children.content:
ADOIT provides a warning when not all mandatory properties of an object have been filled. The affected properties are listed in the notification. To fill a mandatory property:
• Click the property in question.

You jump directly to the selected mandatory property.

children.title: Show or Hide "Validate" Widget
children.summary: The "Validate" widget can be hidden or shown by clicking the icon at its top left corner to manage workspace space.
children.content:
You can hide the "Validate" widget to increase your workspace, and show it again at any time:
• To hide the widget, click the icon at the top left corner of the widget.
• To show the widget again, click the icon .

children.title: Release Workflows
children.summary: Overview of preconfigured release workflows in ADOIT, specifically mentioning the EA Workflow.
children.content:
This chapter provides an overview of the preconfigured release workflows that are included in ADOIT:
• The EA Workflow

children.title: EA Workflow
children.summary: The EA Workflow, available only to existing licensed customers, manages object submission, review, and release with roles like Contributors, Architects, and Administrators, including change comments and automatic notifications.
children.content:
note

The EA Workflow is no longer available to new customers. Existing customers with licences that include the EA Workflow may continue to use it.

The EA Workflow allows submitting repository objects for review and release. During the release process contributors carry out different tasks depending on their system roles:
• Contributors submit objects to review. They can also create new versions of already released objects in order to adapt them.
• Architects can execute all transitions. Unlike Contributors, they can also release or reject objects.
• Administrators can also execute all transitions, but they do not receive automatic notifications.

Objects initially have the state "Draft" which is represented by the icon .

Assignment of change comments and automatic notifications

Whenever you execute a transition you can assign a change comment. This comment is saved in the Version history (property in the chapter "Change History").

Once the transition to a new state is complete, ADOIT automatically sends out emails to notify the user(s) who are responsible for executing the next transition in the release process:
• Architects are notified when objects are submitted to review or submitted for deletion.
• Object owners are notified when their objects are released or rejected, when a new end of life date is set for their objects, and when new draft versions of their objects are created.
• The user is assigned as Responsible business actor (property in the chapter "Organisation").

note

The availability of the EA Workflow depends on the licence.

children.title: Submit to Review
children.summary: To start the release process, submit an object to review via the Release button; validation checks run and the object's state changes to "Under review".
children.content:
In order to start the release process, an object has to be submitted to review:
• Open the properties of the object you want to submit to review.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Submit to review.

Checks are run to find out if the object is valid, e.g. whether the mandatory properties are filled. The results of the checks are shown in the "Validation" widget at the right side of the program window.

Then you can execute the transition. The icon indicates the new state "Under review".

children.title: Release Object
children.summary: To release an object under review, use the Release button; this increments the version number, changes state to "Released", replaces predecessor versions in models, deletes predecessors, and transfers references.
children.content:
In order to release an object which has been submitted to review:
• Open the properties of the object you want to release.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Release.

The internal version number of the object increases to the next whole number (e.g. from "0.01" to "1.00"). The state of the object changes to "Released" (icon ).

Behaviour if a Predecessor Version Already Exists

When you release a new version of an object, keep the following in mind:
• The new object replaces the predecessor version of the object in all models.
• The predecessor version of the object is automatically deleted.
• Incoming references are transferred from the predecessor object to the new version of the object.

children.title: Reject Object
children.summary: To reject an object under review, use the Release button and select Reject; the object's state reverts to "Draft".
children.content:
In order to reject an object which has been submitted to review:
• Open the properties of the object you want to reject.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Reject.

The state of the object returns to "Draft" (icon ).

children.title: Set End of Life Date
children.summary: Set a new end of life date for a released object via the Release button; this creates a new draft version copy with updated version number and state "Draft".
children.content:
In order to set a new end of life date for a released object:
• Open the properties of the object for which you want to set a new end of life date.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Set end of life date.
• In the Valid until or Decommission Date box, enter an end of life date (either manually or via the support dialogue ).
• Click OK.

A new object is created as a copy of the original object with a new internal version number and the state "Draft" (icon ).

note

If the new object is submitted to review and then released, the predecessor version of the object is automatically deleted.

children.title: Change
children.summary: Make changes to a released object by creating a new draft version copy via the Release button; the new object has state "Draft" and a new version number.
children.content:
You can make changes to a released object by creating a new draft version of it. In order to do so:
• Open the properties of the object you want to change.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Change.

A new object is created as a copy of the original object with a new internal version number and the state "Draft" (icon ).

note

If the new object is submitted to review and then released, the predecessor version of the object is automatically deleted.

children.title: Submit for Deletion
children.summary: Submit an object for deletion via the Release button; the state changes to "To be deleted" and can be deleted by an Architect, with warnings if incoming references exist.
children.content:
You can submit an object for deletion. In order to do so:
• Open the properties of the object you want to delete.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Submit for deletion.

The state of the object changes to "To be deleted". The icon represents this state. Any Architect can now delete the object.

note

If an object you want to delete contains incoming references, a warning appears. You can select to delete the object regardless or abort the transition.

note

You cannot submit an object for deletion for which a new draft version already exists.

children.title: Back to Released
children.summary: Change an object marked for deletion back to "Released" state via the Release button.
children.content:
You can change the state of objects marked for deletion back to released. In order to do so:
• Open the properties of the object for which you want to change the state back to released.
• Click the Release button in the menu bar of the properties pane, and then click Back to released.

The state of the object changes to "Released". The icon represents this state.

children.title: Check Version History
children.summary: Check an object's version history, which logs all state changes, in the Version history property under "Change History".
children.content: If you want to see a protocol of all state changes of an object, you can check its version history. The corresponding property Version history is located in the chapter "Change History".

children.title: Accessibility, Videos and More
children.summary: Overview of topics including accessibility features, videos, help functions, settings, workspace survey scoring, ADONIS synchronization mapping, and glossary.
children.content:
In this part of the manual, the following topics are outlined:
• Accessibility in ADOIT: This chapter provides an overview of the accessibility features that make it easier for people with disabilities to work with ADOIT.
• All Videos: Explore a playlist with all our how-to videos for ADOIT.
• Help: All help functions in ADOIT.
• Settings: Functions for manipulating ADOIT itself.
• Workspaces: How the Score of a Survey Is Calculated: This section explains how survey scores are calculated in workspaces.
• Synchronisation with ADONIS - Default Mapping: This section describes the standard mapping for synchronising objects between the ADOIT and ADONIS default libraries.
• Glossary: A short glossary.

children.title: Accessibility in ADOIT
children.summary: ADOIT accessibility features include screen reader support with alternative texts, WCAG 2.2 AA compliant graphics, accessibility mode, keyboard navigation, and light/dark mode in online help.
children.content:
The following accessibility features make it easier for people with disabilities to work with ADOIT:
• You can use a screen reader to read what is displayed on the screen. Alternative texts explain the purpose of buttons and links.
• Graphics have been designed to conform to the WCAG 2.2 AA standard. Good legibility is ensured for users with low vision by providing strong contrasts between text and background where needed.
• Accessibility mode allows users with impairments to more effectively use ADOIT.
• You can navigate through the application and interact with items using the keyboard.

Additionally, in the online help, you can choose between light and dark mode to help you more easily read text.

children.title: Accessibility Mode
children.summary: Accessibility mode enhances usability for impaired users by adding focus indicators and setting the tabular editor as default; enabled via the user symbol menu.
children.content:
Accessibility mode allows users with impairments to more effectively use ADOIT. When this mode is enabled, the following happens:
• Focus indicators are applied to interactive elements, providing keyboard-only users with a clear visual cue to identify the currently focused element.
• The tabular editor becomes the default model editor.

To enable accessibility mode:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Accessibility Mode.

children.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
children.summary: ADOIT provides keyboard shortcuts for navigation and interaction within the application.
children.content: The following keyboard shortcuts are available in ADOIT to navigate through the application and to interact with items.

children.title: Navigate in ADOIT
children.summary: Keyboard shortcuts for navigation include Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys, Enter/Spacebar, Esc, and Ctrl+Shift+X to find focus.
children.content:
Action | Keyboard Shortcut
Move forward through controls | Tab
Move back through controls | Shift+Tab
Move between items in a single control, or among a set of related controls | Arrow keys
Select, activate or execute an item | Enter or Spacebar
Cancel action; exit dialogue box or menu | Esc
Find focus | Ctrl+Shift+X

children.title: General Keyboard Shortcuts
children.summary: General keyboard shortcuts cover cut, copy, paste, delete, rename, save, undo/redo, context menu, properties opening, and group expansion/collapse.
children.content:
Action | Keyboard Shortcut
Cut element | Ctrl+X
Copy element | Ctrl+C
Paste element | Ctrl+V
Delete element | Del
Rename element | F2
Save changes | Ctrl+S
Repeat last action | Ctrl+Y
Undo last action | Ctrl+Z
Open context menu | Shift+F10
Open model properties | Alt+Enter
Open object and connector properties | Enter
Close properties | Esc
Expand selected group | Right Arrow
Collapse selected group | Left Arrow

children.title: Graphical Editor
children.summary: Graphical editor shortcuts include select all, search, create relation, save as, remove objects, move objects, switch connector styles, toggle Hover Modelling Assistant, and display page breaks/numbers.
children.content:
Action | Keyboard Shortcut
Select all | Ctrl+A
Select all (including containers) | Ctrl+Shift+A
Search in model | Ctrl+F
Create relation | R
Save as | Ctrl+Shift+S
Remove selected object from the model | Del
Remove selected object from the model and Object Catalogue | Shift+Del
Move selected objects on the drawing area | Arrow keys
Move selected objects to the front/back | Ctrl+Shift + Page up/down
Switch between drawing right-angled connectors or straight connectors | Ctrl+ #
Enable or disable the Hover Modelling Assistant | Ctrl+Shift+H
Display or hide page breaks | Ctrl+Alt+P
Display or hide page numbers | Ctrl+Alt+N

children.title: Translation Editor
children.summary: Translation editor shortcuts enable switching views, expanding/collapsing nodes, navigation, filtering, saving, and jumping between element explorer and attribute/translation areas.
children.content:
Action | Keyboard Shortcut
Switch between tree and attributes | Ctrl+Enter
Expand selected node in the tree | Right Arrow
Collapse selected node in the tree | Left Arrow
Navigate in tree and attributes | Ctrl+Up Arrow/Down Arrow
Filter translated elements | Ctrl+F
Save translation | Ctrl+S
Select an element in the element explorer and jump to the attribute area / Select an attribute for translation and jump to the translation area | Enter
Leave the translation area and jump to the attribute area / Leave the attribute area and jump to the element explorer: | Esc

children.title: Additional Keyboard Shortcuts
children.summary: Additional keyboard shortcuts exist for the tabular editor and Explorer, detailed in respective sections.
children.content:
• Keyboard shortcuts in the tabular editor (see Edit Property Values and Select Cells/Rows)
• Keyboard shortcuts in the Explorer (see Expand/Collapse Folders)

children.title: Switch between Dark and Light Mode
children.summary: Online help allows switching between dark and light mode via a button at the top of the page.
children.content:
In the online help, you can choose between light and dark mode to help you more easily read text:
• Click the Switch between dark and light mode button at the top of the page.

children.title: Recommended Browsers
children.summary: Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge are recommended browsers for optimal ADOIT accessibility.
children.content: For optimal accessibility when using ADOIT, we recommend using either Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.

children.title: All Videos
children.summary: A playlist named 'ADOIT Tutorials' provides all how-to videos for ADOIT.
children.content:
Explore a playlist with all our how-to videos for ADOIT.
• Playlist: ADOIT Tutorials

children.title: Help
children.summary: The Help menu offers access to the User Manual, trainings, release highlights, user community, news, events, marketplace, developer portal, and getting started resources.
children.content:
The Help menu in the upper-right corner contains all help functions:
• ADOIT User Manual: Read the User Manual online.
• Trainings: Discover the ADOIT Training Portfolio or get individual coaching sessions.
• What's New: Explore the highlights from the latest ADOIT release.
• ADOIT User Community: Connect with ADOIT users. Ask questions and share your knowledge with fellow EA professionals.
• News: Learn more about the latest developments around ADOIT.
• Upcoming Events: Focus weeks, seminars and trainings – your way to connect with EA aficionados.
• ADOIT Marketplace: Discover add-ons and integrations for ADOIT.
• Developer Portal: Access documentation on available APIs and configuration options to build your own extensions and expand existing functionalities.
• Getting Started: Here is everything you need to know to get started with ADOIT in no time. Ready to jump in?

children.title: Settings
children.summary: User symbol menu allows changing password, switching language, and other user settings.
children.content: Click the user symbol to change your password, switch the language etc.

children.title: Change Password
children.summary: Change password by entering old and new passwords via the user symbol menu's Change password option.
children.content:
To change your password:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Change password....
• Type your old password, type your new password, type your new password again to confirm it, and then press < ENTER > .

children.title: Applications
children.summary: View and revoke OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect application access to ADOIT resources via the user symbol menu's Applications option.
children.content:
To view which applications have been granted access to your ADOIT resources using OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC):
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Applications.

You can revoke this access permission here:
• To the right of a listed application, click Revoke access.

children.title: Language
children.summary: Switch ADOIT interface language via the user symbol menu under Language; selection is remembered for future sessions.
children.content:
In order to switch the language of ADOIT :
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, point to Language, and then select a language.

Once you select a language, ADOIT will remember your selection for subsequent visits.

children.title: Preferences
children.summary: User preferences dialog accessed via user symbol menu includes settings for General, Printing, OAuth 2.0 Clients, and Modelling.
children.content:
Adapt ADOIT to your personal needs. To access the user preferences:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Preferences....

The dialogue consists of several areas based on functional groups. The following sections describe the different options you can change:
• General
• Printing
• OAuth 2.0 Clients
• Modelling

children.title: General
children.summary: General preferences include autosave configuration, notification options, and preferred language for email notifications.
children.content:
The following settings are available:
• Autosave: Configure the number of changes after which the current state within an editor is automatically saved. This feature is activated by default. You can turn it off if you prefer to save your progress manually.

Automatically saving after a number of changes is available in the following editors:
• Graphical editor
• Tabular editor
• Properties pane
• Translation editor

Autosave on Session Timeout and New Login

In addition to automatically saving after a number of changes, ADOIT also saves the following changes when your session has expired due to inactivity:
• Changes made in the graphical editor
• Changes made in the tabular editor (when opened based on a model)
• Changes made in the properties pane of models and modeling objects

However, if you close the browser tab without logging off and then log back into ADOIT while your session is still active, ALL unsaved changes will be lost.

• Notifications: Choose what notifications you want to appear in ADOIT.

To turn on notifications when creating relations by drag and drop in the Explorer, select the option Show information dialog when creating relations.

To turn on notifications when clicking a link that opens an external website, select the option Show warning when opening external links.

To enable a hint about creating relations by drag and drop in the properties, select the option Show hint when opening properties.
• Languages: Select your preferred language for email notifications. ADOIT automatically sends out email notifications when specific events occur. For example, users are notified when their attention is required for a step in a release workflow.

children.title: Printing
children.summary: Printing preferences cover default corporate identity schemes, page layouts, and visibility of page breaks and numbers based on model access rights.
children.content:
The following settings are available:
• Corporate Identity: Only available if at least two corporate identity schemes have been configured. Select which corporate identity scheme is set as default for printing models to PDF and creating reports.

note

Corporate identity schemes can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.
• Page Layout: Select which page layout is set as default for printing models to PDF and creating reports. Page layouts determine the appearance of the header and footer.
• Write Access to Model: Select whether page breaks and page numbers are visible, if you have write access to a model.
• Read Access to Model: Select whether page breaks and page numbers are visible, if you have read-only access to a model.

note

Page breaks divide models into separate pages for printing. They are displayed as dashed lines in the graphical editor.

Page breaks are defined in the print settings. When you make page layout changes before printing a model and save the print settings, the page breaks displayed in the graphical editor will be updated automatically.

children.title: OAuth 2.0 Clients
children.summary: OAuth 2.0 Clients preferences allow revoking access for authorized applications; configuration is done in ADOIT Administration.
children.content:
Only available if at least one application that uses OAuth 2.0 has been allowed access to your ADOIT resources. The following settings are available:
• To revoke access for an application, click the Revoke access button .

note

OAuth 2.0 clients can be configured in the ADOIT Administration.

children.title: Modelling
children.summary: Modelling preferences include mode behavior for unused objects/connectors, connector styles, bridges, crosshair display, move along behavior for contained objects, and Hover Modelling Assistant visibility.
children.content:
The following settings are available:
• Mode: Define what should happen to objects and connectors in models that do not match the current mode.

Example

Objects and connectors not used in the current mode can be represented in grey or entirely hidden from the active model.
• Rectangular Connectors: Make ADOIT draw right-angled connectors automatically. Clear this check box to make ADOIT draw straight connectors instead.
• Bridges: Draw bridges if connectors cross.
• Crosshair: Show a crosshair when modelling.
• Move Along: Resizable objects and aggregations can act as container objects for other objects. When you drag such a container around the drawing area, objects placed inside are moved along if you press and hold the < Shift > key at the same time.

Clear this check box if you want contained objects to move along at all times (without simultaneously pressing the < Shift > key).

note

The ArchiMate Application Library does not contain any aggregations (but all object types except the Junction are resizeable by default).

• Hover Modelling Assistant: Show a set of controls when an object is selected in the graphical editor. You can use these controls to add objects to the model and to perform other actions such as opening the properties or generating a URL.

children.title: Info
children.summary: Show detailed session status information via the user symbol menu's Info option.
children.content:
In order to show a dialogue window with detailed status information about the current session:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Info.

children.title: Administration
children.summary: Switch to ADOIT Administration via the user symbol menu's Administration option.
children.content:
To switch to the ADOIT Administration:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Administration.

children.title: Logout
children.summary: Log out of ADOIT via the user symbol menu's Logout option.
children.content:
In order to log out of ADOIT:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Logout.

children.title: Workspaces: How the Score of a Survey Is Calculated
children.summary: Workspace survey scores are calculated by summing question scores (1-4, 1-3, or 1/4) and converting to a 0-100% scale; some questions may be excluded from scoring but used for machine learning.
children.content:
This section explains how survey scores are calculated in workspaces. When users complete a survey, the score for the assessed element is calculated based on the answers given.

Most survey questions in workspaces have four possible answers, but some have two or three.
• For questions with four possible answers, the score is 1-4.
• For questions with three possible answers, the score is 1-3.
• For questions with two possible answers, the score is either 1 or 4.

note

The explanation above refers to the default configuration of surveys in workspaces. In the ADOIT Administration, it is possible to configure questions with more than four answer options, or assign score values higher than 4 to individual answer options.

Once the survey is completed, the scores for all questions are added together and converted to a percentage-based score between 0 and 100. Here's an example to illustrate how this works:

Example: Application Investment Planning Template

The Application Investment Planning template includes a survey that lets you assess the business fitness of applications:
• The survey contains 16 questions with four answer options (worth 1-4 points), one question with three answer options (worth 1-3 points) and two questions with two answer options (worth 1 or 4 points).
• The minimum possible score for the survey is 19 (19 x 1) points, which corresponds to the case where the user selects the lowest possible answer option for each question.
• The maximum possible score is 75 (16 x 4 + 1 x 3 + 2 x 4) points, which corresponds to the case where the user selects the highest possible answer option for each question.
• To standardise the score to a 0-100 scale, the minimum achievable score of 19 points corresponds to 0% and the maximum achievable score of 75 points corresponds to 100%. All other possible scores fall between these two values.

note

Some questions are internally marked as irrelevant for calculating the survey score. These answers contribute to machine learning predictions but do not affect the overall score. In the default ArchiMate Application Library that comes with ADOIT, only one question is marked this way: Question 18, "What is the lifecycle stage of the application?" in the "IT fit" survey.

children.title: Synchronisation with ADONIS - Default Mapping
children.summary: Describes default object synchronization mapping between ADOIT and ADONIS libraries, specifically ArchiMate and ADONIS BPMS libraries.
children.content:
This section describes the standard mapping for synchronising objects between the ADOIT and ADONIS default libraries. The mapping provides the assignment of the exported classes to the classes in the target library.
• ArchiMate Library & ADONIS BPMS Library

children.title: ArchiMate Library & ADONIS BPMS Library
children.summary: Standard mapping covers metamodel elements between ArchiMate Application Library and ADONIS BPMS Library, noting indirect relations and user synchronization considerations.
children.content:
The standard mapping for the ArchiMate Application Library and the ADONIS BPMS Application Library covers the following metamodel elements:

note

When using ADONIS 19.1 or higher together with ADOIT 21.0.0 or higher, the interface also evaluates indirect relations between Processes and Applications via Business Process Diagrams.

The mapped metamodel elements are examined below in more detail.

note

Arrows (- > ) indicate that elements are not mapped one-to-one, but to an element with a different name.

The Users themselves are not replicated. Ideally, they are synchronised from a directory service. If that is not possible, you have to ensure that manually created Users have the same name in both products.

children.title: From ADOIT to ADONIS
children.summary: From ADOIT to ADONIS, Application Components and their attributes and relations (e.g., Responsible business actors) are transferred and mapped accordingly.
children.content:
Application Components and their relations to Users are transferred to ADONIS.

Application Component - > Application
• The following attributes of Application Components are replicated to ADONIS:
• Name
• Description
• Valid from
• Valid until
• Change History
• Lifecycle state
• Investment strategy
• The following relation of Application Components is transferred to ADONIS:
• Responsible business actors - > Responsible person

children.title: From ADONIS to ADOIT
children.summary: From ADONIS to ADOIT, Processes and Roles with their attributes and relations are transferred, including indirect application references via Business Process Diagrams when using compatible versions.
children.content:
Processes and Roles including their relations are transferred to ADOIT.

Process - > Business Process
• The following attributes of Processes are replicated to ADOIT:
• Name
• Description
• Valid from
• Valid until
• Potential and maturity analysis (as-is average) - > Current level of maturity
• Cost efficiency
• Cycle time
• Quality
• Customer satisfaction
• IT support
• Compliance
• Change history
• State
• Risk management
• Process management maturity
• The following relations of Processes are transferred to ADOIT:
• Referenced Applications/IT System Elements - > Serving

note

Applications are identified not only through direct references from Processes, but also through indirect references via Business Process Diagrams. See below for details.
• Process owner - > Responsible business actors
• Subordinated processes - > Aggregation

Role - > Business Actor
• The following attributes of Roles are replicated to ADOIT:
• Name
• Description
• Valid from
• Valid until
• Change history

Application references evaluated for Processes

The following paths are evaluated to identify Applications referenced by a Process:
1. Process - > Referenced applications/IT system elements - > Application
2. Process - > Referenced business process/process landscape - > Business Process Diagram - > Referenced applications/IT system elements - > Application
3. Process - > Referenced business process/process landscape - > Business Process Diagram - > Task - > Referenced applications/IT system elements - > Application
4. Process - > Referenced business process/process landscape - > Business Process Diagram - > Subprocess - > Referenced subprocess - > Business Process Diagram - > ...

The indirect relations between Processes and Applications via Business Process Diagrams (paths 2-4) are only evaluated when using ADONIS 19.0.1 or higher together with ADOIT 21.0.0 or higher, and if the extended configuration is in use. When synchronising objects using earlier product versions, only direct relations (path 1) are evaluated.

children.title: Administrator
children.summary: Administrator is a person with special rights in ADOIT, such as creating user accounts and assigning access rights.
children.content: A person that administrates ADOIT. They are equipped with special rights, e.g. may create user accounts for users and assign access rights to them.

children.title: ADOIT Administration
children.summary: ADOIT Administration is the software package reserved for administrators to manage ADOIT.
children.content: Software package for the administration of ADOIT, reserved exclusively for administrators.

children.title: Application Library
children.summary: Application Library defines model types, objects, connectors, analysis queries, and more; created by the customiser during configuration.
children.content: Contains the definition of the model types, objects and connectors, predefined analysis queries and much more. The Application Library is created by the customiser during ADOIT configuration.

children.title: Attribute
children.summary: Attribute is a property of a model type or class, defined by the customiser with various attribute types.
children.content: Property of a model type or a class. Attributes may be of various attribute types and are defined by a customiser during the Application Library definition.

children.title: Attribute Type
children.summary: Attribute Type defines the data structure of an attribute, such as text, numbers, dates, or tables.
children.content: The data structure of the attribute. Depending on the attribute type, totally different content may be stored in the attribute: text of various length, integer and floating-point numbers, dates, times, tables, and much more.

children.title: Cardinality
children.summary: Cardinality rules specify how many endpoints of a certain type a relation class may have.
children.content: Rules for endpoints. Cardinality rules define how many endpoints of a certain type a relation class may have.

children.title: Class
children.summary: Class is an abstract template element in the Application Library from which objects or relations are instantiated and placed in models.
children.content: An (abstract) template element defined in the ADOIT Application Library, from which (real) objects or relations are created as instances an placed in models. For instance, “Department 5” and “Accounting” are instances of the object class Business Actor and “Write Letter” as well as “Update Virus Protection” instances of the object class Business Process. The same applies to relation classes. The classes are defined by the customiser during the definition of the Application Library. Classes have attributes.

children.title: Component
children.summary: Component is part of ADOIT Administration containing modules for specific tool usage types.
children.content: Part of the ADOIT Administration. Every component contains the modules needed for a certain type of tool usage.

children.title: Connector
children.summary: Connector is an instance of a relation class connecting objects in models, with allowed types depending on model definitions.
children.content: Connection between objects. Instance of a relation class. Shows the relation between (two, sometimes more) objects. Depending on the model type definition and the objects concerned, different types of connectors are allowed.

children.title: Customiser
children.summary: Customiser is a person with full access to ADOIT configuration, defining Application Libraries and component access.
children.content: Person with full access to the ADOIT configuration. A customiser e.g. defines a new Application Library or the overall component access of an existing product.

children.title: Endpoint
children.summary: Endpoint defines which object classes a relation class may attach to and is subject to cardinality rules.
children.content: Endpoints define to which object classes a relation class may attach to. Endpoints are subject to cardinality rules.

children.title: Model
children.summary: Model is a group of objects and connectors representing flows, structures, or information pools; each is an instance of a model type.
children.content: A group of objects, possibly connected by connectors and other relations. Models can picture flows (e.g. a process), structures (e.g. an organisational unit), an information pool (e.g. a document library) and much more. Every Application Library contains different model types, defined by a customiser. Every model is an instance of one of these model types.

children.title: Model Group
children.summary: Model Group is a hierarchical directory structure organizing models in the repository.
children.content: Directory for models in the repository. The model group structure is organised hierarchically.

children.title: Model Type
children.summary: Model Type is part of the Application Library defining aggregations of objects and connectors for illustrating company aspects.
children.content: Part of the ADOIT Application Library. Every model is an instance of a certain model type. A model type contains an aggregation of objects and connectors, serving for illustrating certain company aspects.

children.title: Properties
children.summary: Properties display attributes and relations of models, objects, and connectors organized in editable chapters.
children.content: Graphical display form for the attributes and relations of models, objects, and connectors. The attributes are organised in chapters in the properties and can be edited there.

children.title: Object
children.summary: Object is an instance of an object class, distinguished as repository objects reusable across models or modeling objects local to models.
children.content: Instance of an (object) class. A distinction is drawn between repository objects (re-usable objects, stored in a repository) and modelling objects (maintained only in the models in which they are created).

children.title: Object Class
children.summary: Object Class defines modeling object types such as Business Actors or Business Processes; see Class.
children.content: Object classes define the modelling object types (e.g. Business Actors, Business Processes, etc.). See Class.

children.title: Object Group
children.summary: Object Group is a hierarchical directory organizing objects in the repository.
children.content: Directory for objects in the repository. The object group structure is organised hierarchically.

children.title: Relation Class
children.summary: Relation Class defines connectors used in modeling or non-graphical relations; see Class.
children.content: Relation classes define connectors used in modelling or relations without graphical representation. See Class.

children.title: Rights
children.summary: Rights define access permissions for administrators and user accounts covering components, accounts, models, objects, and structural changes.
children.content: Every ADOIT administrator and every user account has access rights within the application. These cover various aspects (access to components, other user accounts, models and objects, the possibility to change internal structures and more).

children.title: Repository
children.summary: Repository is a database storage allowing multiple versions and languages of models, reusable objects, and local/global information.
children.content: A special kind of information storage in databases. In ADOIT this means for instance that models may exist in any number of versions and languages, that objects can be re-used in multiple models, that objects can contain both local (model-specific) and global (general) information and more.

children.title: User
children.summary: User is a person working with ADOIT who must log in with a user account.
children.content: A person that works with ADOIT. For this, they have to log in with a user account.

children.title: User Account
children.summary: User Account is assigned to each user by an administrator for login, representing the user in the database with credentials and rights.
children.content: Each user is assigned one (or more) user account(s) by an administrator to log in to ADOIT. Thus, a user account is the virtual counterpart of the user in the ADOIT database and has features like user name, password, and rights.

documents.title: ADOIT 21.0 Administration Help
documents.summary: Introduction to ADOIT as an IT service and management tool aligned with standards like ITIL, COBIT, TOGAF, and RiskIT, usable out-of-the-box or customizable.
documents.content:
Welcome to the ADOIT Help. ADOIT is the IT service and management tool of the BOC Group.

ADOIT provides rich functionality for all typical IT management tasks. It is geared to international standards such as ITIL, COBIT, TOGAF and RiskIT, and the considerable experience and expertise of the BOC group gained from a variety of IT management projects.

Use ADOIT either out-of-the-box (ADOIT standard configuration) or expand it to fit your individual needs (ADOIT customising - "tailoring").

children.title: About this Manual
children.summary: This manual provides instructions for using ADOIT Administration, covering getting started, administering ADOIT via browser, and an appendix with advanced topics for administrators.
children.content:
In the following documentation you find instructions on how to use the ADOIT Administration:
• Get Started: This part of the manual describes how to get started with the ADOIT Administration.
• Administration: This part of the manual contains instructions on how to administer ADOIT from your browser. All components of the ADOIT Administration and their functionalities are explained in detail.
• Appendix: The appendix contains topics that ADOIT administrators may find helpful to gain a deeper understanding of certain concepts and functionalities in ADOIT.

children.title: Other Manuals
children.summary: For usage questions about ADOIT, users should consult the User Manual.
children.content: For questions about using ADOIT, please refer to the User Manual.

children.title: Get Started
children.summary: The Get Started section explains how to access ADOIT Administration and navigate the start page to access functionalities.
children.content:
This part of the manual describes how to get started with the ADOIT Administration. It covers the following topics:
• Open ADOIT Administration: Learn how to access the ADOIT Administration.
• Take a Look Around: After logging in, you will be taken to the start page, from where you can access all functionalities.

children.title: Open ADOIT Administration
children.summary: To open ADOIT Administration, enter the URL with /admin.view, log in with credentials, and ensure the user has access to the 'Administration Toolkit' component.
children.content:
To open the ADOIT Administration:
• Enter the URL where ADOIT is available.
• Click Administration or append /admin.view to the URL.
• Enter your credentials (if needed) and log in.

note

To open the ADOIT Administration, a user has to fulfill the following requirement:
• The user must have access to the component "Administration Toolkit" (see View or Change Permissions).

children.title: Take a Look Around
children.summary: After login, the ADOIT Administration start page ('Home') presents components grouped into Users & Access Rights, Libraries & Repositories, and Product Configuration & Licence, with additional tools and help accessible via buttons.
children.content:
After logging in successfully to the ADOIT Administration, you'll find yourself on the start page ("Home").

The start page offers an array of administrative components organised into three main groups:
• Users & Access Rights: This section allows you to manage users, user groups, and system roles efficiently. Create and modify user accounts, assign permissions, and ensure smooth access control.
• Libraries & Repositories: Here, you'll find tools to manage libraries and their repositories, and explore metamodel elements.
• Product Configuration & Licence: In this section, you can fine-tune component settings, view and manage your ADOIT licence, and access the authentication settings.

To open a component, simply click on it.

More Options

Behind the More options button, you'll find access to the Tools menu, which offers a range of additional settings. These include general tools and various support options.

Help and Preferences

If you need guidance, you can click the Help button to access the online help or download the PDF manual. Additionally, you can find various settings to adapt the ADOIT Administration to your personal working style by clicking on the user symbol .

note

All administrative components and the other features mentioned here are explained in detail in the subsequent parts of the Administration Help.

children.title: Administration
children.summary: The Administration section overviews ADOIT Administration components including Users, Rights, System Roles, Libraries, Repositories, Properties, Settings, Licence, Authentication, and advanced Tools menu features.
children.content:
This part of the manual provides an overview of the features of the ADOIT Administration. The ADOIT Administration includes the following components:
• Users: Create, edit, and delete user groups and users.
• Rights: Manage permissions for user groups and users.
• System Roles: Manage system roles and assign members
• Libraries: Update, import and export libraries.
• Repositories: Manage repositories, import and export data.
• Properties: Add, change, remove and organise properties of object and model types.
• Settings: Customise a wide range of library-specific features.
• Licence: View licence information and add new licences.
• Authentication: Manage authentication configurations.

Additionally, the Tools menu provides access to advanced settings, such as authentication settings, monitoring the status of ADOIT, and performing maintenance tasks.

Please refer to the linked chapters above for detailed information on each component of the ADOIT Administration.

children.title: Users
children.summary: The Users page allows creation, editing, deletion, and assignment of user groups and system roles, plus import/export of users and security settings; the default super admin 'Admin' has unrestricted access.
children.content:
The Users page enables you to create, edit, and delete users, and assign user groups and system roles. Additionally, you can export and import users and security settings. With its intuitive interface and powerful functionality, the Users page empowers you to manage your team's user accounts efficiently and effectively, ensuring that they have the access they need to work productively within ADOIT.

Super Admin

During the installation of ADOIT, a user account is created automatically: The user Admin (with the starting password password) is a super user for administrating ADOIT. It has full access to all tool components and database contents. Its rights cannot be restricted.

children.title: View Users
children.summary: The Users page displays a hierarchical or flat list of user groups and users with search, filter, column customization, ID copying, and Excel export features including detailed user attributes.
children.content:
When you open the Users page, a flat list of all top level user groups is the first thing you will see. You can expand the hierarchy to reveal subordinated groups, and the users within the groups.

Search and Filter

To help you quickly find a user group or user, the following options are available:
• Search for a User Group or User: In the Seach box, type the text you want to search for. All user groups and users that contain the search string in their name are shown.
• Show or Hide User Groups: Click Show groups to show or hide user groups. Choose between a flat list of all users or the regular hierarchical view with groups and subgroups containing users.

Examine the User List

The following columns are displayed by default:
• Name: The name of the user group or user. Two types of users can be distinguished. Standard ADOIT users are created manually in the ADOIT Administration, while system users are imported from an external user management system.
• Email: Displays the email address associated with the user.
• Super admin: Indicates whether the user is a super admin.
• System user: Indicates whether the user is a system user .
• Logged In: Indicates whether the user is currently logged into ADOIT.
• Account disabled: Indicates whether the user account is disabled, preventing the user from logging into ADOIT.

Some columns are hidden by default:
• Last Login: Indicates the date and time of the user's last login.
• User-specific information: Shows further information about the user that can be assigned when creating or editing the user.

Show or Hide Columns

To change which columns are displayed:
• At the top right of the user list, click More, point to Show / hide columns, and then choose the columns you want.

Copy ID to Clipboard

To copy the ID of a user group or user to the clipboard:
• Hover over the element, click More, and then select Copy the ID to the clipboard.

Export User Information to Excel

To export user information as an Excel file (XLSX format) for use in other applications:
• Select the check boxes to the left of the user groups you want to export, click Bulk actions, and then select Export as Excel.

The generated Excel file includes all users from the selected user groups, along with their assigned user groups, system roles, and repositories. The following details are also included: name, first name, last name, email, super admin (yes/no), system user (yes/no), last login, user-specific information, and account disabled (yes/no).

children.title: Manage User Groups
children.summary: ADOIT user groups organize users by referencing them, allowing a user to belong to multiple groups simultaneously for better overview and access rights management.
children.content: ADOIT users are organised in user groups for better overview and access rights handling. Please note that ADOIT user groups do not directly contain the users, but reference them: the same user can be referenced from any number of user groups at the same time (and thus exist in them).

children.title: Create User Group
children.summary: User groups can be created as top-level or nested groups via the Users page by naming the group and confirming creation.
children.content:
To create a user group:
1. Go to the Users page.
2. Choose one of the following actions:
• To create a top level user group, click New top level user group.
• For a nested group, hover over the parent group where you want to create a subgroup, click More, and then select Create user group.
3. In the Enter name box, enter a name for your user group, and then click OK.

children.title: Adjust User Groups
children.summary: User groups can be managed by assigning system roles, renaming, deleting, cutting, copying, pasting, moving, and managing repository assignments via the Users page options.
children.content:
User groups can be deleted, copied, pasted, and more:
1. Go to the Users page.
2. Find the user group you want to adjust.
3. Hover over the user group, click More, and then select the option you want:
• Assign system roles
• Rename
• Delete
• Cut, copy and paste
• Move to top level (nested groups only)
• Assign or revoke <active repository>
• Share users with or unshare users from <active repository>

children.title: Manage Users
children.summary: This section introduces key functions for managing users within ADOIT Administration.
children.content: The following sections provide an overview of the most important functions for managing users.

children.title: Create User
children.summary: Creating a user involves entering account details, assigning user groups, system roles, repositories, and optionally enabling trusted login or named user status post-creation.
children.content:
Here is what you need to do to create a user:
1. Go to the Users page and click New User.
2. Begin by filling out the account details on the General tab:
• Enter the name of the new user.
• Enter and confirm the password.
• Optionally, provide additional information such as the first name, last name and email address.
3. Choose additional settings based on the type of user you want to create:
• Select User must change the password to force the user to change their password at the next login.
• Select Account disabled to prevent the user from logging into ADOIT.
• Select Set as super admin to make the user a super admin.
• Trusted Login can only be enabled after the user has been created (see below).
4. Next, go to the Groups and roles tab to assign user groups and system roles:
• Under User groups, click Select user groups and choose at least one user group to assign the user to.
• If you want this person to have access to features of ADOIT (e.g. application scenarios, charts etc.), under System roles, click Select system roles and assign relevant system roles to the user.
5. Next, go to the Repository tab to assign repositories:
• Click Select repository and choose at least one repository to assign as the user's working place to create and save content.
6. The settings on the Named user tab can only be changed after the user has been created (see below).
7. Click Create to complete the user creation process.

note

A user may have access rights to any number of repositories. Users with access rights to more than one repository are presented with a selection window on login.

Post-User Creation Settings

Once user creation is complete, you can configure the following settings:
• Enable trusted login for users who require it. Trusted login means that a user can perform actions without having to enter a username and password. This setting is only relevant in specific scenarios.
• If a scenario license is in use, you can designate the user as a named use user for one or more scenarios.

Proceed as follows:
• Hover over the user, click More, and then click Edit.
• Go to the General tab and enable Trusted Login if the user requires it.
• Go to the Named Use Users tab, click Select Scenarios, and then assign relevant scenarios to ensure the user has guaranteed access.

children.title: Edit User
children.summary: Users can be edited to update details such as passwords, group memberships, and repositories via the Users page edit option.
children.content:
From time to time it may be necessary to edit the user data (forgotten passwords, a new repository is available, the user moves to another department of the company and in the course of that his virtual alter ego moves to a new user group…).

To edit a user:
1. Go to the Users page.
2. Find the user you want to edit.
3. Hover over the user, click More, and then select Edit.
4. Modify the user data as required.
5. Click Update.

note

You can find more information about the various user data in the section Create User.

children.title: Clone User
children.summary: The Clone User function creates a copy of an existing user with identical assignments except for username, password, and personal settings, assigning a random password initially.
children.content:
Using the function Clone User an exact copy of an already existing user can be created. The new user adopts all assignments and authorisations of the original user, except the username, the password and the personal settings stored in the user profile (e.g. language or dialogue settings).

To clone a user:
1. Go to the Users page.
2. Find the user you want to clone.
3. Hover over the user, click More, and then select Clone.
4. In the Enter name box, enter the name of the new user, and then click OK.

note

Please note that a random password will be set for the cloned user. It can be changed later, or the user can set a new password via the "Forgot Password?" link on the login page.

children.title: Delete Users
children.summary: Users can be deleted individually or in bulk, with options to unshare from repositories before deletion; restrictions apply for logged-in users and the super admin cannot be deleted.
children.content:
Users which are no longer needed can be deleted and completely removed from the database by ADOIT administrators.

To delete users:
1. Go to the Users page.
2. Find the users you want to delete.
3. To delete a single user, hover over the user, click More, and then select the option you want:
• Delete: Permanently deletes the user, provided they are not shared with a repository.
• Unshare from all repositories and delete: First removes the user from all repositories they are shared with. Then deletes them permanently — if they are not used in any models.
4. You can also delete multiple users at once:
• Select the check boxes to the left of the users, click Bulk actions, and then select Delete or Unshare from all repositories and delete.

note

Users who are currently logged in cannot be deleted. In addition, if a user has been shared with a repository and the user object is used directly in a model (e.g. placed on the canvas), the user cannot be deleted via Unshare from all repositories and delete until all such usages have been removed.

The super user Admin cannot be deleted.

children.title: Delete User Profile
children.summary: Deleting a user profile resets personalisation data without removing the user account; deleting a user also deletes their profile.
children.content:
Each user has a user profile that stores personalisation data, such as user-specific UI preferences. Deleting a user profile resets this personalisation data for the selected user.

To delete a user profile:
• Go to the Users page.
• Find the user whose profile you want to delete.
• Hover over the user, click More, and then click Delete user profile.

After confirming the security prompt, the user profile is deleted. The user starts with a fresh personalisation state the next time they log in.

note

Deleting a user also deletes the associated user profile. The action Delete user profile only removes the profile data while keeping the user account itself intact.

children.title: Adjust Users
children.summary: Users can be cut, copied, pasted, assigned or revoked from repositories, and shared or unshared with repositories individually or in bulk via the Users page.
children.content:
Users can be cut, copied, pasted, and more:
1. Go to the Users page.
2. Find the users you want to adjust.
3. Choose one of the following actions:
• To adjust a single user, hover over the user, click More, and then select the option you want.
• To adjust multiple users at once, select the check boxes to the left of the users, click Bulk actions, and then select the option you want.
4. The following options are available:
• Cut and copy (and then paste into a user group)
• Assign or revoke <active repository>
• Share users with or unshare users from <active repository>

children.title: Assign or Revoke Current Repository
children.summary: Administrators can assign or revoke the current active repository for users or user groups to control repository access during tasks.
children.content:
As an ADOIT administrator, you can assign or revoke the current repository for individual users or even entire user groups. This ensures that users have access to the correct repository while performing their tasks. When you assign or revoke the current repository at the group level, all users within the group will be affected. For instructions on how to do this:
• Adjust Users
• Adjust User Groups

It's important to note that the current repository refers to the active repository you're currently working in. If you have multiple repositories, it's the one you selected upon login. Additionally, when creating or editing a user, you can assign any repositories they may need access to, in addition to the current repository.

children.title: Share User with or Unshare User from Active Repository
children.summary: Users or user groups can be shared or unshared with the active repository to make them available as modelling objects within ADOIT.
children.content:
It is necessary to share users with a repository to make them available as objects in modelling in ADOIT, for example so that a modeller can assign them as responsible person for an application (in the application´s properties).

As an ADOIT administrator, you can share or unshare individual users or even entire user groups with the currently active repository. When you share or unshare users at the group level, all users within the group will be affected. For instructions on how to do this:
• Adjust Users
• Adjust User Groups

children.title: Export Users
children.summary: Users and user groups can be exported to an AXR file with options to include system roles, metamodel rights, tasks, favourites, and security configuration, optionally password-protected; the Admin user cannot be exported.
children.content:
For external data backup and to transfer user data to ADOIT administrators not networked, it is possible to save user accounts into an external AXR file.

To export users:
1. Go to Users > More options, and then click Export users.
2. Select the users and/or user groups you wish to export. To display all users, select Hide user groups. Then, click Next.

note

To export groups AND all users within those groups, you do not have to manually select each user. Just select the groups you want and proceed to the next page. Then, from the Filter list, select Export user groups and users. Additionally, select Recursive (user groups) to include any sub groups and the users within those.
3. From the Filter list, select whether to export only users, only user groups, or both.
4. Optional: If you are exporting user groups, select Recursive (user groups) to expand the export scope:
• If Export only user groups is chosen from the Filter list, all sub-groups will be included in the export.
• If Export user groups and users is chosen from the Filter list, all users within the selected user groups, as well as any sub-groups and the users within sub-groups, will also be included in the import.
5. Define which additional data to include in the export. Specify the following options:
• Select Including system roles to export all system roles for users and user groups.
• Select Including metamodel rights to export all metamodel rights together with the system roles.
• Select Including rights to export all user rights together with the users.
• Select Including tasks to export all user tasks together with the users.
• Select Including favourites to export all favourites together with the users.
• Select Including security configuration to export the security settings together with the users.
6. Optional: Select Protect export file with password to encrypt the export file.
7. Click Export. The data is exported.

When the export is complete, a success message appears. Close the message to complete the process.

note

The special user Admin cannot be exported.

children.title: Import Users
children.summary: Previously exported users can be imported from AXR files with options for recursive group import, inclusion of roles and settings, repository assignment, and conflict resolution strategies.
children.content:
Users previously exported can be imported and stored in the ADOIT database.

To import users:
1. Go to Users > More options, and then click Import users.
2. Click Browse and select the file you want to import. You can also drag a file from your computer to the Drag and drop files here to upload area.
3. Optional: If the import file is encrypted, enter the password and click Next.
4. Select the items you want to import, and choose the target group for the import. To view the users included in the target groups, select Show users contained in groups. Then, click Next.
5. Optional: If you are importing user groups, select Recursive (including all subordinated users and user groups) to expand the export scope. All users within the selected user groups, as well as any sub-groups and the users within sub-groups, will also be included in the import.
6. Define which additional data to include in the import. Specify the following options:
• Select Including system roles to import all system roles for users and user groups.
• Select Including metamodel rights to import all metamodel rights together with the system roles.
• Select Including tasks to import all user tasks together with the users.
• Select Including favourites to import all favourites together with the users.
• Select Including security configuration to import the security settings together with the users.
7. Select Assign current repository automatically to make sure the imported users will have access to the active repository you're currently working in (see Assign or revoke current repository).
8. From the Conflict strategy if a user in the file is already existing in the user management list, select the behaviour if a user already exists:
• Insert (new data will be inserted. Existing data will be overwritten.): Inserts the user, combining information from both sources (default selection).
• Overwrite (the user data from the import file will overwrite the existing user): Overwrites the user in the database.
• Ignore (The users from the import file will not be imported): Ignores the data in the import file, preserving the original user.
9. Click Import. The data is imported.

When the import is complete, a success message appears. Close the message to complete the process.

children.title: Export Security Configuration
children.summary: Security configuration including password strength and login settings can be exported to an AXR file for backup or distribution, with optional password protection.
children.content:
This procedure allows exporting security settings (password strength settings and login settings) to an external AXR file for backup and distribution matters.

To export the security configuration:
1. Go to Users > More options, and then click Export security configuration.
2. Optional: Select Protect export file with password to encrypt the export file.
3. Click Export. The data is exported.

When the export is complete, a success message appears. Close the message to complete the process.

children.title: Import Security Configuration
children.summary: Security configuration files can be imported into ADOIT to restore password and login settings from AXR files, supporting encrypted files.
children.content:
This procedure allows importing security settings (password strength settings and login settings) to the ADOIT database.

To import a security configuration:
1. Go to Users > More options, and then click Import security configuration.
2. Click Browse and select the file you want to import. You can also drag a file from your computer to the Drag and drop files here to upload area.
3. Optional: If the import file is encrypted, enter the password.
4. Click Import. The data is imported.

When the import is complete, a success message appears. Close the message to complete the process.

children.title: Import Users from Excel
children.summary: ADOIT administrators can import users in bulk from Excel using a downloadable template containing required user information columns.
children.content:
The Users page allows ADOIT administrators to import users from Excel.

You can download a template Excel file that contains columns for the information required to create a new user. You can capture users with this template, and then import users in bulk.

children.title: Open Import Wizard
children.summary: The import wizard for importing users from Excel is accessed via Users > More options > Import Users from Excel.
children.content:
To open the import wizard:
• Go to Users > More options, and then click Import Users from Excel.

children.title: Get Template
children.summary: Template Excel files for user import can be downloaded in XLSX or CSV format from the Template list in the import wizard.
children.content:
To download the template Excel file:
• From the Template list, select the template you want, and then click the Get template button .

You can download an XLSX or CSV template.

children.title: Capture Users
children.summary: To create users via Excel import, required columns include Loginname, Forename, Surname, Email, and optional user-specific information.
children.content:
The following columns need to be populated to create a user:
• Loginname: The username for login.
• Forename: The first name of the new user.
• Surname: The last name of the user.
• Email: The email address of the new user.
• User-specific information: Add additional information that can be viewed in the properties of the user object.

children.title: Import Users
children.summary: User import from Excel supports updating existing users, enabling trusted login, assigning user groups and repositories, and uploading the prepared template file for processing.
children.content:
To perform the user import:
1. To update existing users with data from the template, select the Update users check box.
2. To enable trusted login if the users require it, select the Trusted login check box.
3. From the User groups list, select the user groups the users should belong to.
4. In the Repositories and object groups area, select at least one repository to assign it to the users as their working place. Additionally, define an object group per repository where the user objects should be placed to make them available as modelling objects (see Share or unshare users with active repository).
5. Click Upload File and pick the template Excel file you prepared. The number of users to be processed will be shown. Click Yes to continue.

The users will be imported into ADOIT.

children.title: View Import Report
children.summary: After user import, an import report displays usernames, personal info, CRUD operations performed, results, and details for any errors.
children.content:
Once the import of users into ADOIT is complete, an import report is displayed. It contains the following columns of information:
• Username, Forename, Surname, Email and User-specific information: To let you verify that the data from the template was used correctly.
• CRUD: Shows whether a create, read, update or delete operation was performed.
• Result: Shows whether the operation was successful.
• Details: Provides further details if the operation was not successful.

children.title: Manage Named Users
