Deactivating this option is useful in case of publicly accessible deployments when allowing access to the Organisation Portal without authentication is not desirable.

Deactivating this option has the following effects:
• Only authenticated users with the system role 'Organisation Portal' may log in to the Organisation Portal.
• The link to access the Organisation Portal on the ADOIT login page is not displayed.
• Access to the Organisation Portal via user-specific URLs is disabled.
• The menu entry Organisation Portal from the dropdown menu for scenario selection in ADOIT is disabled.
• The Organisation Portal configuration options Access via the link on the web client login page, Default user for anonymous access and Activate user-specific URL become inactive.
• Access via the link on the web client login page: Select whether a link is displayed on the ADOIT login page that allows users to enter the Organisation Portal. The Standard user (see below) is utilized in this case.
• Default user for anonymous access: Select which user account is utilized when users enter the Organisation Portal via the link on the ADOIT login page.

children.title: Configure Start Model
children.summary: Configure Start Model page in the Organisation Portal wizard allows setting user-specific and repository-specific entry points and defining start models for these entry points.
children.content: The second page of the Organisation Portal configuration wizard allows you to configure user-specific and repository-specific entry points to the Organisation Portal, as well as establish a start model for each of these entry points.

children.title: Users
children.summary: The Users tab lists Organisation Portal user accounts with system role 'Organisation Portal', allowing configuration of user-specific URLs, start models, repository selection, and activation of anonymous access via Trusted Login.
children.content:
This tab lists all user accounts with the system role "Organisation Portal".

You can configure different users (different settings for the Organisation Portal and different user rights). This allows you to provide multiple entry points to the Organisation Portal and to restrict access to the available repository content for employees of your organisation.

note

Trusted Login is a prerequisite for user accounts which are used to access the Organisation Portal anonymously.

• Name: The first column contains the name of the user account.
• User-specific URL: This column contains the URL that allows users to enter the Organisation Portal anonymously, without having to provide credentials. Access rights to the models in the database are based on the user account that is used and on the settings for the Organisation Portal.

The URL is composed of the Base URL and the suffix ?reader= < user account >, e.g. http://server:8000/ADOIT21_0?reader=Reader2.

Click Copy to copy the URL to the clipboard, and then paste the URL where you need it.
• Selected repository: If a start model has been selected for this user-specific URL, the repository that contains the start model will be displayed here.
• Start model: Here you can specify a start model that will appear on the Organisation Portal start page. Click Configure start model, and then choose a repository and the start model you want. If a start model has been selected for this user-specific URL already, it will be displayed here.

note

The start model for the Default user for anonymous access (see above) will also be displayed on the "Read & Explore" scenario start page as long as no specific "Read & Explore" start model has been defined (see Read & Explore Scenario).

• Activate user-specific URL: Select whether anonymous access to the Organisation Portal with this user is possible. This option is useful if you want to temporarily disable an entry point to the Organisation Portal instead of permanently removing it.

When you deactivate this option, the user-specific URL to access the Organisation Portal with this user is disabled. Additionally, in case of the Standard User (see below), the link to access the Organisation Portal on the ADOIT login page is not displayed and the menu entry Organisation Portal from the dropdown menu for scenario selection in ADOIT is disabled.

children.title: Repositories
children.summary: The Repositories tab lets you define fallback configurations for repositories used by authenticated users without user-specific Organisation Portal settings, including enabling fallback, selecting start models, and activating access.
children.content:
This tab lists all repositories. You can define a fallback configuration for each of these repositories. These fallback configurations are used when the option Activate repository fallback is activated.
• Activate repository fallback: Select this check box to enable a fallback mechanism for authenticated users with the system role 'Organisation Portal' that do NOT have a user-specific Organisation Portal configuration. When such users log on to ADOIT, a fallback configuration is used. This is useful in case of deployments where large numbers of users with the system role 'Organisation Portal' are automatically created but configuring them individually is not feasible.
• Start model: Here you can specify a start model that will appear on the Organisation Portal start page. Click Configure start model, and then choose the start model you want. If a start model has been selected for this fallback configuration already, it will be displayed here.
• Active: Select whether access to the Organisation Portal with this fallback configuration is possible. This option is useful if you want to temporarily disable an entry point to the Organisation Portal instead of permanently removing it.

children.title: Absence of Start Model
children.summary: If no start model is configured for the Organisation Portal, the start page omits the 'Home' section and instead displays the 'Architecture Diagrams' section as the default landing page.
children.content:
Explore the implications of not configuring a start model for the Organisation Portal. Read on for the details.

No Start Model Configured

When no start model has been configured for the Organisation Portal, the following applies:
• In the Organisation Portal, the appearance of the start page changes. The "Home" section with the start model is not displayed. Instead, the "Architecture Diagrams" section will appear as the start page.

children.title: Configure IP Restrictions for the Organisation Portal
children.summary: Configure IP restrictions for the Organisation Portal in ADOIT Administration under Authentication > More options > Security Settings > Org Portal IP Restrictions tab to optionally restrict allowed IP addresses.
children.content:
If you want to limit which IPs can access the Organisation Portal, you need to adapt the Security settings in the ADOIT Administration:
• Go to Authentication > More options, and then click Security Settings.
• Switch to the Org Portal IP Restrictions tab.

Adapt the following setting:
• Org Portal IP Restrictions: This setting is optional. You can restrict the IP addresses that are allowed to access the Organisation Portal (see Configure IP Restrictions for more information).

children.title: Property Filter
children.summary: Property filters control visibility of attributes and relations in editors, panes, reports, and comparisons, configurable per system role and scenario via Settings > Property Filter > General.
children.content:
Property filters control the visibility of properties (= attributes and relations) in the following areas:
• Tabular Editor
• Properties pane
• Reports
• Model Comparison

You can define different property filters for different system roles and scenarios.

Open Property Filter Settings

To open the property filter settings:
• Go to Settings > Property Filter > General.

children.title: Add and Configure Property Filter
children.summary: Add property filters by naming them, assigning display names, order, system roles, scenarios, and selecting visible properties or chapters; filters can be copied from existing configurations and visibility depends on combined role and scenario assignments.
children.content:
To add a new property filter:
1. Click the Add filter button.
2. In the Language independent name box, type a name for the property filter. This language-independent name uniquely identifies the filter.
3. In the Display name area, type a name for every language ADOIT supports. These names are visible on the user interface.
4. In the Order area, select the order of the entries when a user selects a property filter in ADOIT.
5. In the System role assignment area, select the system roles to which you want to assign this filter.
6. In the Scenario assignment area, select the scenarios to which you want to assign this filter.
7. On the Model types, Classes and Relation classes tabs, select the properties which should be visible when a property filter is active. You can also select entire chapters (into which the properties are organised) or even all properties at once.
8. Click Add filter, and then click Save. The new property filter is added and the component settings are saved.

Optionally you can also:
• Select an existing configuration as a template for your new property filter. On the General page, in the Property filters area, find the filter you want to use. To the right of the property filter, click More, and then click Copy.

System Role Assignment and Scenario Assignment - Filter Visibility

You can combine system role assignments and scenario assignments. A property filter is only visible if all conditions are met (logical AND operator).

children.title: Edit or Delete Property Filter
children.summary: Edit or delete existing property filters from the General page by selecting the filter and choosing Edit filter or Delete to adjust visibility settings or remove filters.
children.content:
You can edit property filters to fine-tune them, and delete property filters you no longer need:
• On the General page, in the Property filters area, find the filter you want. To the right of the property filter, click More, and then click Edit filter or Delete.

children.title: Settings per Scenario
children.summary: Configure default property filters globally or per scenario, enabling options like 'Show All' and 'Hide Empty Attributes' filters, with scenario-specific defaults overriding global settings upon scenario switch.
children.content:
In this section, you can configure which property filter should be enabled by default in ADOIT. You have the option to set the default filter for all scenarios ("Global") and to define different default filters for specific scenarios as needed.

Global

On the "Global" tab, you can define the default filter for all scenarios. The following settings are available:
• Default filter: Select which property filter should be enabled by default. If a user does not have access to the selected filter, the first filter on the list is activated, then the second filter and so on.
• Enable 'Show All' Filter: Select this option box to make the Show all filter available to all users. When the Show all filter is active, all properties are visible.
• Enable 'Hide empty attributes' filter in Properties in 'read mode': Select this option to make the Hide Empty Attributes filter available to all users. When the Hide Empty Attributes filter is active, no empty properties are visible in read mode.

Scenario-Specific Filter Settings

On the tabs for individual scenarios such as "Read & Explore" or "Design & Document", you can define scenario-specific filter settings. The following settings are available:
• Use default settings: Clear this option to enable scenario-specific filter settings.
• Default filter: Select which property filter should be enabled by default in this scenario.

note

When a filter is defined as default for a scenario, switching to this scenario will always set this default filter, no matter which filter was active before.

• Enable 'Show All' Filter: Select this option to make the Show all filter available to all users in this scenario.

children.title: Read & Explore Scenario
children.summary: The Read & Explore scenario is a read-only mode for quick architecture overview, configurable via Settings > Read & Explore Scenario > General to allow user personalization and define repository-specific start content as models or dashboards.
children.content:
The Read & Explore scenario is a read-only scenario in ADOIT where users can get a quick overview of architecture artefacts. You can configure various settings for this scenario.

Open Read & Explore Scenario Settings

To open the Read & Explore scenario settings:
1. Go to Settings > Read & Explore Scenario > General.

General settings

The following settings are available:
• Allow users to personalise the start content: Select this check box so that users can set their own start content (model or dashboard) for the "Read & Explore" start page.

Select start content per repository

Here you can specify a start content that will appear on the "Read & Explore" scenario start page. You can define a configuration for each repository.

The following settings are available:
• + Select repository: Choose the repository for which a start content should be set up.
• Enable start content: Select whether a start content will be displayed.
• Model / Dashboard: If Enable start content is activated, choose whether you want to set a model or a dashboard as the starting page.
• + Select: Click this button to select the specific model or dashboard you want to display.

children.title: SCIM Services
children.summary: ADOIT supports SCIM 2.0 for user lifecycle management via REST API, requiring REST API license component and setup steps including creating technical users, editing system settings, and configuring authentication methods; documentation and Microsoft Entra ID provisioning guides are available.
children.content:
ADOIT supports user lifecycle management (ULM) via SCIM. This standard REST protocol lets external systems automatically handle user and user group setup, updates, and removal in ADOIT, following the SCIM 2.0 standard.

note

To use SCIM services, your license must include the REST API component.

Activate Access to the SCIM Services

Instructions on how to activate access to the SCIM services are covered here in the Administration Help.

You must first perform the following steps:
• Create Technical User (required for OAuth 2.0 using the Client Credentials Flow and token based authentication only)
• Edit System Settings
• Configure General SCIM Settings

Then you can configure the authentication method you want to use to communicate with the SCIM services:
• Configure Basic Authentication
• Configure OAuth 2.0 Authentication
• Configure OIDC Authentication
• Configure JWT Authentication
• Configure Token Based Authentication

These steps are explained in the following sections.

Use the SCIM Services

For information on how to use the SCIM services, please refer to the BOC Developer Portal, especially:
• SCIM 2.0
• SCIM API Reference

SCIM Provisioning Using Microsoft Entra ID

Looking to automate user lifecycle operations (creation, updates, deletion) between Microsoft Entra ID and ADOIT using SCIM? Explore our step-by-step guide:
• How-to: SCIM Provisioning with Microsoft Entra ID

More

Find extra resources to help you understand the SCIM implementation in ADOIT:
• SCIM Default User Group
• User Account for Provisioning

children.title: Create Technical User
children.summary: Create a technical user in ADOIT Administration for OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow or token-based authentication by defining user details, assigning to Default group, selecting repositories, enabling Trusted Login, and saving the user.
children.content:
Do you want to use OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Client Credentials Flow for authenticating requests to the SCIM API, or token based authentication? If yes, you need to create a technical user now.

note

A technical user is NOT required for the other authentication methods used with the SCIM API, so you can skip this step if you're using one of those methods.

To create the technical user in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to the Users page and click New User.
2. Begin by filling out the account details on the General tab:
• Enter a name for the technical user, e.g. "Technical_SCIMServices".
• Enter and confirm a password of your choice.
3. Next, go to the Groups and Roles tab:
• Under User groups, click Select user groups and assign the user to the Default group.
4. Next, go to the Repository tab:
• Click Select repository and assign all repositories to which users may be assigned by the SCIM API.
5. Click Create to complete the user creation process.
6. Once user creation is complete, you can enable trusted login for the user:
• Hover over the user, click More, and then select Edit.
• On the General tab, under Trusted login, select Enabled.

children.title: Edit System Settings
children.summary: Edit system settings in ADOIT Administration under Settings > System settings > System to set the Base URL and assign the technical user for OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow or token-based authentication before saving.
children.content:
Now you have to define a few technical settings controlling the base functionality of ADOIT in the ADOIT Administration. To edit the System settings:
1. Go to Settings > System settings > System.
2. The Base URL field must contain the URL where ADOIT can be reached from other machines.
3. Do you want to use OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Client Credentials Flow or token based authentication? If yes, click Select users and select the technical user you created, e.g. "Technical_SCIMServices" (see Create Technical User).
4. Click Save.

children.title: Configure General SCIM Settings
children.summary: Describes how to enable SCIM Services globally in ADOIT Administration under Settings > SCIM Services > General, including optional user creation defaults like user groups, system roles, repository assignments, object groups, and named user scenarios for newly provisioned users.
children.content:
Now the general settings for the SCIM services have to be adapted in the ADOIT Administration:
• Go to Settings > SCIM Services > General.
• Select Enable SCIM Services globally to activate the feature. All other settings in this area are inactive unless you select this option.
• Optional: Under User creation defaults, define baseline settings for newly provisioned users (see below).

Once done, you can configure the authentication method you want to use to communicate with the SCIM services.

User creation defaults

You can specify certain user groups, system roles and other properties that should apply to all users provisioned via SCIM. These defaults apply only when no specific assignments for these properties are provided in SCIM POST requests during first user provisioning.

Adapt the following settings:
• Enable user creation defaults: Enable or disable applying defaults to newly provisioned users.
• User groups: Define default user groups for provisioned users.
• System roles: Define default system roles for provisioned users.
• Repository: Select a repository and then choose one or both of the following options:
• Assign repository: Assign this repository to all provisioned users as their workspace.
• Share with repository: Share all provisioned users with this repository to make them available as objects in modelling in ADOIT.
• Object group: If Share with repository is selected, you can specify the object group in which the shared user objects should be placed.
• Named user: Define default scenarios that provisioned users with a named-user license are allowed to access.

children.title: Configure Basic Authentication
children.summary: Explains that basic authentication must be enabled in both SCIM Services and Security settings in ADOIT, noting it is simple and suitable mainly for test environments with SSL/TLS recommended for secure communication.
children.content:
You need to enable basic authentication in the SCIM Services settings (see Configure Settings for Basic Authentication) and in the Security settings (see Enable Basic Authentication for ADOIT).

note

Basic authentication is the simplest authentication method and may be suitable for test environments. Ensure SSL/TLS is enabled for secure communication.

children.title: Configure Settings for Basic Authentication
children.summary: Details enabling Basic Authentication for SCIM services by navigating to Settings > SCIM Services > General > Basic Auth and selecting Enable basic authentication.
children.content:
To enable Basic Authentication for SCIM services:
1. Go to Settings > SCIM Services > General > Basic Auth.
2. Select Enable basic authentication.

children.title: Enable Basic Authentication for ADOIT
children.summary: Outlines enabling Basic Authentication in ADOIT Security settings under Authentication > More options > Security Settings > SCIM tab, including configuring IP restrictions and optional system role restrictions without requiring a restart.
children.content:
For security reasons, basic authentication is turned off by default in ADOIT. If you want to use the SCIM Services with basic authentication, you need to adapt the Security settings in the ADOIT Administration:
• Go to Authentication > More options, and then click Security Settings.
• Switch to the SCIM tab.

Adapt the following settings:
• Basic Authentication IP Restrictions: Specify the IP addresses that shall be allowed to send requests with basic authentication to the SCIM API (see Configure IP Restrictions for more information).
• Basic Authentication Roles: This setting is optional. Select system roles that a user must have at least one of in order to use the SCIM API with basic authentication. If no system role is selected, all system roles will allow access to the API.

No restart is required when modifying these settings.

children.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 Authentication
children.summary: States that OAuth 2.0 authentication must be enabled in both SCIM Services and OAuth 2.0 settings in ADOIT, recommending OAuth 2.0 for secure enterprise provisioning and ensuring the IdP supports SCIM with OAuth.
children.content:
You need to enable OAuth 2.0 authentication in the SCIM Services settings (see Configure Settings for OAuth 2.0) and in the OAuth 2.0 settings (see Enable OAuth 2.0 for ADOIT).

note

OAuth 2.0 is a recommended method for secure automated provisioning in enterprise environments. Ensure the configured IdP supports SCIM with OAuth.

children.title: Configure Settings for OAuth 2.0
children.summary: Explains configuring OAuth 2.0 for SCIM services by enabling it under Settings > SCIM Services > General > OAuth 2.0, adding scopes for Client Credentials or Authorization Code Flow, defining scope names, IP constraints, and mapping scopes to technical users to control API access rights.
children.content:
To enable OAuth 2.0 authentication for SCIM services:
1. Go to Settings > SCIM Services > General > OAuth 2.0.
2. Select Enable OAuth 2.0.
3. Click Add scopes to configure access scopes, if needed (see below).

Scopes (Client Credentials Flow)

OAuth 2.0 offers multiple flows. ADOIT supports the Authorization Code Flow and the Client Credentials Flow.

Do you want to use the Client Credentials Flow? If yes, you need to define at least one scope:
• Add Scope: To add a new scope, click Add scopes.
• Edit or Delete Scope: To the right of the scope, click More, and then click Edit or Delete.

A scope consists of the following parts:
• No scope provided (optional)
• Name
• IP constraints (optional)
• Technical user

The technical user defines the effective access rights of the client: all API calls authenticated with this scope will run under the permissions of the selected technical user.

note

SCIM services support multiple scopes. In general, at least one scope is required. However, the optional "No scope provided" option allows ADOIT to accept tokens from clients using the Client Credentials Flow without sending a scope parameter.

When would you want to use multiple scopes? You can execute requests with access rights of different technical users or from different IP ranges. During execution, you can choose which of the predefined scopes should be used.

Let's take a detailed look at the settings:
• No scope provided: Select this option if you want to allow clients using the Client Credentials Flow to authenticate without sending a scope parameter in their token request. If enabled, such clients are mapped to the technical user defined in this configuration. If disabled, requests without a scope will fail with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

If you select No scope provided, the Name field is disabled because no scope identifier is required. Only one such scope can be created, as it serves as the global fallback for clients using the Client Credentials Flow without sending a scope parameter.
• Name: This parameter represents the name of the scope. Enter a descriptive name, e.g. "SCIM_FULL".
• IP constraints: This parameter is optional. You can restrict the IP addresses that shall be able to access a scope by passing an IP constraint pattern. Here's how the configuration works:
• An IP constraint consists of a comma separated list of rules.
• A rule consists of a keyword ('allow' or 'deny') followed by a white space, and an IP address or address with wild card * (e.g. 192.168. * ). The keyword "all" can be used to match all addresses.
• If rules are present, but no match is made, the default setting is "deny".
• If no rules are present, the default setting is "allow".
• The first matching rule decides. E.g. when you formulate a constraint like "allow 192. * , deny 192.168.0.1", the 'deny' rule would have no effect, as that address matches the 'allow' rule already.

Example

Deny all IP addresses starting with 192., deny the IP address 193.168.0.1, allow all other IP addresses:

deny 192.*,deny 193.168.0.1,allow all

Allow all IP addresses starting with 178. except 178.6.6.6, deny all other IP addresses:

deny 178.6.6.6,allow 178.*

• Technical user: Select the technical user you created, e.g. "Technical_SCIMServices" (see Create Technical User). The permissions of this technical user determine the access rights granted to the client when using this scope.

children.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 for ADOIT
children.summary: Describes enabling OAuth 2.0 in ADOIT under Authentication > OAuth 2.0 by creating clients with parameters like type, ID, name, redirect URI, logo, token validity, first-party application setting, and secret, enabling SCIM API calls with OAuth 2.0 authentication.
children.content:
For security reasons, OAuth 2.0 authentication is turned off by default in ADOIT. If you want to use SCIM services with OAuth 2.0, you need to enable OAuth 2.0 and configure a client in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to Authentication > OAuth 2.0.
2. Select Enabled.
3. Click Create to add a new client. The Client box appears. Adapt the following parameters:
• Type: Select the client type. Confidential clients are e.g. centralized, server based applications, which are capable of securely storing client secrets. Public clients are e.g. purely client based applications and native apps which are not capable of securely storing client secrets.
• ID: The ID of the client system. Must be unique among the clients, should be kept simple as special characters need to be URL encoded.
• Name: The name of the client application. Will be shown on the user interface.
• Redirect URI: The URL of a redirect endpoint inside the client application which will be called by the authorization server when issuing an authorization code.

note

The Redirect URI is mandatory for the Authorization Code Flow but unused in the Client Credentials Flow. However, since the form requires a value, you can enter any valid placeholder URL (e.g., https://localhost/placeholder) for Client Credentials Flow integrations to proceed.

• Logo: Upload a logo to represent the client application. Will be shown on the user interface.
• Access token validity (seconds): The time in seconds how long an access token is valid until it expires. Default: 1800s = 30 minutes.
• Refresh token validity (seconds): The time in seconds how long a refresh token is valid until it expires. Default: 1209600s = 14 days.
• First-party application: If this option is enabled, authorization requests to this client are granted immediately if the user is already logged in, without showing a consent dialog. This setting is intended for applications that are owned and controlled by your organisation (first-party or public clients), where seamless access without repeated authorization is desired.
• Secret: The client secret used for authentication. For confidential clients, this field is enabled and mandatory. You can manually enter a value or click Generate to create a new one automatically. For public clients, the secret field is disabled and not required. These clients cannot securely store client secrets and use PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) to securely complete the authorization code flow.

Back on the OAuth 2.0 page, click Save. Now you can call the SCIM API with OAuth 2.0 authentication.

note

To test client requests, you can generate an access token to authenticate them (see "Generate Token" in the OAuth 2.0 section).

children.title: Configure OIDC Authentication
children.summary: Indicates that OIDC authentication requires enabling in SCIM Services and OIDC settings in ADOIT, noting OIDC is an identity layer on OAuth 2.0 suitable for scenarios needing identity tokens and requires compatible IdP configuration.
children.content:
You need to enable OIDC authentication in the SCIM Services settings (see Configure Settings for OIDC) and in the OIDC settings (see Enable OIDC for ADOIT).

note

OpenID Connect (OIDC) is an identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0 and is suitable for secure authentication scenarios where identity tokens are required. Ensure your Identity Provider supports OIDC and is correctly configured for SCIM integration.

children.title: Configure Settings for OIDC
children.summary: Instructs enabling OIDC authentication for SCIM services by selecting Enable OIDC under Settings > SCIM Services > General > OIDC.
children.content:
To enable OIDC authentication for SCIM services:
1. Go to Settings > SCIM Services > General > OIDC.
2. Select Enable OIDC.

children.title: Enable OIDC for ADOIT
children.summary: Details enabling OIDC in ADOIT under Authentication > OIDC by creating clients with settings including type, ID, name, redirect URI, logo, token validities, preauthorized scopes, first-party application option, and secret, allowing SCIM API calls with OIDC authentication.
children.content:
For security reasons, OIDC authentication is turned off by default in ADOIT. If you want to use SCIM services with OIDC, you need to enable OIDC and configure a client in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to Authentication > OIDC.
2. Select Enabled.
3. Click Create to add a new client. The Client box appears. Adapt the following parameters:
• Type: Select the client type. Confidential clients are, for example, server-based applications capable of securely storing secrets. Public clients include native apps or browser-based apps which cannot securely store secrets.
• ID: The unique identifier for the client application. Should be kept simple, as special characters must be URL encoded.
• Name: The display name of the client application. This name may be shown to users during login.
• Redirect URI: The redirect endpoint of the client application. This is where ADOIT will send the user after successful authentication, along with the authorization code.
• Logo: Optionally upload a logo to visually represent the client application in the user interface.
• Access token validity (seconds): The duration in seconds for which an access token remains valid. Default: 1800 seconds (30 minutes).
• Refresh token validity (seconds): The duration in seconds for which a refresh token remains valid. Default: 1209600 seconds (14 days).
• ID token validity (seconds): The duration in seconds for which an ID token remains valid. Default: 36000 seconds (10 hours).
• Preauthorized scopes: Select the scopes that should be automatically approved without requiring user interaction. Authorization requests containing only these scopes are granted immediately if the user is already logged in, without showing a consent dialog. Requests that include scopes not listed here will still require the user’s explicit consent. This setting is particularly useful in scenarios such as microfrontends, where seamless access without repeated authorization is desired.
• First-party application: If this option is enabled, authorization requests to this client are granted immediately if the user is already logged in, without showing a consent dialog. This setting is intended for applications that are owned and controlled by your organisation (first-party or public clients), where seamless access without repeated authorization is desired.
• Secret: The client secret used for authentication. For confidential clients, this field is enabled and mandatory. You can manually enter a value or click Generate to create a new one automatically. For public clients, the secret field is disabled and not required. These clients cannot securely store client secrets and use PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) to securely complete the authorization code flow.

Back on the OIDC page, click Save. Now you can call the SCIM API with OIDC authentication.

note

To test client requests, you can generate an access token to authenticate them and an identity token that provides information about the authenticated user (see "Generate Token" in the OIDC section).

children.title: Configure JWT Authentication
children.summary: States that JWT authentication must be enabled in SCIM Services and JWT (REST) settings in ADOIT, highlighting JWT as a secure modern method for integration with external IdPs issuing signed tokens.
children.content:
You need to enable JWT authentication in the SCIM Services settings (see Configure Settings for JWT Authentication) and in the JWT (REST) settings (see Enable JWT Authentication for ADOIT).

note

JWT authentication is a secure and modern authentication method suitable for integration with external identity providers that issue signed tokens.

children.title: Configure Settings for JWT Authentication
children.summary: Explains enabling JWT authentication for SCIM services by selecting Enable JWT under Settings > SCIM Services > General > JWT.
children.content:
To configure JWT authentication for SCIM services:
1. Go to Settings > SCIM Services > General > JWT.
2. Select Enable JWT.

children.title: Enable JWT Authentication for ADOIT
children.summary: Describes enabling JWT authentication in ADOIT under Authentication > JWT by creating configurations specifying name, claim validations (issuer, audience), signature validations (HMAC secret, JWKS URI, OIDC URI, RSA/ECDSA keys), and user mapping claim matching ADOIT usernames with Trusted Login, enabling SCIM API calls with Bearer tokens.
children.content:
For security reasons, JWT authentication is turned off by default in ADOIT. To configure the SCIM API to accept a JSON Web Token (JWT) from an Identity Provider (IdP) for authentication, you need to adjust settings in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to Authentication > JWT.
2. Select Enabled.
3. Click Create to add a new configuration. The Create JWT configuration box appears. Edit the properties to match your token:

: Name

Represents the identifier of this configuration.

: Claim validation

A set of claims that need to be contained in the payload of the token. The "iss" (issuer)claim identifies the JWT issuer (required). The "aud" (audience) claim identifies theintended recipient of the token (optional).

: Signature validation

A set of parameters that can be used for JWT signature validation. Which of these parametersis required depends on the algorithm used to generate the signature in the header of thetoken. At least one parameter needs to be configured.

• HMAC shared secret: Base64 encoded shared secret. Used in HS256, HS384 and HS512 signing algorithms.
• JWKS URI: URL of the authorization server's JWK set, it contains the signing key(s) the client should use to validate signatures from the authorization server.
• OIDC URI: URL of the OpenID Connect metadata provider as it is specified in OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0.
• RSA public key: Base64 encoded public key. Used in RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384 and PS512 signing algorithms.
• ECDSA public key: Base64 encoded public key. Used in ES256, ES384 and ES512 signing algorithms.

: User mapping claim

A claim that needs to be contained in the payload of the token. This claim identifies theuser you wish to authenticate. The value of this claim must match the *user name* of a userin ADOIT (must have *Trusted Login*).

Back on the JWT page, click Save. Now you can call the SCIM API with JWT authentication. Add your JWT to the authorization header, formatted as Bearer.

children.title: Configure Token Based Authentication
children.summary: Explains configuring token based authentication for SCIM services by defining one or more security contexts under Settings > SCIM Services > General > Tokens, each with a key, secret, and technical user to allow Java client applications to authenticate via tokens instead of username/password.
children.content:
To configure token based authentication for SCIM services:
1. Go to Settings > SCIM Services > General > Tokens.
2. Click Add context to define at least one security context (see below).

note

Token based authentication is a BOC Group proprietary authentication method which allows access to the SCIM API on behalf of a user by providing a token instead of a username and password. This authentication method is available for Java client applications only.

Define Security Context

You need to define at least one security context for token based authentication:
• Add Context: To add a new security context, click Add context.
• Edit or Delete Context: To the right of the security context, click More, and then click Editor Delete.

A security context consists of the following parts:
• key
• secret
• technical user

note

SCIM services support multiple security contexts. At least one security context is required.

When would you want to use multiple security contexts? You can execute requests with access rights of different technical users. During execution, you can choose which of the predefined security contexts should be used.

Let's take a detailed look at the settings:
• Key (for authentication by target system): This parameter represents the name of the key which is used for communication with the web application using authenticated REST APIs. Enter a descriptive name, e.g. "boc.rest.key.mfb.SCIMServices".
• Secret (for authentication by target system): This parameter represents the secret value of the key which is used for communication with the web application using authenticated REST APIs. Click Generate secret to generate the value of the key.
• Technical user: Select the technical user you created, i.e. "Technical_SCIMServices" (see Create Technical User).

children.title: How-to: SCIM Provisioning with Microsoft Entra ID
children.summary: Provides an overview guide for configuring automated SCIM user provisioning between ADOIT and Microsoft Entra ID, covering setup steps, SCIM-only user account behavior, combining SCIM with SAML, and user deletion strategies.
children.content:
This guide explains how to configure automated user provisioning in ADOIT via SCIM and Microsoft Entra ID. It focuses on the essential configuration steps in both systems and highlights how SCIM can be combined with SAML-based authentication for a seamless and secure user lifecycle.

The following sections walk you through the configuration of Microsoft Entra ID and ADOIT, describe the behaviour of SCIM-only user accounts, and outline best practices when using SCIM provisioning together with SAML authentication.
• Configuring ADOIT for SCIM
• Configuring Microsoft Entra ID for SCIM
• Understanding SCIM-Only User Accounts
• Optional: Using SAML + SCIM Together
• Soft Delete vs. Hard Delete of Users

children.title: Configuring ADOIT for SCIM
children.summary: Details configuring ADOIT for SCIM provisioning with Microsoft Entra ID by creating a technical user with appropriate rights, updating system settings including Base URL and OAuth 2.0 technical user selection, enabling SCIM services with optional user creation defaults, and configuring OAuth 2.0 with a scope allowing no scope parameter and creating a confidential OAuth 2.0 client for integration.
children.content:
To use Microsoft Entra ID as a SCIM Identity Provider, ADOIT must be configured to accept SCIM requests authenticated via OAuth 2.0 using the Client Credentials Flow.

note

The following steps describe the required configuration in ADOIT at a general level. Detailed explanations of each setting can be found in the linked sections.

Create Technical User

First, create a technical user in ADOIT as described in Create Technical User. This user will execute all SCIM requests coming from Microsoft Entra ID.
• Create a dedicated user, for example Technical_SCIMServices.
• If groups will be provisioned, assign Global Administrator rights to the technical user (see Configure Global Administrators). These rights are required to create top level user groups in ADOIT during SCIM group provisioning.

Edit System Settings

Next, update the system settings as explained in Edit System Settings. These settings ensure that ADOIT can be reached by Microsoft Entra ID and that the technical user is used for OAuth 2.0 authentication.
• Ensure that the Base URL is configured correctly.
• Because the integration uses OAuth 2.0 with the Client Credentials Flow, the technical user must be selected in the system settings.

Configure General SCIM Settings

Enable SCIM Services as described in Configure General SCIM Settings. Once enabled, the SCIM endpoints of ADOIT become available for Microsoft Entra ID.
• Optionally define User creation defaults (default user groups, system roles, repository settings) for SCIM-provisioned users. This is particularly important in SCIM-only scenarios where SCIM provisioning is not used together with SAML authentication. In such cases, no SAML claims are available to assign user groups and more in ADOIT, so predefined defaults become essential to reduce manual administrative efforts.

Configure OAuth 2.0 Authentication

Configure OAuth 2.0 in ADOIT as described in Configure OAuth 2.0 Authentication. Only this authentication method is supported for SCIM provisioning using Entra. This includes two configuration areas:
• When configuring the OAuth 2.0 settings, create a scope with No scope provided selected and map it to the technical user. This is required because Microsoft Entra ID does not send a scope parameter when using the Client Credentials Flow.
• To enable OAuth 2.0 for ADOIT, create a confidential OAuth 2.0 client. The generated values are required in Microsoft Entra ID:
• ID of the OAuth 2.0 client (e.g. ME-ID).
• Secret of the OAuth 2.0 client.

Now you can begin configuring Microsoft Entra ID.

children.title: Configuring Microsoft Entra ID for SCIM
children.summary: Describes configuring Microsoft Entra ID for SCIM provisioning to ADOIT by creating a non-gallery enterprise app, setting up OAuth 2.0 client credentials provisioning with ADOIT endpoints and client credentials, defining user and group attribute mappings aligned with ADOIT expectations, assigning users/groups for provisioning, and enabling on-demand and automatic provisioning with periodic delta syncs.
children.content:
To provision users and groups from Microsoft Entra ID into ADOIT via SCIM, you must create a non-gallery enterprise app, configure an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials provisioning setup, and define the attribute mappings that ADOIT expects to receive. These steps are explained in the following sections.

Prerequisites

Before configuring provisioning in Microsoft Entra ID, ensure that you have already created an OAuth 2.0 client in ADOIT and that the following values are available:
• The ID of the OAuth 2.0 client configured in ADOIT.
• The corresponding Secret of the OAuth 2.0 client.
• The HTTPS Base URL of your ADOIT installation, used to construct the SCIM endpoint and the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint.

Sign in to Microsoft Entra ID

To get started, sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center using an administrator account with permissions to create and manage enterprise applications.

Create the Enterprise Application

To integrate ADOIT with Microsoft Entra ID, you need to create an application within the Microsoft Entra admin center:
1. Go to Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications.
2. Select + New application and then + Create your own application.
3. In the Input name box, enter the name of your application (for example ADOIT).
4. Select Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery).
5. Click Create.

Create the Provisioning Configuration

After creating the application within the Microsoft Entra admin center, you'll need to create a provisioning configuration:
1. On the application’s Overview page, select Provisioning.
2. Select + New configuration.
3. Under Select authentication method, choose OAuth2 client credentials grant.
4. For Tenant URL, enter the SCIM endpoint of ADOIT: https://<base-url>/scim/2.0.
5. For Token endpoint, enter the OAuth 2.0 token URL of ADOIT: https://<base-url>/oauth2/token.
6. For Client identifier, enter the ID of the OAuth 2.0 client created in ADOIT.
7. For Client secret, enter the corresponding Secret of the OAuth 2.0 client.
8. Click Test connection. If successful, select Create to create the provisioning job.

Configure Attribute Mappings for Users

Next, define the user attributes that will be sent from Microsoft Entra ID to ADOIT. Only the attributes required by ADOIT should be configured:
1. On the Provisioning page, select Attribute mapping.
2. Select Provision Microsoft Entra ID Users.
3. Delete all existing attribute mappings except userName.
4. Select Show advanced options and then Edit attribute list for customappsso.
5. Add the following attributes and click Save:
• String: FORENAME, SURNAME, EMAIL
• Boolean: ACCOUNT_DISABLED
6. Back in the mapping list, select Edit for each attribute and adapt the following parameters:
• Map a Microsoft Entra ID attribute (Source attribute) to the corresponding ADOIT attribute (Target attribute).
• For newly added attributes, set Match objects using this attribute to No because the only possible matching is based on userName.
• Leave the remaining settings as they are.

The recommended mapping for user attributes is:
customappsso Attribute (= Target attribute) | Microsoft Entra ID Attribute (= Source attribute) | Matching precedence | Notes
userName | userPrincipalName | 1 | Unique identifier and login name in ADOIT
ACCOUNT_DISABLED | IsSoftDeleted | | Prevents false positives in PATCH requests
FORENAME | givenName | | First name
SURNAME | surname | | Last name
EMAIL | mail | | Email address

Change the source attributes if the defined attributes do not match those used in your organisation.

Configure Attribute Mappings for Groups

To ensure consistent provisioning behavior, the group attributes sent from Microsoft Entra ID must align with the attribute expectations of ADOIT:
1. Return to the Attribute mapping page.
2. Select Provision Microsoft Entra ID Groups.
3. Delete the attribute mapping externalId (not supported by ADOIT).

The recommended mapping for group attributes is:
customappsso Attribute | Microsoft Entra ID Attribute | Matching precedence | Notes
displayName | displayName | 1 | Group name; ensure uniqueness among sibling groups in ADOIT.
members | members | | Group’s member list

Assign Users and Groups

Next, assign the users or groups you want to synchronize:
1. On the Provisioning page, select Users and groups.
2. Select + Add user/group and assign all users and groups that should be provisioned to ADOIT.

Provisioning and Rollout

After completing the configuration, you can validate the setup using on-demand provisioning before enabling automatic provisioning for all assigned users and groups.

Provision Users or Groups On-Demand
1. On the application’s Overview page, select Provisioning.
2. Select Provision on demand.
3. In the Select a user or group box, search for a user or group.
4. Click Provision.

Review the provisioning logs to confirm that the user or group was created or updated successfully in ADOIT. If the on-demand provisioning succeeds, you can enable automatic provisioning.

Enable Automatic Provisioning
1. On the application’s Overview page, select Provisioning.
2. Select Provisioning.
3. Set Provisioning mode to Automatic.
4. Change the Provisioning Status to On.
5. Click Save to activate the provisioning process.

Microsoft Entra ID will now perform periodic delta synchronizations.

children.title: Understanding SCIM-Only User Accounts
children.summary: Explains SCIM-only user accounts provisioned via Microsoft Entra ID to ADOIT are authenticated locally without SAML, initially have no password requiring manual or user-set passwords, and recommends defining user creation defaults to assign access rights and manage group provisioning carefully to avoid importing undesired groups.
children.content:
This section outlines what to expect when users are provisioned between Microsoft Entra ID and ADOIT through SCIM only. While many organisations pair SCIM with SAML for a full identity solution, it is also possible to use SCIM independently. In this "SCIM-only" scenario, Microsoft Entra ID handles the lifecycle operations (creation, updates, deactivation), but it does not perform the authentication handshake.

Essentially, a SCIM-only account is provisioned automatically but authenticated locally within ADOIT. This means that while an employee’s account will appear automatically, they will use the standard username/password login flow rather than a one-click SSO experience. Because SAML is absent, users provisioned this way will rely on local credentials to access ADOIT.

SCIM-Created Users Have No Initial Password

Microsoft Entra ID does not send passwords via SCIM. Consequently, when an account is first provisioned in ADOIT, it does not possess a local password.
• Users cannot log in until a local password is established.
• Administrators can set a password manually on the Users page (see Edit User).
• Recommended approach: Users can set their own password via the "Forgot Password?" link on the login page. This ensures security and reduces administrative overhead.

Provisioning Strategy: Users and Groups

When using SCIM without SAML, user data is supplied exclusively through SCIM. In such scenarios, defining sensible defaults becomes essential to avoid manual adjustments for every new account.
• SCIM can provision users alone, or users together with their corresponding Entra ID groups.
• User creation defaults (e.g., default user groups, system roles, and repository assignments) are strongly recommended. Without these defaults, newly provisioned users will lack the necessary access rights at their first login.
• It may be preferable to provision users only and allow ADOIT to assign default groups. This avoids importing technical or non-descriptive Entra ID groups.
• If group provisioning is desired, a global administrator must perform SCIM requests (see Configuring ADOIT for SCIM).

children.title: Optional: Using SAML + SCIM Together
children.summary: This section explains how to combine SCIM provisioning with SAML-based SSO in ADOIT using a single Microsoft Entra ID application, detailing alignment of login identifiers, attribute sources, group management approaches, user assignment requirements, and how SAML resolves password issues for SCIM-created users.
children.content:
Organisations can combine SCIM provisioning with SAML-based Single Sign-On (SSO) to achieve a complete identity management setup between Microsoft Entra ID and ADOIT. In such scenarios, SCIM handles user lifecycle operations (creation, updates, deactivation), while SAML performs the actual authentication.

When SCIM and SAML are used together, users are created and kept up to date via SCIM, but log in through the organisation’s standard SAML SSO process. This provides the advantages of automated user provisioning combined with a seamless authentication experience. To ensure a smooth integration, SCIM and SAML must follow a few alignment rules regarding identifiers, user attributes and group management.

note

This section builds on the information provided in the ADOIT SAML Guide. For detailed, step-by-step instructions on configuring SAML between Microsoft Entra ID and ADOIT, please refer to that guide.

Because SCIM and SAML integrations can become complex when combined, it is advisable to collaborate with an ADOIT consultant and confirm the setup before starting.

Use a Single Microsoft Entra ID Application

Microsoft Entra ID allows a single enterprise application to be used for both SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. This means that if you have already created an application for SCIM, you do not need to create a second one for SAML integration.
• One Entra ID application can manage both authentication (SAML) and provisioning (SCIM).
• This reduces configuration effort and avoids duplicated application objects.
• All relevant settings (SAML claims, certificates, SCIM configuration) are managed centrally.

Align Login Identifiers

For SCIM provisioning and SAML authentication to work together reliably, both must use the same unique login identifier.
• In SCIM, this identifier is the userName attribute, which determines how user accounts are created and matched in ADOIT.
• In SAML, ADOIT does not use the NameID element for identification. Instead, it expects a specific claim (by default the name claim) to contain the user’s login identifier.
• To ensure consistent identity matching, configure Microsoft Entra ID so that the same directory attribute (typically userPrincipalName) is used as the value for both the SAML name claim and the SCIM userName attribute.

Avoid Duplicate Attribute Sources

When SCIM and SAML are combined, SCIM should be the authoritative source for user attributes such as first name, last name and email. The ADOIT SAML Guide shows how such attributes can be sent via SAML claims (see Set Up SAML SSO), but they are not needed in this scenario because SCIM already provides them reliably.
• Do not send first name, last name or email as SAML claims when SCIM is enabled.
• SCIM supplies the FORENAME, SURNAME and EMAIL attributes.
• Keep SAML claims minimal and focused on authentication and (optionally) group membership.

Combining SCIM and SAML for Group Management

Both SCIM and SAML can supply group information to ADOIT. The ADOIT SAML Guide explains how SAML group claims can be emitted from Microsoft Entra ID (see Set Up SAML SSO). Depending on your organisational structure, you may choose one of the following approaches:
• SCIM-only groups: Synchronise directory groups into ADOIT via SCIM.
• SAML-only group claims: Let SAML supply group membership information without provisioning groups in ADOIT.
• Hybrid approach: Use SCIM User creation defaults to assign baseline permissions and rely on SAML group claims for additional access control. This avoids importing technical or non-descriptive groups into ADOIT.

User Assignment Requirement

The Assignment required? property for Microsoft Entra ID applications affects both login and provisioning behaviour. The ADOIT SAML Guide describes this setting in detail (see Disable User Assignment Requirement).
• For SCIM provisioning, it is recommended to set Assignment required? to Yes, ensuring that only assigned users and groups are provisioned into ADOIT.
• For SAML authentication, organisations may set Assignment required? to No so that any directory user can sign in via SSO.
• When using SCIM and SAML together, keep required assignment enabled (Yes).

SAML Solves the Password Issue

As SCIM-created users in ADOIT have no local password, SAML authentication fully solves the login limitation described in Understanding SCIM-Only User Accounts:
• With SAML enabled, users authenticate externally, and ADOIT receives a trusted login assertion from Microsoft Entra ID. No local password is required for login.
• If a password was already set by an administrator before the first SAML login, it becomes inactive while the user account in ADOIT is automatically converted from a standard ADOIT user into a system user with trusted login enabled, allowing external authentication and enabling quick access to ADOIT via SAML SSO.

children.title: Soft Delete vs. Hard Delete of Users
children.summary: Describes SCIM's soft delete and hard delete behaviors in ADOIT when integrated with Microsoft Entra ID, where soft delete deactivates user accounts without removal, and hard delete permanently removes users causing broken references if they were assigned in models or objects.
children.content:
SCIM defines two different behaviors for removing users: soft delete and hard delete. When SCIM provisioning with Microsoft Entra ID is enabled in ADOIT, these behaviours are applied as follows:
Entra Action | How SCIM Interprets It | ADOIT Action
The user is deleted in Entra and moved to the recycle bin (where it can be recovered for 30 days), or the user is unassigned from the ADOIT enterprise application in Entra. | Soft Delete | If the ADOIT attribute ACCOUNT_DISABLED is mapped to Entra’s isSoftDeleted, the user account is deactivated in ADOIT. The user account remains, but login is disabled.
The user is permanently deleted from the Entra recycle bin. | Hard Delete | ADOIT removes the user entirely from the system. If the user was referenced in models or objects (e.g., assigned as a responsible person), these references will no longer have a valid target and become broken references (icon ).

children.title: More
children.summary: Introduces the topics covered in the following sections: SCIM Default User Group and User Account for Provisioning.
children.content:
In this section:
• SCIM Default User Group
• User Account for Provisioning

children.title: SCIM Default User Group
children.summary: Details the SCIM Default User Group in ADOIT, which automatically receives users provisioned without group info and serves as a fallback group when users lose all group memberships during provisioning, requiring provisioning users to have permissions for this group.
children.content:
A special user group in ADOIT supports user provisioning: the SCIM Default User Group.
• This group is created automatically when the Enable SCIM Services globally option is activated (see Activate Access to the SCIM Services) and the ADOIT application server is restarted.
• When users are provisioned from an Identity Provider (IdP) into ADOIT without group information, they are placed in this group. If group information is provided in a later provisioning, the user's group membership is updated accordingly.
• If a user is removed from their last group during provisioning, they are moved to the SCIM Default User Group.
• The user executing the provisioning must have permissions for the SCIM Default User Group (see User Account for Provisioning).

children.title: User Account for Provisioning
children.summary: Specifies requirements for the ADOIT user account executing SCIM requests, including necessary write permissions for relevant user groups and how the user context depends on the configured authentication method such as Basic Auth, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT, or Token-Based Authentication.
children.content:
The user account in ADOIT under whose context SCIM requests are executed must meet specific requirements:
• The user must have Write permissions for the SCIM Default User Group and any other user groups to which users are provisioned in ADOIT.
• These permissions can be assigned by a ADOIT administrator in the ADOIT Administration, on the Rights page under the Users tab (see View or Change Permissions).

The user context for executing SCIM requests depends on the configured authentication method:
• Basic Authentication: The user whose username and password are sent Base64-encoded in the HTTP authorization header.
• OAuth 2.0 Authentication
• Authorization Code Flow: The user who authenticated and issued the access token.
• Client Credentials Flow: The technical user associated with the configured scope.
• OIDC Authentication: The user who authenticated and issued the access token.
• JWT Authentication: The user identified via the claim (e.g., sub) in the validated JWT token.
• Token-Based Authentication: The technical user associated with the configured key and secret.

children.title: REST API
children.summary: Describes ADOIT's generic REST API for authenticated data queries, noting license-dependent availability and request limits, and outlines prerequisite steps and authentication methods configuration covered in subsequent sections, with usage details available in the BOC Developer Portal.
children.content:
ADOIT offers a generic, extensible REST API that allows authenticated access to exposed functionality. The REST API can be used to e.g. send GET requests to query ADOIT for data.

note

The availability of this feature depends on the licence. Access to the application programming interface (API) is limited to 500 requests per hour.

Activate Access to the REST API

Instructions on how to activate access to the REST API are covered here in the Administration Help.

You must first perform the following steps:
• Create Technical User (required for OAuth 2.0 using the Client Credentials Flow and token based authentication only)
• Assign Access Rights to the ADOIT Administration
• Edit System Settings
• Configure General Settings

Then you can configure the authentication method you want to use to communicate with the REST API:
• Configure Basic Authentication
• Configure OAuth 2.0 Authentication
• Configure OIDC Authentication
• Configure JWT Authentication
• Configure Token Based Authentication

These steps are explained in the following sections.

note

Need help deciding on a suitable authentication method? Check out Choosing an Authentication Method for a short overview of each method.

Use the REST API

For information on how to use the REST API, please refer to the BOC Developer Portal.

children.title: Create Technical User
children.summary: Explains how to create a technical user in ADOIT Administration for OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow or token-based authentication, including setting account details, group assignments, repository access, and enabling trusted login.
children.content:
Do you want to use OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Client Credentials Flow to authenticate requests to the REST API, or token based authentication? If yes, you need to create a technical user now.

note

A technical user is NOT necessary for basic authentication, OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Authorization Code Flow and JWT authentication.

To create the technical user in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to the Users page and click New User.
2. Begin by filling out the account details on the General tab:
• Enter a name for the technical user, e.g. "Technical_StandardRESTfulServices".
• Enter and confirm a password of your choice.
3. Next, go to the Groups and roles tab:
• Under User groups, click Select user groups and assign the user to the Default group.
4. Next, go to the Repository tab:
• Click Select repository and only (!) assign the repository to the user which holds the data to be queried.
5. Click Create to complete the user creation process.
6. Once user creation is complete, you can enable trusted login for the user:
• Hover over the user, click More, and then select Edit.
• On the General tab, under Trusted login, select Enabled.

children.title: Assign Access Rights to the ADOIT Administration
children.summary: Guides assigning access rights to the ADOIT Administration for users or technical users to enable user write API operations, detailing navigation and permission settings.
children.content:
If you want to use user write APIs, you must assign access rights to the ADOIT Administration to the user in whose context requests should be executed.

note

This can either be the technical user (for OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Client Credentials Flow and token based authentication) or any ADOIT user (for basic authentication, OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Authorization Code Flow and JWT authentication).

To assign access rights to the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to the Rights page.
2. In the Users / Groups catalogue on the left, select the user to whom you want to grant access rights to the ADOIT Administration.
3. Go to the Components tab.
4. In the workspace, find the "Administration Toolkit" component.
5. In the Access column, click Change Permissions, and then choose Access.

children.title: Edit System Settings
children.summary: Instructs editing ADOIT System settings to define the Base URL and assign the technical user for OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow or token-based authentication before saving changes.
children.content:
Now you have to define a few technical settings controlling the base functionality of ADOIT in the ADOIT Administration. To edit the System settings:
1. Go to Settings > System settings > System.
2. The Base URL field must contain the URL where ADOIT can be reached from other machines.
3. Do you want to use OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Client Credentials Flow or token based authentication? If yes, click Select users and select the technical user you created, e.g. "Technical_StandardRESTfulServices" (see Create Technical User).
4. Click Save.

children.title: Configure General Settings
children.summary: Covers configuring general REST API settings in ADOIT Administration, including enabling the REST API globally, optional cache path for performance optimization, enabling response validation, and toggling HATEOAS links in responses.
children.content:
Now the general settings for the REST API have to be adapted in the ADOIT Administration:
• Go to Settings > Standard RESTful Services > General.

These settings apply to all authentication methods:
• Enable Standard RESTful Services globally: Select this option to enable the REST API. All other settings in this area are inactive unless you select this option.
• Cache Path: This parameter is optional. Enter the absolute path to the directory in which cache files must be stored. The user under which the web server is running must have write access to this directory. If the directory does not exist, it will be created by ADOIT.

note

Advantages of using the Cache Path parameter:

Model images and model image maps are generated only once and then cached. Every time the model image or image map is requested, a check is performed if the model has changed. If there are no changes, the information is loaded from the file system. Otherwise, the cache is updated first. As a result, responses to these types of requests are faster and use fewer server resources.

For search jobs the advantage is that created queries are saved in cache files and can be reused after a server restart. Without the cache path, queries are saved only in memory and are lost during restart.

• Enable Validator: This parameter is optional. Select this option to turn on syntax and semantic validation of XML and JSON responses. Enabling this parameter may slow down the execution of requests and cause high memory consumption and CPU usage on the web server.
• Enable HATEOAS links: This parameter is enabled by default. When you clear this option, responses to requests will not include HATEOAS links that help you find related resources.

children.title: Configure Basic Authentication
children.summary: States that enabling basic authentication for the REST API requires activation in both Standard RESTful Services and Security settings within ADOIT Administration.
children.content: You need to enable basic authentication in the Standard RESTful Services settings (see Configure Settings for Basic Authentication) and in the Security settings (see Enable Basic Authentication for ADOIT).

children.title: Configure Settings for Basic Authentication
children.summary: Details configuring basic authentication settings for the REST API in ADOIT Administration, including enabling basic auth and selecting enabled REST scenarios which control endpoint accessibility and related HATEOAS links.
children.content:
To configure basic authentication for the REST API in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to Settings > Standard RESTful Services > General.
2. Edit the settings on the Basic Auth tab.

The following settings are available:
• Enable Basic Authentication: Select this option to enable basic authentication. All other settings in this tab are inactive unless you select this option.
• Repository scenarios | Users scenarios | Metamodel scenarios: In this area, you can enable specific REST scenarios. If a scenario is not enabled, all requests to its endpoints will return a 403 FORBIDDEN status. HATEOAS links that help you find related resources are also affected. For example, the response to a request to get user information may contain a HATEOAS link to delete the user. If the user write APIs scenario is disabled, a request to this link will return the status code 403 FORBIDDEN.

note

To find out which endpoints are assigned to the REST scenarios, see the API Reference in the BOC Developer Portal where they are grouped according to the scenarios.

children.title: Enable Basic Authentication for ADOIT
children.summary: Explains enabling basic authentication in ADOIT's Security settings, including configuring IP restrictions and optional role-based access controls for REST API usage without requiring a restart.
children.content:
For security reasons, basic authentication is turned off by default in ADOIT. If you want to use the REST API with basic authentication, you need to adapt the Security settings in the ADOIT Administration:
• Go to Authentication > More options, and then click Security Settings.
• Switch to the REST tab.

Adapt the following settings:
• Basic Authentication IP Restrictions: Specify the IP addresses that shall be allowed to send requests with basic authentication to the REST API (see Configure IP Restrictions for more information).
• Basic Authentication Roles: This setting is optional. Select system roles that a user must have at least one of in order to use the ADOIT REST API with basic authentication. If no system role is selected, all system roles will allow access to the API.

No restart is required when modifying these settings.

children.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 Authentication
children.summary: Indicates that enabling OAuth 2.0 authentication for the REST API requires configuration in both Standard RESTful Services and OAuth 2.0 settings in ADOIT Administration.
children.content: You need to enable OAuth 2.0 authentication in the Standard RESTful Services settings (see Configure Settings for OAuth 2.0) and in the OAuth 2.0 settings (see Enable OAuth 2.0 for ADOIT).

children.title: Configure Settings for OAuth 2.0
children.summary: Describes configuring OAuth 2.0 authentication for the REST API in ADOIT Administration, including enabling OAuth 2.0, selecting REST scenarios, and defining scopes for Client Credentials Flow with options for IP constraints and associated technical users.
children.content:
To configure OAuth 2.0 authentication for the REST API in the ADOIT Administration:
1. Go to Settings > Standard RESTful Services > General.
2. Edit the settings on the OAuth 2.0 tab.

The following settings are available:
• Enable OAuth 2.0: Select this option to enable OAuth 2.0 authentication. All other settings in this tab are inactive unless you select this option.
• Repository scenarios | Users scenarios | Metamodel scenarios: In this area, you can enable specific REST scenarios. If a scenario is not enabled, all requests to its endpoints will return a 403 FORBIDDEN status. HATEOAS links that help you find related resources are also affected. For example, the response to a request to get user information may contain a HATEOAS link to delete the user. If the user write APIs scenario is disabled, a request to this link will return the status code 403 FORBIDDEN.

note

To find out which endpoints are assigned to the REST scenarios, see the API Reference in the BOC Developer Portal where they are grouped according to the scenarios.

Scopes (Client Credentials Flow)

OAuth 2.0 offers multiple flows. ADOIT supports the Authorization Code Flow and the Client Credentials Flow.

Do you want to use the Client Credentials Flow? If yes, you need to define at least one scope:
• Add Scope: To add a new scope, click Add scopes.
• Edit or Delete Scope: To the right of the scope, click More, and then click Edit or Delete.

A scope consists of the following parts:
• No scope provided (optional)
• Name
• IP constraints (optional)
• Technical user

The technical user defines the effective access rights of the client: all API calls authenticated with this scope will run under the permissions of the selected technical user.

note

ADOIT RESTful services support multiple scopes. In general, at least one scope is required. However, the optional "No scope provided" option allows ADOIT to accept tokens from clients using the Client Credentials Flow without sending a scope parameter.

When would you want to use multiple scopes? You can execute requests with access rights of different technical users or from different IP ranges. During execution, you can choose which of the predefined scopes should be used.

Let's take a detailed look at the settings:
• No scope provided: Select this option if you want to allow clients using the Client Credentials Flow to authenticate without sending a scope parameter in their token request. If enabled, such clients are mapped to the technical user defined in this configuration. If disabled, requests without a scope will fail with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

If you select No scope provided, the Name field is disabled because no scope identifier is required. Only one such scope can be created, as it serves as the global fallback for clients using the Client Credentials Flow without sending a scope parameter.
• Name: This parameter represents the name of the scope. Enter a descriptive name, e.g. "REST_READ".
• IP constraints: This parameter is optional. You can restrict the IP addresses that shall be able to access a scope by passing an IP constraint pattern. Here's how the configuration works:
• An IP constraint consists of a comma separated list of rules.
• A rule consists of a keyword ('allow' or 'deny') followed by a white space, and an IP address or address with wild card * (e.g. 192.168. * ). The keyword "all" can be used to match all addresses.
• If rules are present, but no match is made, the default setting is "deny".
• If no rules are present, the default setting is "allow".
• The first matching rule decides. E.g. when you formulate a constraint like "allow 192. * , deny 192.168.0.1", the 'deny' rule would have no effect, as that address matches the 'allow' rule already.

Example

Deny all IP addresses starting with 192., deny the IP address 193.168.0.1, allow all other IP addresses:

deny 192.*,deny 193.168.0.1,allow all

Allow all IP addresses starting with 178. except 178.6.6.6, deny all other IP addresses:

deny 178.6.6.6,allow 178.*

• Technical user: Select the technical user you created, e.g. "Technical_StandardRESTfulServices" (see Create Technical User). The permissions of this technical user determine the access rights granted to the client when using this scope.

children.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 for ADOIT
children.summary: Explains enabling OAuth 2.0 authentication in ADOIT Administration, adding and configuring clients with parameters like client type, ID, redirect URI, token validity, and secret, and notes testing via token generation.
children.content:
If you want to use the REST API with OAuth 2.0, you need to enable OAuth 2.0 and configure a client in the ADOIT Administration:
• Go to Authentication > OAuth 2.0.

The necessary settings are described below.

Enable OAuth 2.0 Authentication for ADOIT

For security reasons, OAuth 2.0 authentication is turned off by default in ADOIT. To enable OAuth 2.0 authentication:
• Select Enabled.

Add and Configure Client

Next, you will need to add a new client:
• Click Create to add a new client. The Client box appears.

Adapt the following parameters:
• Type: Select the client type. Confidential clients are e.g. centralized, server based applications, which are capable of securely storing client secrets. Public clients are e.g. purely client based applications and native apps which are not capable of securely storing client secrets.
• ID: The ID of the client system. Must be unique among the clients, should be kept simple as special characters need to be URL encoded.
• Name: The name of the client application. Will be shown on the user interface.
• Redirect URI: The URL of a redirect endpoint inside the client application which will be called by the authorization server when issuing an authorization code.

note

The Redirect URI is mandatory for the Authorization Code Flow but unused in the Client Credentials Flow. However, since the form requires a value, you can enter any valid placeholder URL (e.g., https://localhost/placeholder) for Client Credentials Flow integrations to proceed.

• Logo: Upload a logo to represent the client application. Will be shown on the user interface.
• Access token validity (seconds): The time in seconds how long an access token is valid until it expires. Default: 1800s = 30 minutes.
• Refresh token validity (seconds): The time in seconds how long a refresh token is valid until it expires. Default: 1209600s = 14 days.
• First-party application: If this option is enabled, authorization requests to this client are granted immediately if the user is already logged in, without showing a consent dialog. This setting is intended for applications that are owned and controlled by your organisation (first-party or public clients), where seamless access without repeated authorization is desired.
• Secret: The client secret used for authentication. For confidential clients, this field is enabled and mandatory. You can manually enter a value or click Generate to create a new one automatically. For public clients, the secret field is disabled and not required. These clients cannot securely store client secrets and use PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) to securely complete the authorization code flow.

Back on the OAuth 2.0 page, click Save. Now you can call the REST API with OAuth 2.0 authentication.

note

To test client requests, you can generate an access token to authenticate them (see "Generate Token" in the OAuth 2.0 section).

children.title: Configure OIDC Authentication
