• You can configure synchronisation for all domains simultaneously in the right pane, under LDAP Settings, in the Schedule section.
• Or you can configure synchronisation for a specific domain. Find the domain you want to adjust in the left pane, under LDAP Domains. Hover over the domain, click More, and then select Edit. The settings you want are on the third page, Schedule.

The configuration works in the same way in both cases. Adapt the following parameters:
• Name: Choose a name for this job (for traceability in the log files).
• Filter: A filter to narrow down what should be queried from the directory service. For example, set the value to (objectClass=user) to fetch only users.
• Start node: Define the node in the directory service tree structure that should be used as the starting point for user searches.

note

The Sync base DN parameter is used as a fallback when no Start node is defined for the synchronisation job. If neither Sync base DN nor Start node are defined, the Login base DN parameter is used as a fallback.
• Start at: Optional start date indicating when the schedule should become active. By default, the schedule is active immediately.
• End at: Optional end date specifying when the schedule should become inactive. After this date, the schedule will no longer be active.
• Type: Choose the time unit for the synchronisation schedule. Available options include secondly, minutely, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
• Interval: Define the frequency of the synchronisation job for schedules based on seconds, minutes, hours or years. Select every how many time units ADOIT performs the job.
• Day of month: Specify the day of the month when the job should run for monthly schedules.
• Weekdays: Select the days on which the job should run for daily and weekly schedules as follows:
• Days: The job runs every day by default, but you can optionally restrict it to specific days of the week.
• Weeks: The job runs once per week on the selected day.
• Execution time: Specify the exact hour and minute at which the job should start for daily, weekly and monthly schedules.

Example

Name: my5minSync | Filter: (objectClass=user) | Start node: dc=company,dc=eu | Type: minutely | Interval: 5

Objects are imported from the directory service:
• every 5 minutes [Type = minutely, Interval = execute every 5 units (= minutes) ] ,
• if they are user objects [Filter = (objectClass=user) ] and
• if they belong to the node "dc=company,dc=eu" or its children [Start node] .

children.title: Start Synchronising Users
children.summary: Start Synchronising Users covers saving synchronization settings to activate immediate and scheduled synchronization jobs, running synchronization on demand via Server options, and monitoring logs for errors.
children.content:
Save your changes in the ADOIT Administration. Once the changes are saved, they take effect immediately. A restart is not required.

The synchronisation of users will start. Jobs that run at fixed time intervals will be executed immediately and then repeated each time the time interval has passed. Schedules based on days, weeks or months will execute at the specified time.

Run the Synchronisation on Demand

The ADOIT Administration allows you to run the synchronisation on demand. The synchronisation is triggered according to the configuration specified for all configured domains.
• In the ADOIT Administration, go to Home > More options, and then click Server.
• Click Start LDAP synchronisation.

(Optional) Tracking Errors

Logging output and errors are written to the ADOIT21_0.log and ADOIT21_0_LDAP.log files in the configured log directory of the web server container and to *_aworker.log files in the configured log directory of the application server container, as well as to the standard container streams.

children.title: Tools
children.summary: Tools menu provides access to General settings (system preferences, file management, database statistics update, bandwidth analysis, licence overview, script execution, server management) and Support settings (support info package, debug mode, maintenance, repository statistics, support access).
children.content:
The Tools menu provide access to two types of settings:

General

The following settings are available in this section:
• System Preferences: Managing system preferences.
• File Management: Managing auxiliary files in the database; interface to the file system of the computer or network.
• Update Database Statistics: Optimising the database content structuring.
• Analyse Bandwidth: Analysing the bandwidth and response times between the ADOIT application server and the database server.
• Licence Overview: Summary of used and available scenario licence slots.
• Script Execution: Using external scripts.
• Server: Managing server restarts and server-related functionality.

Support

The following settings are available in this section:
• Information: Downloading a support information package (SIP) containing logging and system information.
• Debug Mode: Managing debug mode.
• Maintenance: Managing maintenance mode and the operations tool.
• Repository Statistics: View information about your ADOIT deployment.
• Support Access: Managing access for BOC employees to your ADOIT Administration for troubleshooting and support purposes.

children.title: System Preferences
children.summary: System Preferences accessed via Home > More options > System Preferences includes tabs for Security Settings (password and login configurations) and Audit Log management.
children.content:
To access the system preferences:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click System Preferences.

The System Preferences window opens. It contains the following tabs:
• Security Settings: Password strength and login settings.
• Audit Log: Enable the audit log.

These tabs are discussed in more detail in the following sections.

children.title: Security Settings
children.summary: Security Settings allow customizing password strength requirements (minimum strength, custom regex rules, password history, age limits) and login security (max allowed login failures before user lockout).
children.content:
The following options are available:

Password Strength Settings

Here you can customise the password strength settings. The following options are available:
• Minimal password strength: ADOIT determines the strength of passwords based on their length, complexity, and predictability and assigns them a value of 0 - 100%. Here you can set the minimum strength passwords must have: from very weak (0%), weak (20%), good (40%), strong (60%) to very strong (80%).
• Custom password rule: By default, a new password must have at least 8 characters and contain at least one digit (e.g. 0-9) and uppercase as well as lowercase characters (e.g. A-Z, a-z). You can change this setting and specify a custom password rule via a regular expression pattern.

Examples of custom password rules

Passwords should have at least 5 characters and contain a lowercase character (e.g. a-z). The Custom password rule field should therefore read:

^(?=.*[a-z]).{5,}$

Passwords should have at least 8 characters and contain a digit (e.g. 0-9), a lowercase character (e.g. a-z) and an uppercase character (e.g. A-Z). The Custom password rule field should therefore read:

^(?=.*\d)(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z]).{8,}$
• Number of not allowed previous passwords: Specify the number of previous passwords that are stored by ADOIT and must not be reused on password change.
• Maximum password age (days): Specify the period of time (in days) that a password can be used before ADOIT requires the user to change it.
• Minimum password age (days): Specify the period of time (in days) that a password must be used before the user can change it.

note

Passwords must meet the minimum password strength settings (e.g., reach 60%) AND match the custom password rule (e.g., contain at least 8 characters and contain numeric and uppercase and lowercase characters).

Login Settings

Here you can customise security relevant login settings. The following options are available:
• Number of allowed login failures: Choose a maximal number of allowed login failures before a user is disabled and cannot log in anymore.

children.title: System Preferences – Audit Log
children.summary: System Preferences – Audit Log refers to the Enable Audit Log section for detailed information on audit log configuration.
children.content: Please refer to the section Enable Audit Log for details.

children.title: File Management
children.summary: File Management tool enables managing auxiliary files in the database including searching, creating, renaming, deleting, importing, and exporting files and folders, with full access restricted to the Admin super user.
children.content:
This tool allows managing auxiliary files (graphic files, scripts…) in the database. To open the file manager:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click File Management.

The Database File Management window opens. The following functions are available:
• Search: Search for a file or folder in the database.
• File and Folder Management: Create new folders, cut and paste files, rename files and folders, delete files and folders, refresh the content of the catalogue.
• Export: Export files and folders from the database into the file system.
• Import: Import external files into the database.

note

Only the super user Admin has full access to all files in the database.

children.title: Update Database Statistics
children.summary: Update Database Statistics improves database query performance by refreshing catalogue statistics and can be executed via Home > More options > Update database statistics, with optional maintenance method and topic selection.
children.content:
The contents of the database are subject to permanent change: models and objects are created and deleted, libraries imported and much more. Every action creates new information which - over time - slows down the database access. Therefore, it is advisable to update the catalogue statistics of the database system either after major reorganisations or periodically.

Database catalogue statistics are data about the distribution of table and index values which are consulted by the database system for query optimisation. Up-to-date catalogue statistics lead to more efficient execution plans resulting in considerably shorter system response times and thus speeding up the user's work.

To update the database statistics:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Update database statistics
• Optional: Adapt the Maintenance method and Topic (table group) settings.
• Click Execute.

info

Updating the database statistics can take a while. During the update other users will experience significant slowdowns in the database communication with ADOIT. Therefore, we recommend not updating the database statistics during times of heavy use.

children.title: Maintenance Method
children.summary: Maintenance Method options for updating database statistics include default settings, statistics update only, leaf-level index defragmentation, full index rebuild, and online index rebuild (except for PostgreSQL).
children.content:
When you update the database statistics, you can select the maintenance method:
• Default settings: These are the default settings as defined in the configuration.
• Statistics update: The database catalogue statistics are updated, while the indexes are not defragmented.
• Defragmentation on leaf level: The indexes are defragmented on leaf level, and the database catalogue statistics are updated.
• Index rebuild: The complete index is defragmented.
• Index rebuild (online):: The complete index is defragmented while the index remains online. Not available for PostgreSQL databases.

children.title: Topic (Table Group)
children.summary: Topic (Table Group) selection specifies which database tables to maintain during statistics update, including all tables, migration-related, repository data, models, objects, users, or metamodel definition tables.
children.content:
When you update the database statistics, you can select for which database tables the selected maintenance method should be performed:
• All: Maintenance is performed for all database tables.
• Migration (all data tables except library definition): Maintenance is performed for all database tables containing ADOIT data which are relevant for migrations.
• Repository (repository list, groups, models, objects and users, relations): Maintenance is performed for all database tables which contain repository data including the repository list.
• Models (groups, models, objects and users, relations): Maintenance is performed for all database tables which contain repository data excluding the repository list.
• Objects (groups, objects and users, relations): Maintenance is performed for all database tables which contain object data.
• Users (groups, objects and users, rights and system roles; no relations): Maintenance is performed for all database tables which contain user data.
• Metamodel (library definition): Maintenance is performed for all database tables which contain the metamodel definition.

children.title: Analyse Bandwidth
children.summary: Analyse Bandwidth measures upload, download, and deletion times of test files between ADOIT Administration and database server to assess bandwidth and response times, initiated via Home > More options > Analyse Bandwidth.
children.content:
This function allows you to perform a quick, superficial analysis of the bandwidth and response times between the ADOIT Administration and the database server. To analyse the bandwidth:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Analyse Bandwidth.
• Click Start.

Three files (1KB, 1MB, 10MB) will be generated. Then ADOIT measures how long it takes to
• upload the files to the database (a temp directory will be created in the database),
• download the files from the database and
• delete the files from the database.

When the analysis is completed, you can compare your results with the reference values.

children.title: Licence Overview
children.summary: Licence Overview displays total and used scenario licences and active users with login and last action times, accessible via Home > More options > Licence Overview, with login name visibility controlled by the ADOXX_WEB_TRACK_LOGINS environment variable.
children.content:
This page shows you at a glance the total number of available scenario licences as well as the number of scenario licences currently in use. You can also find out quickly about all active ADOIT users including the time of login and the time of the last action. To open the Licence Overview page:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Licence Overview.

note

If you have questions about the different types of licences or the difference between concurrent users and named users, please refer to the sections Product Licences vs. Scenario Licences and Named Users vs. Concurrent Users.

note

You can control whether actual login names are shown in this widget by setting the environment variable ADOXX_WEB_TRACK_LOGINS to "true" or "false" in the deployment configuration of the application server container.

children.title: Script Execution
children.summary: Script Execution allows applying configuration changes via JavaScript scripts online without full product lifecycle, supporting script upload, server or browser execution, and cautioning to use only tested scripts from BOC employees.
children.content:
From time to time it can be advantageous to make small modifications of the ADOIT configuration without having to perform a full product configuration life cycle. The function Script Execution allows wrapping the changes into a JavaScript and applying them online.

To execute a JavaScript:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Script Execution.
• Click Browse and select the script you want to execute. You can also drag a file from your computer to the Drag and drop files here to upload area.
• Select Execute on server to execute the script on the application server. When this option is disabled, the script is executed in the web browser. If you are unsure which option to select, please contact a BOC employee.
• Click Execute Script.

caution

Only import tested JavaScripts which you have received from a BOC employee!

children.title: Server
children.summary: The Server page in ADOIT Administration enables maintenance tasks such as restarting the environment or web application, reinitializing the search index, starting LDAP synchronization, and clearing the LDAP cache to ensure correct user-role assignments.
children.content:
This page allows you to perform various maintenance tasks. To open the Server page:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Server.

The following functionalities are available:
• Restart Environment: Restart the application server and the web application. All users will be logged out. As soon as the application server is up and running again, and the web application is completely initialised, login is possible again.
• Restart Web Application: Restart the web application. All ADOIT users will be logged out. As soon as the web application is completely initialised, login is possible again.
• Re-intialise search index: Reinitialize the search index if you if you are encountering problems with the search function in ADOIT. Depending on the number of models and objects in the database this process may take a few minutes.
• Start LDAP synchronisation: Start the synchronization of users with an LDAP-compliant directory service according to the configuration specified in the ADOIT Administration. The synchronization is triggered for all configured domains. During the synchronization, a progress bar provides information on the current status. After the synchronization, all newly synchronized users and any error codes are displayed for each domain.
• Clear LDAP Cache: When synchronization of users with an LDAP-compliant directory service is enabled and the option recursiveNodeLookup is enabled for one or more LDAP properties, ADOIT is caching results to speed up performance. To detect changes in the directory structure, this cache is automatically cleared when the web application is restarted, when you start LDAP synchronization here in the ADOIT Administration, or when a periodic synchronization of users with LDAP is triggered.

Use this button to clear the LDAP cache if recursiveNodeLookup is enabled, there are changes in the directory structure, and you want to make sure that users that log in to ADOIT for the first time will be assigned correctly to system roles, user groups and repositories.

children.title: Information
children.summary: The Information page allows downloading encrypted support information packages containing log and configuration files in SMALL, MEDIUM, or LARGE sizes, and supports direct URL access for log retrieval even when ADOIT Administration is unreachable.
children.content:
This page allows you to download support information packages in different sizes. A support information package contains log files of the application server, log files of the web server including the web application as well as configuration files within an encrypted Zip archive. To open the Information page:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Information.

The following sizes are available:
• Support Package SMALL: Downloads log files from the last 24 hours.
• Support Package MEDIUM: Downloads log files from the last week.
• Support Package LARGE: Downloads all log files.

Download Support Information Package when Access to the ADOIT Administration is not possible

You can still download the support package when the ADOIT Administration cannot be reached in case of an error. In order to do so:
• Open a web browser and navigate to "ht ﻿ tp:// < SERVER_NAME > : < TOMCAT_PORT > /ADOIT21_0/supportinformation".

< SERVER_NAME > is the name of the server machine, < TOMCAT_PORT > is the port at which Apache Tomcat is accessible (by default this is 8000).

Example

If you are running ADOIT locally, the URL should look like this:

"ht ﻿ tp://localhost:8000/ADOIT21_0/supportinformation"

You can modify the URL to only download log files from a certain time period. In order to do this, add ?logType= < PARAMETER > to the URL. The following parameters that correspond to the package sizes listed above are available: "small", "medium" and "large".

Example

If you are running ADOIT locally and you want to download log files from the last 24 hours, the URL should look like this:

"ht ﻿ tp://localhost:8000/ADOIT21_0/supportinformation?logType=small"

note

Please provide these log files when you contact our support team.

children.title: Debug Mode
children.summary: The Debug Mode page lets administrators activate, change duration, or deactivate debug mode for error analysis, with automatic deactivation after a set timespan and a caution against permanent activation.
children.content:
This page allows you to activate the debug mode. The debug mode influences various details in the behaviour of the application and can be used for error analysis. To open the Debug Mode page:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Debug Mode.

The following functionalities are available:

Activate Debug Mode

To activate the debug mode:
• Click Activate. Enter a duration and, optionally, a reason. Then, click OK.

The debug mode will automatically deactivate after the selected timespan.

Change Duration

To change the duration of the debug mode:
• Click Change duration. Modify the duration as needed. Then, click OK.

Deactivate Debug Mode

To deactivate the debug mode:
• Click Deactivate.

caution

The debug mode should never be permanently enabled! It is recommended to only activate the debug mode on request of a BOC employee.

children.title: Maintenance
children.summary: The Maintenance page provides options to enable maintenance mode for planning maintenance windows and to access the Operations Tool for critical operational functions like product upgrades.
children.content:
The Maintenance page allows you to enable maintenance mode and the operations tool:
• Maintenance Mode: Maintenance mode eases the planning of maintenance windows.
• Operations Tool: This web application provides access to important functionality relevant for operations, such as upgrading the product.

children.title: Maintenance Mode
children.summary: Maintenance Mode restricts user logins to the web application while allowing ADOIT Administration access, with options to log out users immediately and persist mode after restarts, and can be activated or deactivated via the Maintenance page.
children.content:
Maintenance mode eases the planning of maintenance windows. When maintenance mode is enabled, no further logins to the web application will be allowed and a corresponding message will be displayed. The ADOIT Administration is excluded from maintenance mode and can still be used.

Activate Maintenance Mode

To activate maintenance mode:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Maintenance.
• Click Activate Maintenance Mode.
• Choose further options based on your preference:
• To log out all regular ADOIT users right now, click Log out all non-admin users.
• To keep maintenance mode enabled even if the web application or the entire environment are later restarted on the Server page, select Keep maintenance mode active after restart.
• Click Close.

Deactivate Maintenance Mode

To deactivate maintenance mode:
• On the Maintenance page, click Deactivate Maintenance Mode.

children.title: Operations Tool
children.summary: The Operations Tool is a web application offering essential administrative operations for ADOIT without needing direct server or database access.
children.content: The Operations Tool is a web application that provides access to important operations for administering ADOIT. It is available when needed and allows you to perform certain operations without direct access to the application server or database server.

children.title: Start the Operations Tool
children.summary: The Operations Tool can be started from ADOIT Administration in maintenance mode, automatically for uninitialized databases, or via the ADOXX_OPERATIONS_TOOL_MODE environment variable set to 'initdb' or 'maintenance' for database initialization or maintenance tasks respectively.
children.content:
The Operations Tool can be started in different ways depending on the operation you need to perform:
• From the ADOIT Administration: Go to Home > More options > Maintenance, and click Activate Operations Tool. The Operations Tool starts in maintenance mode. To stop the Operations Tool, return to the Maintenance page and click Deactivate Operations Tool (restarts the environment).
• Automatically when the database is not initialized: If you deploy ADOIT with an empty, uninitialized database, or if you use the database user ADOxx with the predefined default password, the Operations Tool starts automatically in initialize empty database mode when the application server starts. Use this mode to encrypt the database credentials and initialize the database.
• Using an environment variable: To start the Operations Tool, set the ADOXX_OPERATIONS_TOOL_MODE environment variable to initdb or maintenance, and restart the environment. Use initdb to start the Operations Tool for database initialization. Use maintenance to start it in maintenance mode. The latter option can be used, for example, if you need to reset or enable the Admin account and cannot access the ADOIT Administration.

children.title: Access the Operations Tool
children.summary: Access the Operations Tool via its URL on port 9090 (default), ensuring the port is exposed in deployment configurations; access is IP-restricted by default and can be managed via the OPERATIONS_IP_RESTRICTIONS environment variable.
children.content:
To access the Operations Tool, open its URL in a web browser. The Operations Tool uses port 9090 by default. To construct the URL, take the URL where ADONIS is available and replace the web server port with port 9090 (for example, http://localhost:9090/).

Make sure that the Operations Tool port is exposed in the deployment configuration of the application server container. For example, in a Kubernetes deployment, configure the Kubernetes networking accordingly to make the Operations Tool port accessible. For development and testing purposes, you can use port forwarding to access the Operations Tool:

kubectl port-forward service/<your-service-name> 9090:9090

If you configure a different port using the OPERATIONS_SERVER_PORT environment variable, expose the corresponding port in your deployment configuration.

note

Access to the Operations Tool is restricted by the OPERATIONS_IP_RESTRICTIONS environment variable. By default, the tool will refuse all incoming connections unless this variable is explicitly defined.

children.title: Environment Variables
children.summary: Configure Operations Tool behavior using environment variables like ADOXX_OPERATIONS_TOOL_MODE (mode), OPERATIONS_SERVER_PORT (port), OPERATIONS_IP_RESTRICTIONS (IP access control), TLS certificate/key paths, max upload size, download TTL, and encrypted database credentials (ADOXX_DBMS_CREDENTIALS).
children.content:
You can configure the following environment variables in the deployment configuration of the application server container:
Environment Variable | Description
ADOXX_OPERATIONS_TOOL_MODE | Forces the application server container to start the Operations Tool in the specified mode. Possible values are initdb for database initialization and maintenance for maintenance mode.
OPERATIONS_SERVER_PORT | (Optional) Specifies the port used by the Operations Tool. The default is 9090.
OPERATIONS_IP_RESTRICTIONS | Specifies which IP addresses can access the Operations Tool. If this variable is not configured, access to the Operations Tool is denied. You can specify individual IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, IPv4 wildcards or subnets, and IPv6 subnets. Use * to allow access from all IP addresses.
OPERATIONS_SERVER_CERT | (Optional) Specifies the path to the TLS certificate used by the Operations Tool. Not required if secure connections are handled externally (for example, via a Kubernetes Ingress controller).
OPERATIONS_SERVER_KEY | (Optional) Specifies the path to the TLS key used by the Operations Tool. Not required if secure connections are handled externally.
OPERATIONS_MAX_FILE_SIZE_UPLOAD | (Optional) Specifies the maximum size of an uploaded file in MB. The default is 5 GB.
OPERATIONS_DOWNLOAD_TTL | (Optional) Specifies how long files generated by an operation remain available for download. The default is 12 hours.
ADOXX_DBMS_CREDENTIALS | Specifies the encrypted database credentials used to connect to the ADOIT database.

children.title: Maintenance
children.summary: The Maintenance mode in the Operations Tool provides operations including encrypting database credentials, resetting/enabling the Admin account, importing/exporting migration packages or repositories, executing scripts, exporting libraries, and upgrading the product, all requiring database connection parameters and often used under BOC employee guidance.
children.content:
The Maintenance mode provides access to the following operations:
• Encrypt Credentials
• Reset Admin Password
• Enable Admin
• Import Migration Package/Repository
• Export Migration Package/Repository
• Script Execution
• Export Library
• Upgrade Product

These operations use the same database connection parameters.

Encrypt Credentials

Use Encrypt Credentials to encrypt the credentials of the database user that ADOIT uses to connect to the database. This can either be the database user ADOxx or an individual database user.

Encrypt Database Credentials

To encrypt the database credentials:
• In the Operations Tool, click Encrypt Credentials.
• Enter the database username in Username.
• Enter the corresponding password in Password and Retype Password.
• Click Encrypt.

Provide the generated encrypted credentials to the application server through the ADOXX_DBMS_CREDENTIALS environment variable.

Reset Admin Password

To reset the password of the ADOIT super user Admin, for example if the password has been forgotten:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Reset Admin Password.
2. Enter the username of the database user in DB User Name.
3. Enter the corresponding password in DB User Password.
4. Enter the new password for the Admin account in New Admin Password and Retype New Admin Password.
5. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
6. Click Reset Admin Password.

Enable Admin

To re-enable the ADOIT superuser Admin if the account has been disabled and you can no longer log in to ADOIT:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Enable Admin.
2. Enter the username of the database user in DB User Name.
3. Enter the corresponding password in DB User Password.
4. Enter the new password for the Admin account in New Admin Password and Retype New Admin Password.
5. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
6. Click Enable Admin.

Import Migration Package/Repository

note

For regular import operations, use the corresponding functions in the ADOIT Administration: Import Repository, Import Migration Package, or Import Migration Package with Multiple Repositories. Use the Operations Tool for these operations if instructed by a BOC employee or if you need to import very large files.

To import a repository, migration package, or multi-repository migration package into the ADOIT database:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Import Migration Package/Repository.
2. Enter the username of an ADOIT administrator in Username.
3. Enter the corresponding password in Password.
4. Upload the repository or migration package in Archive File.
5. If the archive is password-protected, enter its password in Archive File Password.
6. Select the type of archive in Archive Type:
• Repository (.axr)
• Migration Package (.axr)
• Multi-Repository Migration Package (.axm)
7. If you selected Repository (.axr) or Migration Package (.axr), configure the following options:
• Select Import as New repository to import the archive as a new repository. If you select this option, Target Repository ID is not required.
• If you do not select Import as New repository, enter the ID of the repository into which the archive is to be imported in Target Repository ID.
8. If you selected Multi-Repository Migration Package (.axm), configure the following options:
• Select Skip Users to exclude users from the import.
• Optionally, enter a comma-separated list of repository IDs in Repositories to Import. Leave the field empty to import all repositories contained in the migration package.
9. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
10. Click Import.

Export Migration Package/Repository

note

For regular export operations, use the corresponding functions in the ADOIT Administration: Export Repository, Export Migration Package, or Export Migration Package with Multiple Repositories. Use the Operations Tool for these operations if instructed by a BOC employee or if you need to export very large files.

To export a repository, migration package, or multi-repository migration package:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Export Migration Package/Repository.
2. Enter the username of an ADOIT administrator in Username.
3. Enter the corresponding password in Password.
4. Select the type of archive in Archive Type:
• Repository (.axr)
• Migration Package (.axr)
• Multi-Repository Migration Package (.axm)
5. If you selected Repository (.axr) or Migration Package (.axr), configure the following options:
• Enter the ID of the repository to export in Target Repository ID.
6. If you selected Multi-Repository Migration Package (.axm), configure the following options:
• Optionally, enter a comma-separated list of repository IDs in Repositories to Export. Leave the field empty to export all repositories.
• Select Skip Users to exclude users from the export.
7. Optionally, enter a password for the exported archive in Archive File Password and Retype Archive File Password.
8. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
9. Click Export.

Script Execution

note

For regular script execution, use Script Execution in the ADOIT Administration. The Operations Tool always executes scripts on the live data and is intended for cases where you are instructed to use it by a BOC employee.

To execute a JavaScript on the application server:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Script Execution.
2. Enter the username of an ADOIT administrator in Username.
3. Enter the corresponding password in Password.
4. Upload the JavaScript in Script.
5. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
6. Click Execute Script.

caution

Only execute tested JavaScripts that you have received from a BOC employee.

Export Library

note

You can also export the library in the ADOIT Administration using Export Library.

To export the active library:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Export Library.
2. Enter the username of an ADOIT administrator in Username.
3. Enter the corresponding password in Password.
4. Optionally, select the language to export in Export Language. Leave the field empty to export all available languages.
5. Optionally, select the following options:
• Select Unique Export to export the library with new IDs assigned to all library elements. Use this option only in special cases and if instructed by a BOC employee.
• Select Skip Library Logs to export the library without library logs. Library logs are used to preserve custom metamodel changes made on the Properties page in the ADOIT Administration when a new application library is imported later. Use this option only in special cases and if instructed by a BOC employee.
• Select Include Base Library to include the base library in the exported AXL file. The base library is the version of the library on which custom metamodel changes were made on the Properties page in the ADOIT Administration. Use this option only in special cases and if instructed by a BOC employee.
6. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
7. Click Export.

Upgrade Product

note

For the complete upgrade procedure, including the required preparation and post-upgrade steps, see Upgrade ADOIT in the Installation Manual.

The Operations Tool can upgrade the ADOIT database from an older version to version 21.0.

To start the upgrade:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Upgrade Product.
2. Enter the username of the database user in DB User Name.
3. Enter the corresponding password in DB User Password.
4. Enter the version of ADOIT that you are upgrading from in Source Version.
5. Enter the password of the ADOIT Admin account in Admin Password.
6. If you have received an upgrade package from a BOC employee, upload it in Upgrade Package. Otherwise, leave the field empty.

note

If you leave Upgrade Package empty, only the component settings are updated, but not the application library. Your component settings are exported before the upgrade and re-imported afterwards, ensuring that your custom configuration is preserved.
7. Optionally, select the following options:
• Select Dry Run to perform a test run without applying the upgrade.
• Select Skip DB Scripts to skip the execution of all database scripts.
8. Configure the database connection parameters as required.
9. Click Start Upgrade.

Database Connection Parameters

The following optional parameters are available for database connections within specific maintenance operation dialogs (such as repository exports). In many environments, these parameters can safely be left empty. The fields are only required depending on your targeted database system and its specific encryption configuration.
• SSL Mode: For PostgreSQL, allows to specify that an encrypted connection to the database is set up. Possible values are allow, prefer, disable, require, verify-ca and verify-full.
• SSL Key: For PostgreSQL, specifies the file path to the client SSL key. This is only needed if your database enforces client certificate authentication.
• SSL Certificate: For PostgreSQL, specifies the file path to the client SSL certificate. This is only needed if your database enforces client certificate authentication.
• Root Certificate: For PostgreSQL, specifies the file path to the SSL certificate authority (CA) bundle to verify the database server's identity.
• Trust Server Certificate: For Microsoft SQL Server, specifies whether the server certificate is trusted without validation. Possible values are yes and no.
• Encryption: For Microsoft SQL Server, specifies the encryption mode for the database connection. Possible values are mandatory, optional and strict.

note

For PostgreSQL, connection encryption configurations are optional. If your database does not strictly demand SSL certificates or secure transport configurations, you can leave all four SSL fields completely blank.

note

For Microsoft SQL Server, encrypted database connections are used by default. If your SQL Server is not configured for encrypted connections, specify optional for Encryption. If your SQL Server uses an encrypted connection with an untrusted server certificate, you may also need to specify yes for Trust Server Certificate.

children.title: Initialize the Database
children.summary: Initialize the database by preparing it with required scripts, optionally changing the ADOxx user password, encrypting database credentials via the Operations Tool, and uploading license and optional library files to complete initialization, after which ADOIT starts normally.
children.content:
Use initialize empty database mode to prepare a newly created, empty database for use with ADOIT. In this mode, the Operations Tool starts automatically if the database has been created and the required database tables exist but have not yet been initialized for ADOIT.

Prepare the Database

Before deploying ADOIT, create the database and execute the required database scripts:
• For PostgreSQL, execute prepareDB.sql (adapt vDBName and <ADOXX_PASSWORD>) and then postgresql.sql.
• For Microsoft SQL Server, execute sqlserver_create_db.sql (adapt vDBName and ADOXX_PASSWORD) and then sqlserver.sql.

You can download the database scripts from the BOC Group deployment-examples GitHub repository.

Optional: Change Password of Database User ADOxx

ADOIT communicates with the database using a dedicated database user. You can use the database user ADOxx or an individual database user.

If you use ADOxx with the predefined default password, you must change the password before proceeding. You can change the password using your database administration tool, for example pgAdmin or SQL Server Management Studio.

Encrypt Database Credentials

After deploying ADOIT, the Operations Tool starts automatically if the encrypted database user credentials have not yet been provided to ADOIT. Encrypt and provide the database credentials as follows:
1. In the Operations Tool, click Encrypt Credentials.
2. Enter the database username in Username.
3. Enter the corresponding password in Password and Retype Password.
4. Click Encrypt.
5. Provide the generated encrypted credentials to the application server through the ADOXX_DBMS_CREDENTIALS environment variable.

Initialize the Database

Restart the environment. If the database has not yet been initialized, the Operations Tool starts automatically. To initialize the database:
• In the Operations Tool, upload the required License File.
• Optionally, upload a Library File if you are using a custom library and select the Primary Language.
• Configure the database connection parameters as required.
• Click Initialize Database.

After successful initialization, the Operations Tool shuts down and ADOIT starts normally.

children.title: Logging
children.summary: The Operations Tool logs activities per application server logging settings, creating timestamped log files with INFO/WARN/ERROR levels, while programs started by it generate separate logs; all accessing IP addresses are logged unencrypted.
children.content:
The Operations Tool logs its activities according to the logging configuration of the application server. You can configure logging using the ADOXX_LOG_MODE and ADOXX_LOG_DIR environment variables.

The Operations Tool creates a separate log file with the following naming scheme:

yyyy.MM.dd_hh.mm.ss_PID_aoperations.log

Each log entry uses the following format:

yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss.SSS [INFO/WARN/ERROR] [T:AOPERATIONS]

Programs started by the Operations Tool, such as maintenance operations, write their own log files in addition to the Operations Tool log. Their output is not included in the Operations Tool log.

note

All IP addresses that access the Operations Tool are logged in unencrypted form.

children.title: Repository Statistics
children.summary: Repository Statistics display detailed information about the ADOIT deployment including product, database, user, license details, and repository contents with counts of models, objects, relations, and groups accessible via Home > More options > Repository Statistics.
children.content:
View information about your ADOIT deployment. To open the repository statistics:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Repository Statistics.

The Scenario Data window opens. The following data is displayed:
• Product Information: Details about the product, including name, version, platform version, and database schema.
• General Information: Information about the database, application libraries, repositories, current repository and application library, and available UI languages.
• User Information: Data about the number of users, the current user’s username, name, and type.
• License Information: Details on licensed scenarios, including IDs, user limits, and advanced components with their IDs.
• Repository Contents: Statistics on repositories, including application library, content languages, primary language, and counts for models, objects, relations, and groups. Detailed breakdowns of the number of instances in the database for each model type, object type, and relation type are also included.

children.title: Support Access
children.summary: Support Access enables temporary BOC employee access to ADOIT Administration for SaaS deployments with prerequisites like configured email and audit logging; activation creates a full-access support user and sends notification emails, while deactivation disables the user and revokes IP allowances.
children.content:
The Support Access functionality allows temporarily enabling BOC employees to access your ADOIT Administration for troubleshooting and support purposes.

note

This feature is only available for SaaS deployments.

Prerequisites

Before you can activate support access, the following prerequisites must be met:
• The Email settings have to be configured correctly.
• The audit log needs to be enabled.
• The deployment must be SaaS.

Activate Support Access

To activate support access:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Activate Support Access.
• Confirm the activation in the dialogue box that appears.

Once activated, a temporary support user account is created with the following properties:
• This user belongs to the user group Default group and has access to all repositories.
• The user has full access to the ADOIT Administration and its components.

When support access is activated:
• A red message indicating "Support Access is active!" appears in the ADOIT Administration next to the welcome text.
• An email is sent to the BOC support team confirming the activation, along with deployment details (e.g. URL, username, version, etc.).
• If IP restrictions are active for the ADOIT Administration, BOC support IP addresses are automatically allowed.

Deactivate Support Access

To deactivate support access:
• Go to Home > More options, and then click Deactivate Support Access.

When support access is deactivated:
• The support user account is not deleted but is disabled.
• BOC support IP addresses are no longer automatically allowed.
• An email is sent to the BOC support team confirming the deactivation.
• The red "Support Access is active!" indicator disappears from the ADOIT Administration.

note

If audit logging is enabled or disabled while support access is active, this does not end support access. The support user is also able to manage audit logging settings.

children.title: Appendix
children.summary: The Appendix covers ADOIT usage concepts, user settings, detailed rights overview, metamodel access impact, audit log details, emergency mode, glossary, metamodel conflict resolution during library updates, and configuration changes requiring server restarts.
children.content:
In the Appendix, the following topics are outlined:
• Concept of Use: General information on the use of ADOIT.
• Settings: Change your password, switch the language, log out etc.
• Detailed Rights - All Available Actions: An overview of all available actions when assigning detailed rights (= extended rights).
• Impact of Restricting Access to Metamodel Elements: Look up examples that illustrate how changing metamodel rights affects working with ADOIT.
• Audit Log Files: The file-based audit log in ADOIT tracks administrative actions automatically and stores them in structured log files.
• Audit Log - Logged Actions: A list describing the categories of actions that are in the audit log.
• Emergency Mode: If normal operation is not possible, ADOIT will enter emergency mode.
• Glossary: A short glossary.
• How Metamodel Conflicts Are Resolved During Library Updates: In this chapter, you will learn how ADOIT handles metamodel conflicts when updating a library that contains custom local changes.
• Configuration Changes That Require a Server Restart: An overview of all configuration changes necessitate restarting the application server or web server.

children.title: Concept of Use
children.summary: The Concept of Use chapter provides general guidance on using ADOIT.
children.content: This chapter provides general information on the use of ADOIT.

children.title: Types of Roles
children.summary: System Roles are created and assigned in ADOIT Administration granting feature and metamodel access including EA workflow roles, while Roles are business role objects referenced within models and objects.
children.content:
System Roles

System Roles are created in the ADOIT Administration and assigned to users.
• System Roles grant access to ADOIT features and to the available metamodel elements (= metamodel rights)
• A special case of system roles are EA workflow roles.

Roles

Roles (business roles) are objects that are created in ADOIT.
• Roles are referenced in the properties of models and objects .

children.title: Trusted Login
children.summary: Trusted Login enables single sign-on (SSO) scenarios allowing users authenticated externally or technical users to perform actions without entering credentials, inheriting this right if their user group has it.
children.content:
This setting is only relevant in certain scenarios. It enables simple and quick access to ADOIT via single sign-on (SSO).

Trusted login means that a user for whom this right is set can perform actions without having to enter a user name and password.

Trusted login is a prerequisite for:
• users who are authenticated outside of ADOIT (Login with LDAP Coupling, IDM, SAML, OIDC)
• technical users which are used for special scenarios (e.g. for synchronizing objects between ADOIT and another BOC Management Office product)
• users who are used to access the Organisation Portal anonymously

If a user is in a user group that has this right, the user inherits this right.

children.title: Settings
children.summary: The user symbol in the upper-right corner provides access to settings such as changing password and switching language.
children.content: Click the user symbol to change your password, switch the language etc.

children.title: Change Password
children.summary: To change your password, use the user symbol menu to enter old and new passwords and confirm the change by pressing Enter.
children.content:
To change your password:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Change password....
• Type your old password, type your new password, type your new password again to confirm it, and then press < ENTER > .

children.title: Language
children.summary: Switch the ADOIT Administration language via the user symbol menu under Language; the selection is remembered for future sessions.
children.content:
In order to switch the language in the ADOIT Administration:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, point to Language, and then select a language.

Once you select a language, the ADOIT Administration will remember your selection for subsequent visits.

children.title: Info
children.summary: The Info option under the user symbol shows a dialogue with detailed status information about the current session.
children.content:
In order to show a dialogue window with detailed status information about the current session:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Info.

children.title: ADOIT
children.summary: Clicking ADOIT under the user symbol switches the interface to ADOIT.
children.content:
To switch to ADOIT:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click ADOIT.

children.title: Logout
children.summary: Logout from ADOIT via the user symbol menu by selecting Logout.
children.content:
In order to log out of ADOIT:
• Click the user symbol in the upper-right corner, and then click Logout.

children.title: Detailed Rights - All Available Actions
children.summary: Detailed Rights documentation explains all assignable extended rights actions with a note to refer to the Set Extended Rights for Content section for editing instructions.
children.content:
In the following sections, all available actions when assigning detailed rights (= extended rights) are viewed in detail.

note

For information on how to edit detailed rights, please refer to the section Set Extended Rights for Content for details.

children.title: Detailed Rights of Model Groups
children.summary: Detailed rights for model groups include specific permissions related to managing models and subgroups within the group.
children.content: The following detailed rights are available for model groups:

children.title: Write
children.summary: Write rights for model groups cover adding/removing models and subgroups, renaming groups, and modifying attributes and modelling elements within the group, with some permissions applying only for inheritance.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Adding models: New models can be created in this model group.
• Adding subgroups: New subgroups can be created in this model group.
• Removing models: Models can be deleted from this model group.
• Removing subgroups: Subgroups can be deleted from this model group.
• Renaming groups: The model group can be renamed.
• Adding contexts (only for inheritance): New contexts (e.g. new languages) can be added to the models in this group (no relevance for the group itself).
• Adding modelling elements (only for inheritance): Objects and connectors can be added to the models in this group (no relevance for the group itself).
• Modifying attribute values (only for inheritance): Object attributes can be edited in the models in this group. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).
• Modifying model attribute values (only for inheritance): The attributes of the models in this group can be edited (no relevance for the group itself). If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).
• Removing modelling elements (only for inheritance): Objects and connectors can be deleted from the models in this group (no relevance for the group itself).

children.title: Read Models with Translation Option (only for inheritance)
children.summary: Read Models with Translation Option rights for model groups allow adding contexts and modifying attribute values for models in the group, applicable only for inheritance scenarios.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Adding contexts (only for inheritance): New contexts (e.g. new languages) can be added to the models in this group (no relevance for the group itself).
• Modifying attribute values (only for inheritance): Object attributes can be edited in the models in this group. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).
• Modifying model attribute values (only for inheritance): The attributes of the models in this group can be edited (no relevance for the group itself). If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Detailed Rights of Models
children.summary: Detailed rights for individual models specify granular permissions applicable to that model.
children.content: The following detailed rights are available for individual models:

children.title: Read Models with Translation Option
children.summary: Read Models with Translation Option rights for models include adding contexts and modifying model and object attribute values, with restrictions making attributes read-only except for relations if denied.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Adding contexts: New contexts (e.g. new languages) can be added to the model.
• Modifying model attribute values: The attributes of the model can be edited. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).
• Modifying attribute values: The attributes of the objects in this model can be edited. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Write
children.summary: Write rights for models allow adding contexts and modelling elements, modifying model and object attributes, and removing modelling elements, with attribute modification restrictions making attributes read-only except for relations if denied.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Adding contexts: New contexts (e.g. new languages) can be added to the model.
• Adding modelling elements: Objects and connectors may be added to the model.
• Modifying model attribute values: The attributes of the model can be edited. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).
• Removing modelling elements: Objects and connectors may be deleted from the model.
• Modifying attribute values: The attributes of the objects in this model can be edited. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Detailed Rights of Object Groups
children.summary: Detailed rights for object groups define specific permissions related to managing repository objects and subgroups within the group.
children.content: The following detailed rights are available for object groups:

children.title: Write
children.summary: Write rights for object groups include adding/removing repository objects and subgroups, renaming groups, and modifying attributes of objects within the group, with attribute modification applying only for inheritance.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Adding repository objects: New repository objects can be created in this object group.
• Adding subgroups: New subgroups can be created in this object group.
• Removing repository objects: Repository objects can be deleted from this object group.
• Removing subgroups: Subgroups can be deleted from this object group.
• Renaming groups: The object group can be renamed.
• Modifying attribute values (only for inheritance): The attributes of the objects in this group can be edited (no relevance for the group itself). If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Read Repository Objects with Translation Option (only for inheritance)
children.summary: Defines detailed rights for reading repository objects with translation option limited to inheritance, specifically allowing or denying modification of attribute values while still permitting relation modifications.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Modifying attribute values (only for inheritance): The attributes of the objects in this group can be edited (no relevance for the group itself). If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Detailed Rights of Objects
children.summary: Introduces the availability of detailed rights applicable to individual objects within ADOIT.
children.content: The following detailed rights are available for individual objects:

children.title: Read Repository Objects with Translation Option
children.summary: Specifies detailed rights for reading repository objects with translation option, focusing on permission to modify attribute values while relations remain modifiable even if attribute editing is denied.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Modifying attribute values: The attributes of the object can be edited. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Write
children.summary: Details write permissions allowing modification of object attribute values, with denial resulting in read-only attributes but still permitting relation modifications.
children.content:
The following detailed rights can be granted / restricted:
• Modifying attribute values: The attributes of the object can be edited. If this permission is denied, all attributes are read-only (although modifying relations is still allowed).

children.title: Impact of Restricting Access to Metamodel Elements
children.summary: Explains how changes to metamodel rights impact ADOIT usage, referencing the section on viewing or changing metamodel rights for configuration guidance.
children.content:
Based on examples, this chapter illustrates how changing metamodel rights affects working with ADOIT.

note

For information on how to change metamodel rights, please refer to the section View or Change Metamodel Rights.

children.title: Scenario 1: Creating Models/Objects
children.summary: Scenario illustrating that creating models or objects requires creation permissions for the type and write access to the Name attribute, with examples modifying system role rights to restrict creation.
children.content:
Creating models/objects requires permissions to create models/objects of this type and write permissions to the Name attribute.

Example

Edit the basic metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the model type Cross-Domain Model:
• Set the permissions to the Name attribute to Read.

Now users with the system role "Participant" cannot create Cross-Domain Models.

You can achieve the same result by editing the detailed metamodel rights of the system role to the model type and setting "Create models" to denied.

children.title: Scenario 2: Editing Models/Objects
children.summary: Scenario showing that editing models or objects requires edit permissions for the type, demonstrated by denying edit rights to a system role for a specific class.
children.content:
Editing models/objects requires permissions to edit models/objects of this type.

Example

Edit the detailed metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the class Service:
• Set "Edit objects" to denied.

Now users with the system role "Participant" cannot edit or rename Services.

children.title: Scenario 3: Adding Objects to a Model
children.summary: Scenario explaining that adding objects to a model requires creation rights for the object type, with an example denying creation rights to prevent new object additions but allowing reuse from the Object Catalogue.
children.content:
Creating objects in a model requires permissions to create objects of this type.

Example

Edit the detailed metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the class Risk:
• Set "Create objects" to denied.

Now users with the system role "Participant" cannot create new Risks. They can still re-use Risks from the Object Catalogue in models.

children.title: Scenario 4: Saving a Copy of a Model
children.summary: Scenario describing that saving a copy of a model requires creation permissions for all object and relation types contained in the model, with denial preventing saving copies containing restricted types.
children.content:
Saving a copy of a model requires permissions to create all the modelling object and relation types which the model contains.

Example

Edit the detailed metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the class Note:
• Set "Create objects" to denied.

Now users with the system role "Participant" cannot create new Notes. They cannot save a copy of a model that contains a Note.

children.title: Scenario 5: Deleting Objects
children.summary: Scenario stating that deleting objects requires delete permissions for the object type, with denial preventing deletion of objects or models containing those objects.
children.content:
Deleting objects requires permissions to delete objects of this type.

Example

Edit the detailed metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the class Note:
• Set "Delete objects" to denied.

Now users with the system role "Participant" cannot delete Notes. They cannot delete a model that contains a Note.

children.title: Scenario 6: Opening a Model that Contains Unavailable Objects
children.summary: Scenario detailing that opening a model with unavailable objects requires read permissions for those object types, with denial causing such objects to be invisible in the model.
children.content:
Accessing an object in a model requires permissions to read objects of this type:

Example

Edit the basic metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the class Risk:
• Set the permissions to No access.

Now Risks are not available for users with the system role "Participant". When they open a model that contains a Risk, the Risk is invisible for them.

children.title: Scenario 7: Deleting a Model
children.summary: Scenario indicating that deleting a model requires delete permissions for the model type, with denial preventing users from deleting models of that type.
children.content:
Deleting a model requires permissions to delete models of this type.

Example

Edit the detailed metamodel rights of the system role "Participant" to the model type Cross-Domain Models:
• Set "Delete models" to denied.

Now users with the system role "Participant" cannot delete Cross-Domain Models.

children.title: Overview of Permissions to Individual Functions
children.summary: Comprehensive overview of permissions required for various ADOIT functions including dashboards, model time filter, quick links, organisation portal, reporting, validation, charts, and multiple workspaces, specifying required read/write access to metamodel elements and attributes.
children.content:
What permissions are required for the different tasks that can be performed in ADOIT?

Dashboards (ADOIT Scenarios)
• Widgets are empty if none of the displayed object types are available.
• Columns in a widget are empty if the displayed relations and attributes are not available.
• Charts are only available if the queried object types, relations and attributes are available.

Model Time Filter
• The Model Time Filter is only available if the object types for which the filter is configured are available.

Quick Links
• Links are removed or disabled based on metamodel rights.

Organisation Portal
• The Organisation Portal is only available if the configured model types and State attribute are available.

Reporting Board
• Individual Reports are only available if the respective view or report is available.

Reports
• Standard reports omit relations and attributes that are not available.

Validation
• A check is only available if the required object types, relations, model types or attributes are available.

Charts
• Matrix charts are only available if there is at least one available object type/relation for the row/column/cell.
• Bubble charts are only available if the configured object type and the x-axis/y-axis attributes are available.
• Gantt charts are only available if the configured object type and the attributes are available.
• The dependency modeller is only available if Architecture Diagrams or Analysis Models are available. When an analysis is performed with the dependency modeller, layers which contain unavailable object types are empty.
• Box-in-box charts are only available if the configured object types, relations and the model type are available.

Workspaces (All)
• Workspaces are only available to users who have read access to User objects and the following attributes of those objects:
• Name
• Email
• First name
• Last name

Workspace "Application Cost Management"
• The Application Cost Management template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Write access to the Contract metamodel element and to at least one of the Application Component or Application Service metamodel elements.
• Read access to the Association relationship.
• For the properties listed below, read access is required unless write access is explicitly stated.

Contract
• Name (write access required)
• Description
• Annual cost (write access required)
• Currency (write access required)
• Valid until

Application Component or Application Service (at least one)
• Name (write access required)
• Investment strategy (requires the default enumeration values)
• Lifecycle state (requires the default enumeration values)

Association
• Name

note

For outgoing Association relations from Contracts, the target classes Application Component and/or Application Service must not be restricted.

Workspace "Application Compliance Assessment"
• The Application Compliance Assessment template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Write access to the Application Component metamodel element and to at least one of the Principle or Constraint metamodel elements.
• Read access to the Association relationship.
• For the properties listed below, read access is required unless write access is explicitly stated.

Application Component
• Name (write access required)
• Investment strategy (requires the default enumeration values)
• Lifecycle state
• Constraint fulfillment score (write access required)
• Principle fulfillment score (write access required)

Principle or Constraint (at least one)
• Name (write access required)
• Description
• Fulfillment score (write access required)

Association
• Name

note

For outgoing Association relations from Principles or Constraints, the target class Application Component must not be restricted.

Workspace "Application Investment Planning"
• The Application Investment Planning template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Write access to at least one of the Application Component or Application Service metamodel elements.
• Read access to the Responsible business actors, Accountable business actors, Consulted business actors, and Informed business actors relationships.
• For the properties listed below, read access is required unless write access is explicitly stated.

Application Component or Application Service (at least one)
• Name (write access required)
• Business fitness (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Business fitness score (write access required)
• Technology fitness (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Technology fitness score (write access required)
• Investment strategy (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Lifecycle state
• State (requires the default enumeration values)

Responsible business actors
• Name

Accountable business actors
• Name

Consulted business actors
• Name

Informed business actors
• Name

note

For outgoing RACI relations from Application Components or Application Services, the target classes Business Actor and User must not be restricted.

Workspace "Capability Investment Planning"
• The Capability Investment Planning template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Write access to at least one of the Capability or Business Function metamodel elements.
• For the properties listed below, read access is required unless write access is explicitly stated.

Capability or Business Function (at least one)
• Name (write access required)
• Level (Capabilities only)
• Strategic importance (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Strategic importance score (write access required)
• Maturity (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Maturity score (write access required)
• Investment strategy (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• State (requires the default enumeration values)

Workspace "Application-based Roadmap"
• The Application-based Roadmap template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Read access to the Requirement metamodel element and to at least one of the Application Component, Application Service, Application Function, or Application Interface metamodel elements.
• Read access to the Association relationship.
• For the properties listed below, read access is required unless write access is explicitly stated.

Requirement
• Name (write access required)
• Description
• Valid until (write access required)
• Status (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Estimated cost

Application Component, Application Service, Application Function or Application Interface (at least one)
• Name (write access required)
• Investment strategy (except Application Functions) (requires the default enumeration values)
• Lifecycle state (except Application Functions)

Association
• Name

note

For outgoing Association relations from Requirements, the target classes Application Component, Application Service, Application Function and/or Application Interface must not be restricted.

Workspace "Capability-Based Roadmap"
• The Capability-Based Roadmap template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Read access to the Requirement metamodel element and to at least one of the Capability, Course of Action, Business Actor, or Business Function metamodel elements.
• Read access to the Association relationship.
• For the properties listed below, read access is required unless write access is explicitly stated.

Requirement
• Name (write access required)
• Description
• Valid until (write access required)
• Status (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Estimated cost

Capability, Course of Action, Business Actor or Business Function (at least one)
• Name (write access required)
• Level (Capabilities only)

Association
• Name

note

For outgoing Association relations from Requirements, the target classes Capability, Course of Action, Business Actor and/or Business Function must not be restricted.

Workspace "Goal-Based Roadmap"
• The Goal-Based Roadmap template is only available to users who have the following access rights:
• Read access to the Requirement metamodel element and to at least one of the Goal, Outcome, or Driver metamodel elements.

Requirement
• Name (write access required)
• Description
• Valid until (write access required)
• Status (requires the default enumeration values) (write access required)
• Estimated cost

Goal, Outcome or Driver (at least one)

Association
