children.title: Audit Log Files
children.summary: Describes ADOIT's automatic audit logging of administrative actions like user management and data import/export, with logs written immediately in primary language and sensitive data encrypted by default; also notes availability of a manual audit log export feature.
children.content:
ADOIT automatically tracks administrative actions, such as
• creating and deleting users,
• changing access rights and
• importing and exporting repository data.

note

For a complete list of logged actions, please refer to the chapter Audit Log - Logged Actions.

Audit entries are written to *_audit.log files in the configured log directory of the application server container, as well as to the standard container streams. This functionality is always active and cannot be disabled.

How Audit Data Is Written

The following rules apply to audit data logging:
• Actions are logged immediately upon execution, not after database commit. This ensures that attempted actions are recorded, along with their commit status (successful or aborted).
• Strings in log entries are written in the primary language of the application library. If the primary language is not available, fallback rules apply. If no library is available yet (for example during database creation), strings are written in English.
• By default, sensitive data (such as user names and user properties) is encrypted in the audit logs.

info

In addition to the audit log files described here, ADOIT also provides an audit log that can be enabled manually in the ADOIT Administration and exported as CSV. For details, see Audit Log.

children.title: Log File Location and Naming
children.summary: Specifies audit log files are stored in the /logs folder with a naming convention including date, time, and process ID, and are included in the support information package (SIP).
children.content:
Audit log files are placed in the same /logs folder as other application server log files. The naming convention is:

<DATE>_<TIME>_<PROCESS_ID>_audit.log

Example

2025.09.16_11.53.57_86752_audit.log

Audit log files are also included automatically in the support information package (SIP).

children.title: Deanonymise Audit Data
children.summary: Explains how to disable encryption of sensitive audit log data by editing the server.conf file to uncomment a specific parameter, with caution about security and compliance risks such as GDPR violations.
children.content:
If required, sensitive data can be written in plain text instead of being encrypted. To enable this, you need to modify a configuration file:
1. Navigate to the directory <ADOIT application server>/conf.
2. Open the file server.conf in a text editor with administrative privileges.
3. Find the parameter ADOXX_SECURITY_DISABLE_AUDIT_LOG_SENSITIVE_DATA_ENCRYPTION.
4. Remove the leading # to uncomment the line.
5. Save the changes and restart the ADOIT application server to apply the modifications.

caution

Use with caution. Enabling this option will store sensitive personal data in plain text within audit logs. This may violate internal security policies or external compliance obligations, including GDPR. Ensure that appropriate safeguards, access controls, and retention policies are in place.

children.title: Audit Log - Logged Actions
children.summary: Lists categories of actions recorded in audit logs including user, system role, group, rights, import, metamodel, repository, and library management activities, detailing specific operations logged.
children.content:
The following list outlines the categories of actions recorded in the audit log (can be enabled manually in the ADOIT Administration and exported as CSV) and in the audit log files (always active, automatically saved to the /logs folder within the application server installation directory):

Users
• create/delete user
• change user attributes
• change user group assignment
• share/unshare user
• change repository assignment
• change component assignment

System Roles
• create/delete system role
• change system role properties
• user assignment to/removal from system role
• group assignment to/removal from system role

Groups
• create/delete user group
• rename group
• change user group hierarchy
• move user group

Rights
• change user access rights
• change access rights of groups
• change meta model rights
• change release workflow rights

Import
• repository
• migration package
• models/objects
• excel import
• translation
• users
• system users
• rights
• system roles
• component settings

Metamodel
• metamodel modifications

Repository
• create/delete repository
• rename repository

Library
• create/delete library
• update library
• rename library

children.title: Emergency Mode
children.summary: Describes ADOIT's emergency mode triggered by issues like database connection failures, library misconfiguration, JS syntax errors, or invalid licenses, restricting user access except for the default admin and providing troubleshooting steps including support information package download.
children.content:
If normal operation is not possible, ADOIT will enter emergency mode. Until the problem is resolved, users will see an error message when attempting to log in to ADOIT.

There can be various reasons for ADOIT to enter emergency mode:
• No connection to the specified ADOIT database could be established.
• The log entry Application has started in emergency mode because it could not establish a connection to the database! is written to the ADOIT21.0.log file in the configured log directory of the web server container, as well as to the standard container streams.
• Check whether the environment variables ADOXX_SERVER_DBNAME and ADOXX_SERVER_DBTYPE have been configured correctly in the deployment configuration of the application server container.
• Contact your database administrator if the problem persists.
• The library that should be used was not specified correctly (most often the case if there are multiple application libraries in the ADOIT database).
• The log entry Application has started in emergency mode because of a library misconfiguration! is written to the ADOIT21.0.log file in the configured log directory of the web server container, as well as to the standard container streams.
• Check whether the environment variable ADOXX_SERVER_LIBNAME has been configured correctly in the deployment configuration of the application server container.
• There are syntax errors in the application code which cause validation on the web server to fail.
• The log entry Application has started in emergency mode because of JS syntax in a MFB! is written to the ADOIT21.0.log file in the configured log directory of the web server container, as well as to the standard container streams.
• Contact our support team to help you solve this issue.
• No valid licence is available.
• One of the following log entries will be written to the ADOIT21.0.log file in the configured log directory of the web server container, as well as to the standard container streams: Application has started in emergency mode because of an invalid licence! or Application has started in emergency mode because the database contains data in a language not present in the selected licence!.
• A login to the ADOIT Administration will be possible, and the Import Licence dialogue will open automatically.

note

Only the default super admin "Admin" can log in to the ADOIT Administration in emergency mode if no valid licence is available.

For troubleshooting purposes, you can still download the support information package (SIP) containing all relevant log files when ADOIT is in emergency mode. For on-premise deployments, you must ensure that the container log directories are mapped to persistent storage for this data to be available. Be aware that the SIP will only include the log files of the web server if no connection to the application server could be established. To download the SIP:
• Enter the URL where ADOIT is available and add /supportinformation, e.g. https://pp2****.de.boc-cloud.com/supportinformation.

note

If you cannot fix the issue on your own, feel free to contact our support team.

children.title: Administrator
children.summary: Defines an Administrator as a person managing ADOIT with special rights such as creating user accounts and assigning access rights.
children.content: A person that administrates ADOIT. They are equipped with special rights, e.g. may create user accounts for users and assign access rights to them.

children.title: ADOIT Administration
children.summary: Defines ADOIT Administration as the software package reserved for administrators to manage ADOIT.
children.content: Software package for the administration of ADOIT, reserved exclusively for administrators.

children.title: Application Library
children.summary: Defines Application Library as the configuration containing model types, objects, connectors, and predefined queries, created by the customiser during setup.
children.content: Contains the definition of the model types, objects and connectors, predefined analysis queries and much more. The Application Library is created by the customiser during ADOIT configuration.

children.title: Attribute
children.summary: Defines Attribute as a property of a model type or class, with various types defined by the customiser in the Application Library.
children.content: Property of a model type or a class. Attributes may be of various attribute types and are defined by a customiser during the Application Library definition.

children.title: Attribute Type
children.summary: Defines Attribute Type as the data structure of an attribute, supporting diverse content like text, numbers, dates, and tables.
children.content: The data structure of the attribute. Depending on the attribute type, totally different content may be stored in the attribute: text of various length, integer and floating-point numbers, dates, times, tables, and much more.

children.title: Cardinality
children.summary: Defines Cardinality as rules specifying how many endpoints of a certain type a relation class may have.
children.content: Rules for endpoints. Cardinality rules define how many endpoints of a certain type a relation class may have.

children.title: Class
children.summary: Defines Class as an abstract template element in the Application Library from which objects or relations are instantiated, with examples and attributes defined by the customiser.
children.content: An (abstract) template element defined in the ADOIT Application Library, from which (real) objects or relations are created as instances an placed in models. For instance, “Department 5” and “Accounting” are instances of the object class Business Actor and “Write Letter” as well as “Update Virus Protection” instances of the object class Business Process. The same applies to relation classes. The classes are defined by the customiser during the definition of the Application Library. Classes have attributes.

children.title: Component
children.summary: Defines Component as part of ADOIT Administration containing modules needed for specific tool usage types.
children.content: Part of the ADOIT Administration. Every component contains the modules needed for a certain type of tool usage.

children.title: Connector
children.summary: Defines Connector as an instance of a relation class connecting objects, showing relations allowed by model type definitions.
children.content: Connection between objects. Instance of a relation class. Shows the relation between (two, sometimes more) objects. Depending on the model type definition and the objects concerned, different types of connectors are allowed.

children.title: Customiser
children.summary: Defines Customiser as a person with full access to ADOIT configuration, responsible for defining Application Libraries and component access.
children.content: Person with full access to the ADOIT configuration. A customiser e.g. defines a new Application Library or the overall component access of an existing product.

children.title: Endpoint
children.summary: Defines Endpoint as the attachment points of relation classes to object classes, governed by cardinality rules.
children.content: Endpoints define to which object classes a relation class may attach to. Endpoints are subject to cardinality rules.

children.title: Model
children.summary: Defines Model as a group of objects and connectors representing flows, structures, or information pools, instantiated from model types defined in the Application Library.
children.content: A group of objects, possibly connected by connectors and other relations. Models can picture flows (e.g. a process), structures (e.g. an organisational unit), an information pool (e.g. a document library) and much more. Every Application Library contains different model types, defined by a customiser. Every model is an instance of one of these model types.

children.title: Model Group
children.summary: Defines Model Group as a hierarchical directory structure organizing models in the repository.
children.content: Directory for models in the repository. The model group structure is organised hierarchically.

children.title: Model Type
children.summary: Defines Model Type as part of the Application Library aggregating objects and connectors to illustrate specific company aspects, with models being instances of these types.
children.content: Part of the ADOIT Application Library. Every model is an instance of a certain model type. A model type contains an aggregation of objects and connectors, serving for illustrating certain company aspects.

children.title: Properties
children.summary: Defines Properties as the graphical interface displaying and organizing attributes and relations of models, objects, and connectors into editable chapters.
children.content: Graphical display form for the attributes and relations of models, objects, and connectors. The attributes are organised in chapters in the properties and can be edited there.

children.title: Object
children.summary: Defines Object as an instance of an object class, distinguishing between reusable repository objects and modelling objects maintained only within models.
children.content: Instance of an (object) class. A distinction is drawn between repository objects (re-usable objects, stored in a repository) and modelling objects (maintained only in the models in which they are created).

children.title: Object Class
children.summary: Defines Object Class as the modelling object types like Business Actors or Processes, synonymous with Class.
children.content: Object classes define the modelling object types (e.g. Business Actors, Business Processes, etc.). See Class.

children.title: Object Group
children.summary: Defines Object Group as a hierarchical directory structure organizing objects in the repository.
children.content: Directory for objects in the repository. The object group structure is organised hierarchically.

children.title: Relation Class
children.summary: Defines Relation Class as classes defining connectors used in modelling or non-graphical relations, synonymous with Class.
children.content: Relation classes define connectors used in modelling or relations without graphical representation. See Class.

children.title: Rights
children.summary: Defines Rights as access permissions assigned to administrators and users covering components, user accounts, models, objects, and internal structures.
children.content: Every ADOIT administrator and every user account has access rights within the application. These cover various aspects (access to components, other user accounts, models and objects, the possibility to change internal structures and more).

children.title: Repository
children.summary: Defines Repository as a specialized database storage enabling versioning, multilingual models, reusable objects, and local/global information management.
children.content: A special kind of information storage in databases. In ADOIT this means for instance that models may exist in any number of versions and languages, that objects can be re-used in multiple models, that objects can contain both local (model-specific) and global (general) information and more.

children.title: User
children.summary: Defines User as a person working with ADOIT who logs in with a user account.
children.content: A person that works with ADOIT. For this, they have to log in with a user account.

children.title: User Account
children.summary: Defines User Account as the virtual representation of a user in ADOIT with credentials and assigned rights, enabling login.
children.content: Each user is assigned one (or more) user account(s) by an administrator to log in to ADOIT. Thus, a user account is the virtual counterpart of the user in the ADOIT database and has features like user name, password, and rights.

children.title: How Metamodel Conflicts Are Resolved During Library Updates
children.summary: Explains how ADOIT resolves metamodel conflicts during library updates by merging custom and product changes with specific rules for attributes, chapters, groups, relations, enumerations, and mandatory settings.
children.content:
In this chapter, you will learn how ADOIT handles metamodel conflicts when updating a library that contains custom local changes.

When you update your library and the current library contains custom metamodel changes (applied on the Properties page), ADOIT merges these changes with the new version of the library. The table below outlines how conflicts are resolved:
Custom change | Product change | Resolution
Add a new attribute and assign to a chapter | Delete group | The group is retained
| Delete chapter | The chapter is retained
| Delete preceding element | The new attribute is added at the last position in the container
| Delete class | The class is deleted, and the attribute is unassigned
Rename attribute | Rename attribute | Custom name is retained
| Delete attribute | The attribute is retained
Change attribute infotext | Change attribute infotext | Custom infotext is retained
Change attribute position | Change attribute position | Custom position is retained
| Delete preceding element | The attribute is moved to the last position in the container
| Change position of preceding attribute | Custom attribute is moved after the newly positioned attribute
Rename chapter | Rename chapter | Custom chapter name is retained
| Delete chapter | The chapter is deleted
Change chapter position | Delete chapter | The chapter is deleted
| Delete preceding chapter | The chapter is moved to the last position
| Change position of preceding chapter | Custom chapter is moved after the newly positioned chapter
Change group position | Delete preceding element | Group is moved to the last position in the chapter
| Change position of preceding element | Custom group position is retained
Rename group | Rename group | Custom group name is retained
| Delete group | The group is deleted
Change relation name | Change relation name | Custom relation name is retained
Change relation position | Change relation position | Custom relation position is retained
| Delete preceding element | The relation is moved to the last position in the container
| Change position of preceding element | Custom relation is moved after the newly positioned relation
Add enumeration value | Add enumeration value | Values are merged, with the custom value placed before the product value
| Remove enumeration value | The product change is retained
| Rename enumeration value | Changes are merged; both custom and renamed product values are retained
Rename enumeration value | Rename enumeration value | Custom name is retained
Change enumeration order | Keep or change enumeration order | Custom order is retained
Change "Mandatory" setting | Change "Mandatory" setting | Custom value (Y/N) is retained

children.title: Configuration Changes That Require a Server Restart
children.summary: Lists configuration changes in ADOIT that require application server or web server restarts, including settings for active features, email, integration, licensing, modules, and more.
children.content:
Most configuration settings in ADOIT take effect immediately after saving. However, some settings require a restart of the ADOIT application server or the Apache Tomcat web server. These are listed below.
Setting | Additional Information | Application Server Restart | Web Server Restart
Active features | Settings impacting the fundamental behaviour of ADOIT | Yes | –
Application server: change configuration files | server.conf, adoxx.conf, adoxx_web_conf.js, afts_server.conf, etc. | Yes | –
Change history | Settings for tracking changes to repository objects | Yes | –
Corporate identity | Add and configure CI schemes | Yes | –
Document management: basic settings | Settings for uploading documents | Yes | –
Email | Configure email service | – | Yes
Full-text search | Configure the general search function and the search in Explorer | Yes | –
iFrame embedding ADOIT | Allows you to embed ADOIT in a website | – | Yes
Integration ADONIS: configure interface | Setting up synchronisation of objects between ADOIT and ADONIS | Yes | Yes
Licence management | Adding a new ADOIT licence | Yes | –
Media management | Settings for uploading images | Yes | –
Model comparison | Defining the properties to consider when comparing models | Yes | –
Modelling | Settings for automatic saving and more | Yes | –
Modules | Assigning modules to system roles for access to features in ADOIT | Yes | –
Object mouseovers | Defining the properties to display in object tooltips in ADOIT | Yes | –
Object owners | Settings for assigning users ownership of repository objects | Yes | –
System | Technical settings controlling the base functionality of ADOIT | Yes | –
Tomcat: change configuration files | adoxx_web.properties, logback.xml, web.xml, server.xml, etc. | – | Yes
Tomcat: configure SSL/TLS support | Encrypt the communication between client and web server | – | Yes
Upgrade ADOIT | Migration from an earlier version to ADOIT 21.0 | Yes | Yes

documents.title: Quick Start Guide
documents.summary: Introduces ADOIT Quick Start Guides tailored for new customers, admins, and testers with standard or premium accounts to facilitate initial setup and exploration.
documents.content:
To make getting started and the initial setup as easy as possible, we've created the ADOIT Quick Start Guides. These will walk you through the most important first steps so you can start working in ADOIT with your colleagues right away!

Select what applies to you in order to receive the relevant information:
• ADOIT Quick Start Guide

For new customers and admins who want to get ADOIT up and running quickly with the essential configurations in place.
• Quick Start Guide for Standard Test Accounts

For testers who want to explore ADOIT and understand its features quickly. Please check your email with your credentials to see whether you have a Premium or Standard test account.
• Quick Start Guide for Premium Test Accounts

For testers who want to explore ADOIT and understand its features quickly. Please check your email with your credentials to see whether you have a Premium or Standard test account.

children.title: Welcome to ADOIT!
children.summary: Welcomes users to ADOIT and provides a Quick Start Guide selection based on user role (Administrator or User) to assist with initial setup and usage.
children.content:
Thank you for choosing ADOIT! To make getting started and the initial setup as easy as possible, we've created this short Quick Start Guide. It will walk you through the most important first steps so you can start working in ADOIT with your colleagues right away!

Note: Before you begin, an administrator must complete the basic settings. Only then can everyone continue with the user guide.

Select what applies to you in order to receive the relevant information.
• I am an Administrator

The most important information for administrators, including setup, permissions, and basic configuration.
• I am a User

Essential information for users, Enterprise Architects, and anyone with read-access.

children.title: Welcome to ADOIT!
children.summary: Provides an admin-focused Quick Start Guide overview encouraging flexible step prioritization for initial ADOIT configuration and setup.
children.content:
Thank you for choosing ADOIT! The admin section of this Quick Start Guide helps you quickly explore the most important settings. It walks you through the initial steps so you can get started with your colleagues in ADOIT right away!

note

You don’t need to follow the steps in the exact order described here. Simply review them - you might decide to prioritize or skip certain steps.

children.title: The first E-mail & Login
children.summary: Guides users through first login steps including accessing account via emailed credentials, logging into administration, and changing the initial password.
children.content:
You’ve received an email with an access credentials sheet. This sheet contains your login details as well as a link to your account. The email also includes your BOC contact person, who is available to support you every step of the way - whether it’s about steps in this Quick Start Guide or any future questions you may have!
1. Click on the link in the credentials sheet to access your account.
2. Click the gear icon in the top right corner next to your username to log into the administration area.
3. Use the login credentials provided in the credentials sheet.
4. Change your password the first time you log in - and be sure to remember it!

children.title: Get to know the ADOIT administration and settings
children.summary: Summarizes key ADOIT administration settings for user, permission, role, repository, property, and system management, supplemented by videos and resources.
children.content:
To help you quickly find your way around the ADOIT administration and set up a configuration that fits your team’s needs, we’ve compiled the most important information for you. Further down, you’ll find a list of videos and links to helpful resources.

Important Settings:
• Users: Management of users and user groups
• Permissions: Assignment and management of permissions
• System Roles: Management of system roles
• Repositories: Management of repositories, import/export of migration packages and models
• Properties: Customization of fields for ArchiMate elements
• Settings: Various options, mostly preset

children.title: Helpful Videos to Get Started
children.summary: Provides a selected tutorial video overviewing key administration components and links to a playlist with more ADOIT functions and tips.
children.content:
To make getting started easier for you, we’ve selected a video from our tutorial series that walks you through some helpful first steps in the administration:

Get an overview of the key components of administration.

Our playlist offers more exciting videos – featuring the key functions and clever tips for ADOIT!

children.title: Our Admin-Help
children.summary: Offers detailed written descriptions of all administrative settings in the Admin-Help for users who prefer reading over videos.
children.content: Prefer reading over watching? In our Admin-Help, you’ll find all the settings described in detail.

children.title: Initial Administrative Tasks
children.summary: Guides importing the Quick Start Migration Package to pre-configure folder structures, user groups, and permissions for initial ADOIT setup.
children.content:
Just a few more steps and you’re ready to go! To get started, you’ll need to define an initial folder structure, create a few user groups, and assign permissions. No worries – we’ve already prepared everything for you in what we call the Quick Start Migration Package. All you need to do is import a file, and the most important settings will be pre-configured.

You can download the Quick Start Migration Package here.

To import the Quick Start Migration Package:
1. In the Administration section, go to Repositories.
2. Click on “More Options” in the top right corner → “Import Migration Package”.
3. Upload the downloaded Quick Start Migration Package – either by drag & drop or using the file selector.
4. Import the migration package directly into the active standard repository.

You can find more information in our online help. There, you can also get familiar with our terminology around repositories and migration packages. Check out the following articles in the online help: What are repositories?, What is a migration package?.

note

You’ve successfully setup:
1. A folder structure for objects
2. A folder structure for models
3. Initial user groups
4. First permission settings

Of course, you can adjust structures, permissions, etc. later on - we’ll take care of that further down in the guide. You’ll also find a dummy user called “arch” in your user groups. This account is needed for a few example models you’ll import later - feel free to ignore it for now.

children.title: Create a super-user for yourself
children.summary: Explains how to create a super-user account aligned with company policies, including assigning administrator roles and repository access.
children.content:
The user account you’ve been using so far probably doesn’t align with your company’s guidelines. We’ll cover how to set up Single Sign-On (SSO) and SAML later - but for now, let’s get you ready by creating a user account that meets your organization’s policies.

note

Ideally, use your company’s standard format for usernames, such as your Windows login or email address. This will make integrating with your Directory Service much easier. If you're unsure, it’s best to check with your IT Service Desk.

Here’s how to proceed:
1. Log in to the Administration
2. Go to Users
3. Create a new user• Under “General”: define the username, password, email address, etc.
• Under “Groups and Roles”: assign the user to the “Administrator” group
• Under “Repository”: select the “Standard Repository”
• Under ”Named user”: select scenarios if you want to login with the super-user in ADOIT

You can find more detailed information on how to create new users and what each setting means here.

It’s also important to enter your email address under “General”, so you can reset your password in case you forget it.

If you’d like your BOC contact to have access to your ADOIT environment — to better assist you with any questions or issues — we’ve already created a user account for them. You just need to activate it in the Administration panel. You’ll find more about editing users in our online help.

children.title: Great, the first steps are done! Now let's move on to your colleagues
children.summary: Describes predefined user groups (Reader, User, Administrator) and their permissions to prepare for creating user accounts for colleagues.
children.content:
To make sure your colleagues also have access to ADOIT, we’ll now create user accounts for them. Before doing so, let’s take a quick look at the existing user groups. You can find them in the administration under “Users”. User groups allow you to manage your users’ permissions. The following groups have already been prepared for you during the installation:
• Reader: Users assigned to this group have read-only access.
• User: Users assigned to this group have full write access.
• Administrator: Users in this group have full write access, as well as access to the administration features.

The "Standard Group" and "ppXXXXXX" groups are not needed for now.

children.title: Create users for the members of your core team
children.summary: Recommends manually creating initial users via an Excel import template with required email addresses and assigning them to the User group.
children.content:
Normally you will manage your ADOIT accounts via SAML. This usually takes a little longer, as some clarifications have to be made.

We therefore recommend that you create your first users manually. So that you don't have to do this individually, we have prepared an Excel template that you can download and enter all your users. Then all you have to do is import them and the user accounts for your colleagues are created in ADOIT!
1. Go to the administration section → "Users" → "More options" → "Import users from Excel."
2. Download the template "UserImport.xlsx."
3. Enter all the users' details. IMPORTANT: An email address must be provided for each user. This is required to reset the password later!

Enter all users who are to work with ADOIT in the start phase. All other users will be created automatically via SAML in the future. You typically give the core team members write permissions. You can of course restrict this later.

Now you have to upload the file with the registered users again. Use the following import options:
1. Select the “Trusted login” checkbox. (You can read why and why this is important here)
2. For user groups: User (this gives your core team write access to models and objects)
3. Under “Repositories and object groups”: Standard repository and objects
4. Then click on “Upload file”

children.title: Assign scenarios to your users
children.summary: Details assigning named-use scenario licenses (Design & Document, Read & Explore, Workspaces) to users via the administration panel.
children.content:
There are named-use scenario licenses in ADOIT. Named-use scenario licenses define the users who can use a scenario. Scenarios are the main components of ADOIT. There are:
• Design & Document
• Read & Explore
• Workspaces

This is how you assign scenarios to users:
1. Go to Administration > Users > Select a user > Edit (⋮) > Named-Use user
2. Select the desired scenario in the “Select scenarios” field
3. Click on “Select”

note

The users are now configured. Now distribute the ADOIT URL to your users by email and inform them of their user name. The users can reset their password via “Forgot password”.

children.title: Import examples for your colleagues
children.summary: Provides instructions to import 5 industry-specific example models as independent repositories and assign access rights to colleagues.
children.content:
We have prepared 5 industry-specific example models for getting started in ADOIT. These consist of:
• 3 models
• 1 analysis model
• 1 workspace

Simply import the file, and your colleagues can explore the models at their own pace.

Download the desired example model directly:
• Model of an Airport
• Model of a Bank
• Model of an Insurance
• Model of a Retailer
• Model of a Toymanufacturer

Structure of the example models:
• Capability Map
• Operating Model
• Application Landscape
• An analysis with a portfolio view of the application components

Additionally, you will find a pre-configured workspace in the Workspaces scenario.

Importing the example models:
• Download one of the example models above.
• Go to Repositories in the administration and click on More Options in the top right corner. Then click Import Repository.
• It is important to import it as an INDEPENDENT Repository (select the first option in the import settings).
• After importing the example model, you will need to assign access rights to yourself or the responsible colleagues who should see the example. You can do this under Users in the administration. Select your user and those of your colleagues who should be able to see the example and click Edit. Under Repository, you now need to select the corresponding repository. For more information, please refer to our Online-Help.
• Log out of the administration and log into ADOIT to check if the import was successful. When logging in, select the new repository. You should now see the following in the explorer:

Great, your colleagues are now on board! Share the User Guide with them and inform them about their login credentials.

children.title: Further useful information for you as an Administrator
Import existing data via the Excel Interface
children.summary: Explains importing existing architecture data from Excel using downloadable templates accessible via the Object Explorer context menu.
children.content:
Do you already have architecture information in Excel format? Use our Excel templates to import the data:

You can find our template directly in the Object Explorer:
1. Select the folder where you want to import the data.
2. Open the context menu (the three dots in the top right corner of the Explorer).
3. Choose "Import/Export" → "Import objects from Excel...".
4. Download the template using the download icon.
5. Fill in the template with your architecture information and upload it again.

For more information, please refer to our Online-Help!

note

Of course, you can also customize the template to fit your needs. You can find more information about this here.

children.title: Reduce modeling complexity with metamodel profiles
children.summary: Introduces metamodel profiles as filters to reduce ArchiMate modeling complexity, recommending the 'ADOIT for Fans of Lean Architecture' profile.
children.content:
In ArchiMate, there are many elements and relationships. Initially, your team will only use a few of them. Therefore, we offer so-called metamodel profiles. These act as a filter for elements and relationships. All our predefined views, analyses, examples, and templates are based on this filter.

note

Switch the metamodel profile via Setup in the toolbar. Please note that the selected profile will also be activated for your colleagues. More information about metamodel profiles can be found here.

In most cases, the profile "ADOIT for Fans of Lean Architecture" is used. In this profile, we have reduced the possible relationships between two classes to just one relationship. We recommend using this profile as a starting point. You can expand or further restrict it later based on your specific use case. More information, can be found here.

children.title: Activate ADOIT Forms
children.summary: Describes activating ADOIT Forms, a SaaS-based user-friendly form interface for data entry, via administration settings with automatic OAuth, REST, and CORS configuration.
children.content:
With ADOIT Forms, you can simplify data maintenance. It is a user-friendly, form-based interface that allows for easy data entry and updates – even for users who are less familiar with ADOIT or enterprise architecture.

There are 3 use cases in ADOIT Forms:
• Create forms
• Distribute forms
• Fill out forms

For more information about ADOIT Forms, please refer to our Online-Help.

How to activate ADOIT Forms:
1. ADOIT Forms runs in SaaS mode, so no additional installation is required.
2. To activate Forms, log in to the administration.
3. Navigate to “Settings” and click on “ADOIT Forms” in the list on the left.
4. You can now activate Forms with the click of a button. All necessary settings for OAuth, REST, and CORS will be automatically configured in the background.

note

You can find more information on installing ADOIT Forms here. To learn which rights or licenses your users need, you can read more here.

children.title: Prepare the SAML integration
children.summary: Lists prerequisites and required information from the customer's SAML Identity Provider to prepare for Single Sign-On integration with BOC SaaS.
children.content:
To set up Single-Sign-On (SSO) on your BOC SaaS account (SP) and your SAML Identity Provider (IdP), some preliminary work is required. Please prepare the following and send us the details up to 24 hours before the first scheduled customer meeting.

We need the following from your SSO technical team:
• The following claims should be configured in your SAML Identity Provider (IdP):
• Username = E-mail address
• First name
• Last name
• E-mail address
• Groups
• After configuring the Identity Provider (IdP), you need to think about the AD groups to be configured: In ADOIT we have the following user groups by default:
• Administrators
• Readers
• Users

Please talk to your administrator about possible AD groups. You will probably add a few more in the course of further configuration. For more information, please ask your BOC contact person.
• We also require the necessary information from the customer IdP:
• IdPURL
• Token signing certificate
• The “metadata.xml” file or the metadata URL
• The names of the configured claim attributes
• If your IdP endpoint is not accessible via the internet, we need someone on your side to test it. Please provide us with the contact information of a possible test assistant.
• Once you have collected all the important information, we would ask you to contact your BOC contact person. They will provide you with a secure file exchange service through which you can upload all the necessary files and information. For this we also need a telephone number from your side. Please also provide this to your BOC contact person.

Once we have received the required data, we configure SAML. First, it is set up as a secondary authentication method to avoid any impact on the productive use of your instance. After successful testing during the session, SAML will be enabled as the default authentication method. If you have any further questions on this topic, you can always contact your BOC contact person!

children.title: The most important steps are done!
children.summary: Congratulates on completing initial steps and suggests exploring integrations, extensions, e-learning, blogs, and FAQs with BOC contact support.
children.content:
Great job! You've successfully completed the first steps in ADOIT! Now you and your colleagues can continue exploring the software at your own pace. The next steps can now be discussed with your BOC contact person. Here is a small list of useful features and settings that we would recommend at the beginning:
• Already using ADONIS? Discover the possibilities of integration with ADO Connect:• ADO Connect in our Marketplace
• More Infos about ADO Connect
• Explore all extensions for ADOIT in our EA Marketplace:• EA Marketplace
• Free e-learning courses for you and your colleagues
• For more insights, know-how, and useful tips, check out our blogs or EA resources:• ADOIT EA Blogs
• EA Resources
• Got more questions? Browse our FAQ section for many interesting topics:• Help-Center
• Submit a request

note

For any further questions or concerns, please reach out to your BOC contact person!

children.title: Welcome to ADOIT!
children.summary: Welcomes users to ADOIT and encourages flexible prioritization of Quick Start Guide steps for initial exploration with colleagues.
children.content:
Thank you for choosing ADOIT! The user section of this Quick Start Guide helps you quickly explore the most important features. It walks you through the initial steps so you can get started with your colleagues in ADOIT right away!

note

You don’t need to follow the steps in the exact order described here. Simply review them - you might decide to prioritize or skip certain steps.

children.title: Login
children.summary: Instructs users to contact their administrator for login credentials and use the 'Reset Password' function if no password is set.
children.content:
Please contact your administrator. He or she has created an account for you and knows your login details. Login & Password: You likely don’t have a password yet. Use the "Reset Password" function to create a new one. You will receive an email to reset your password.

If you did not receive an email, please contact your administrator and check if your email address has been correctly entered in your user account.

You're all set now! You can start exploring ADOIT.

children.title: Get to Know the ADOIT Interface and Features
children.summary: Introduces the ADOIT interface toolbar functions including Home, Scenarios, New, Find, Analyze, and Setup for user navigation.
children.content:
To help you get familiar with ADOIT quickly, we have compiled the most important information for you. Below, you will find a list of helpful videos and links to additional resources to make the most of your ADOIT experience.

In the top toolbar, you will find all key functions and settings:
• Home Button: Takes you back to the start page at any time.
• Scenarios: Switch between different use cases such as Design & Document, Read & Explore, or Workspaces. More details below…
• New: Create new objects and diagrams.
• Find: Search for objects and diagrams in your repository.
• Analyze: Perform analyses or access analyses, reports, and dashboards.
• Setup: Customize the metamodel profile here. (Only visible to users in the User group!)

children.title: ADOIT Scenarios
children.summary: Explains ADOIT's three scenarios—Read & Explore, Workspaces, and Design & Document—tailored to different stakeholder needs.
children.content:
ADOIT is divided into different scenarios, each tailored to the specific needs of different stakeholders:

Read & Explore: This scenario ensures that important information within the organization is easily accessible.

Workspaces: Collaboration is the focus here. Different teams work together on application assessments or the development of roadmaps.

Design & Document: In this scenario, models can be created, analyses performed, and the repository maintained.

For more information on each scenario and its features, please refer to our Online-Help!

children.title: Helpful Videos to Get Started
children.summary: Recommends three tutorial videos covering creating objects, performing analyses, and collaborating via workspaces to get started with ADOIT.
children.content:
To help you get started , we have selected three videos from our video tutorial series. These provide useful first steps for modeling, analyses, and working with workspaces:
1. Create Objects in ADOIT

Learn how to create objects, such as applications.
2. Perform Analyses

Learn how to create analyses based on the data in your repository and visualize the results.
3. Collaborate with your colleagues

Use workspaces to collaborate with your team on EA initiatives.

Our playlist offers more exciting videos – featuring the key functions and clever tips for ADOIT!

children.title: Our Online-Help
children.summary: Points users to the Online-Help for detailed written descriptions of all ADOIT functions as an alternative to videos.
children.content: If you prefer reading over watching videos, you can find all the information in our Online-Help. It provides detailed descriptions of all the functions.

children.title: Free E-Learning Course for you and your colleagues
children.summary: Offers a free 2-3 hour e-learning course on ArchiMate, modeling, and ADOIT basics for users and colleagues.
children.content:
If you want to learn more about ArchiMate, modeling, and using ADOIT, you can take our free e-learning course. In just 2-3 hours, you will get to know the key concepts, so you and your colleagues will be ready to get started with ArchiMate and ADOIT!

Take our free e-learning course now!

children.title: More examples for you and your colleagues
children.summary: Describes 5 industry-specific example models including capability maps, operating models, application landscapes, analyses, and workspaces for user exploration.
children.content:
We have prepared 5 industry-specific example models for getting started in ADOIT. These consist of:
• A Capability Map
• An Operating Model
• An Application Landscape

children.title: Reduce modeling complexity with metamodel profiles
children.summary: Reiterates metamodel profiles as filters for ArchiMate elements and relationships, recommending the 'ADOIT for Fans of Lean Architecture' profile as a starting point.
children.content:
In ArchiMate, there are many elements and relationships. Initially, your team will only use a few of them. Therefore, we offer so-called metamodel profiles. These act as a filter for elements and relationships. All our predefined views, analyses, examples, and templates are based on this filter.

note

In most cases, the profile "ADOIT for Fans of Lean Architecture" is used. In this profile, we have reduced the possible relationships between two classes to just one relationship. We recommend using this profile as a starting point. You can expand or further restrict it later based on your specific use case. More information, can be found here.

children.content:

• 3 models
• 1 analysis model
• 1 workspace

Simply import the file, and your colleagues can explore the models at their own pace.

Download the desired example model directly:
• Model of an Airport
• Model of a Bank
• Model of an Insurance
• Model of a Retailer
• Model of a Toymanufacturer

Structure of the example models:
• Capability Map
• Operating Model
• Application Landscape
• An analysis with a portfolio view of the application components

Additionally, you will find a pre-configured workspace in the Workspaces scenario.

Importing the example models:
• Download one of the example models above.
• Go to Repositories in the administration and click on More Options in the top right corner. Then click Import Repository.
• It is important to import it as an INDEPENDENT Repository (select the first option in the import settings).
• After importing the example model, you will need to assign access rights to yourself or the responsible colleagues who should see the example. You can do this under Users in the administration. Select your user and those of your colleagues who should be able to see the example and click Edit. Under Repository, you now need to select the corresponding repository. For more information, please refer to our Online-Help.
• Log out of the administration and log into ADOIT to check if the import was successful. When logging in, select the new repository. You should now see the following in the explorer:

children.title: Great, the first steps are done! Now, let’s move on with your colleagues
children.summary: Explains managing pre-created user accounts in test environments, adjusting user details, and differentiating Reader, User, and Administrator roles.
children.content:
Normally, ADOIT accounts are managed via SAML. However, in the test account, it works differently. To allow your colleagues to test ADOIT freely, we have already prepared user accounts for them. You can find these accounts in the Administration section under "Users" or on the credentials sheet. There are just a few details you need to adjust:
1. Go to Administration > Users > select a user > edit (⋮) > General
2. Name: Enter the names of your testers to stay organized.
3. Email: Make sure an email address is provided for each user. This is required for password resets!
4. Finally, distribute the login details from the credentials sheet to your testers and share the ADOIT URL with them via email.

Difference between User and Reader: In the test account, you will most likely use the User role to fully test ADOIT’s features. However, in general, we differentiate between:
• Reader: Users assigned to this group have read-only access.
• User: Users assigned to this group have full write access.
• Administrator: Users in this group have full write access and additional access to the administration.

children.title: Activate ADOIT Forms
